question: How does Bootstrap.verifiedJavaAgent() work?
answer:
Persists correlated availability resources to storage during shutdown.

This method sends a request to the availability correlation event bus address to write correlated resources to persistent storage. This ensures that availability correlation data is preserved across application restarts.

The method uses a 10-minute timeout (600000ms) to allow sufficient time for the write operation to complete, which may involve a large amount of data. It returns a Future that completes when the write operation is finished. @return A Future that completes when the correlated resources have been written / public static Future writeCorrelatedResources() { var promise = Promise.promise(); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().request(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AVAILABILITY_CORRELATION + ".write", null, new DeliveryOptions().setSendTimeout(600000L), reply -> promise.complete()); return promise.future(); } / Persists dependencies of a specific type to storage during shutdown.

This method sends a request to the dependency event bus address for the specified dependency type to write dependencies to persistent storage. This ensures that dependency data is preserved across application restarts.

The method uses a 10-minute timeout (600000ms) to allow sufficient time for the write operation to complete, which may involve a large amount of data. It returns a Future that completes when the write operation is finished. @param dependencyType The type of dependencies to persist (e.g., LOCAL_DOMAIN, NETWORK, etc.) @return A Future that completes when the dependencies have been written / public static Future writeDependencies(AIOpsConstants.DependencyType dependencyType) { var promise = Promise.promise(); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().request(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DEPENDENCY + "." + dependencyType.getName() + ".write", null, new DeliveryOptions().setSendTimeout(600000L), reply -> promise.complete()); return promise.future(); } / Checks if a Java agent is attached to the JVM.

This method examines the JVM runtime arguments to detect if any Java agent is attached using the -javaagent flag. This is a security measure to prevent potential interception of sensitive information like passwords or encryption keys by unauthorized agents.

If a Java agent is detected, the application may refuse to start as a security precaution, as agents can potentially modify application behavior or intercept sensitive data. @return true if a Java agent is attached, false otherwise

question: Show the pattern for: How does APIServer.forgotPasswordLimitExceeded() work?
answer:
Checks if a user has exceeded the forgot password request limit within the configured time window.

This method implements rate limiting for forgot password requests to prevent abuse and potential security attacks. It evaluates whether a user can make another forgot password request based on:

  • Number of previous attempts within the time window
  • Time elapsed since the last attempt
  • Configured maximum attempts and time window limits

Rate Limiting Logic:

  • If the time window has expired since the last attempt, the user can proceed
  • If within the time window and under the attempt limit, the user can proceed
  • If within the time window and at/over the attempt limit, the user is blocked

Security Benefits:

  • Prevents automated attacks on the password reset functionality
  • Reduces email spam from excessive reset requests
  • Protects against user enumeration attacks
@param user The user JsonObject containing forgot password attempt tracking data. Must include:
  • {@code USER_FORGOT_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS} - Number of previous attempts (defaults to 0)
  • {@code USER_LAST_FORGOT_PASSWORD_ATTEMPT_TIME} - Timestamp of last attempt (defaults to 0)
@return {@code true} if the user is within limits and can make another request, {@code false} if the user has exceeded the limit and should be blocked

answer: Returns the version number of this patch.             @return The version string "8.1.1"      /     @Override     public String getVersion()     {         return VERSION;     }      @Override     public Future<Void> doPatch()     {         var promise = Promise.<Void>promise();          try         {             LOGGER.info("executing 8.1.1 patch...");              var futures = new ArrayList<Future<Void>>();              futures.add(updateObjectNotificationContext());              futures.add(executeMetricGroupAttachPatch());              futures.add(executeColumnMapperPatch());              Future.join(futures).onComplete(result ->             {                 if (result.succeeded())                 {                     LOGGER.info("successfully executed 8.1.1 patch");                      promise.complete();                 }                 else                 {                     LOGGER.error(result.cause());                      promise.fail(result.cause());                 }             });         }         catch (Exception exception)         {             LOGGER.error(exception);              promise.fail(exception);         }          return promise.future();     }      /       Attaches "maridbindex" metrics to MariaDB Database objects       if not already present. Saves and updates the metrics asynchronously.             @return a Future completing when all patches are applied      /     private Future<Void> executeMetricGroupAttachPatch()     {          var promise = Promise.<Void>promise();          var futures = new ArrayList<Future>();          var items = ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItemsByType(NMSConstants.Type.MARIADB);          for (var item : items)         {              var metrics = MetricConfigStore.getStore().getItemsByObject((Long) item);              var doPatch = true;              for (var metric : metrics)             {                 if (metric.getString(Metric.METRIC_PLUGIN).equals("mariadbindex"))                 {                     doPatch = false;                 }             }              if (doPatch)             {                 var itemPromise = Promise.promise();                  futures.add(itemPromise.future());                  var mariadbIndexMetric = metrics.getFirst().mergeIn(ObjectManagerCacheStore.getStore().getItemByMetricPlugin("mariadbindex"));                  mariadbIndexMetric.remove(ID);                  Bootstrap.configDBService().save(DBConstants.TBL_METRIC, mariadbIndexMetric, DEFAULT_USER, SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS, result ->                 {                     if (result.succeeded())                     {                          MetricConfigStore.getStore().addItem(result.result()).onComplete(response ->                         {                             LOGGER.info("successfully attached plugin for monitor " + item);                          });                          itemPromise.complete();                     }                     else                     {                         LOGGER.error(result.cause());                          itemPromise.fail(result.cause());                      }                 });             }         }          CompositeFuture.all(futures).onComplete(result ->         {             if (result.succeeded())             {                 LOGGER.info("successfully attached plugin for all monitors");                  promise.complete();             }              else             {                 LOGGER.error(result.cause());                  promise.fail("Failed to attach plugin for all monitors with reason : " + result.cause().getMessage());              }         });          return promise.future();     }      // While bulk notification now we have different json structure which support rich notification like channel     // so we will change json structure here like the policy context     private Future<Void> updateObjectNotificationContext()     {         var promise = Promise.<Void>promise();          try         {             var items = ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItems();              for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++)             {                 var object = items.getJsonObject(index);                  if (object != null && object.containsKey(OBJECT_MONITOR_POLLING_FAILED_NOTIFICATION_STATUS) && object.getString(OBJECT_MONITOR_POLLING_FAILED_NOTIFICATION_STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(YES))                 {                     var notificationContext = new JsonObject().put(Notification.NotificationType.EMAIL.getName(),new JsonArray());                         }                     }                      object.put(OBJECT_NOTIFICATION,notificationContext);                      object.remove(OBJECT_EMAIL_NOTIFICATION_RECIPIENTS);                      object.remove(OBJECT_SMS_NOTIFICATION_RECIPIENTS);                 }             });         }         catch (Exception e)         {             LOGGER.error(e);              promise.fail(e);         }          return promise.future();      }       private Future<Void> executeColumnMapperPatch()     {         Promise<Void> promise = Promise.promise(); question: What does the Patch8020 class do?
answer:

This patch migrates IP/IP Range mappings into domain mappings. It processes IP groups from the FlowIPGroupConfigStore, handles various IP formats including individual IPs, IP ranges (e.g., 192.168.1.1-192.168.1.10), partial ranges (e.g., 172.16.10.1-55), and wildcard notations (using 'xx').

question: Show the pattern for: How does ServiceOpsIntegration.generateToken() work?

question: How does AgentCacheManager.processFiles() work?
answer:
The AgentCacheManager class is responsible for managing the cache files generated by agents.

This verticle handles the following operations:

  • Periodically checking and processing cached agent data files
  • Sending cached data to the Motadata server when connectivity is restored
  • Managing cache directory size by implementing cleanup strategies
  • Chunking large files for efficient processing

The cache manager ensures that agent data is not lost during network outages by storing it locally and forwarding it when connectivity is restored. It also implements size-based cleanup to prevent disk space issues. / public class AgentCacheManager extends AbstractVerticle { / The folder where agent cache files are stored / public static final File CACHE_FOLDER = new File(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "cache"); public static final String PENDING_CACHE_FILES = GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "agent-pending-files"; / The number of chunks to split cache files into for processing / public static final int CACHE_FILE_CHUNKS = AgentConfigUtil.getAgentCacheFileChunks(); / Maximum allowed size of the cache directory in bytes / public static final long CACHE_DIRECTORY_MAX_SIZE_BYTES = AgentConfigUtil.getAgentCacheDirectoryMaxSizeBytes(); / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(AgentCacheManager.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_AGENT, "Agent Cache Manager", true); / List of remote event senders (master devices) to which the agent can send events / private static final JsonArray HOSTS = CommonUtil.getRemoteEventSenders(); / The interval in seconds after which the agent should consider a master device as down if no heartbeat is received / private static final Long AGENT_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = AgentConfigUtil.getAgentHeartbeatTimeoutSeconds(); / Map to track cache files by agent, with file paths and timestamps / private final Map> cacheFiles = new HashMap<>(); // agent -> (absoluteFilePath -> timestamp) / Map to track pending files by master ip address, with absoluteFilePath / private final Map> pendingFiles = new HashMap<>(); / Map to track availability status of each master device based on port check result / private final Map activeServerByStatus = new HashMap<>(); / Initializes the AgentCacheManager and sets up a periodic timer to process cache files.

This method:

  • Sets up a periodic timer to check and process cache files
  • Checks connectivity to the Motadata server
  • Processes cache files when connectivity is available
  • Manages cache directory size by implementing cleanup strategies
  • Listens for remote session status updates to update host statuses

The method handles different scenarios:

  • When server is reachable: Processes files normally
  • When server is not reachable: Manages cache size to prevent disk space issues
@param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done @throws Exception If an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { // load pending files from disk if bootstrap type is AGENT & not for health agent if (MotadataConfigUtil.getSystemBootstrapType().equalsIgnoreCase(GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.AGENT.name())) { var file = new File(PENDING_CACHE_FILES); if (file.exists()) { try { var buffer = Bootstrap.vertx().fileSystem().readFileBlocking(file.getPath()); if (buffer != null && buffer.getBytes().length > 0) { var context = new JsonObject(Buffer.buffer(CodecUtil.toBytes(buffer.getBytes()))).getMap(); if (context.containsKey("pending.files")) { ((Map) (context.get("pending.files"))).forEach((key, value) -> { if (HOSTS.contains(key)) { pendingFiles.put(key, new HashSet<>((List) value)); } }); LOGGER.info("loaded agent pending files from disk..."); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } else { Bootstrap.vertx().fileSystem().createFileBlocking(file.getPath()); } vertx.setPeriodic(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(AgentConfigUtil.getAgentPendingFilesCacheDumpSeconds()), timer -> dump()); } for (var index = 0; index < HOSTS.size() ; index++) { pendingFiles.computeIfAbsent(HOSTS.getString(index), value -> new HashSet<>()); } vertx.setPeriodic(AgentConfigUtil.getAgentCacheFlushTimerSeconds(), timer -> { try { var files = CACHE_FOLDER.listFiles(); if (files != null && files.length > 0) { HOSTS.stream().forEach(host -> activeServerByStatus.put(host.toString(), RemoteSessionCacheStore.getStore().getStatus(host.toString(), AGENT_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS))); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("statuses of remote hosts: %s", JsonObject.mapFrom(activeServerByStatus).encode())); } if (activeServerByStatus.containsValue(STATUS_UP)) { populate(files); // preparing cacheFiles map for (var entry : cacheFiles.entrySet()) { var sortedFiles = new ArrayList<>(entry.getValue().entrySet()); // absolute filepath -> timestamp sortedFiles.sort(Map.Entry.comparingByValue()); if (FileUtils.sizeOfDirectory(CACHE_FOLDER) < CACHE_DIRECTORY_MAX_SIZE_BYTES) { processFiles(sortedFiles, entry.getKey(), false); } else { processFiles(sortedFiles, entry.getKey(), true); LOGGER.debug(String.format("Cache folder size crossed max threshold %s, Processing %s files at a time", CACHE_DIRECTORY_MAX_SIZE_BYTES, sortedFiles.size() / CACHE_FILE_CHUNKS)); } } } if ((activeServerByStatus.containsValue(STATUS_UNKNOWN) || activeServerByStatus.containsValue(STATUS_DOWN)) && FileUtils.sizeOfDirectory(CACHE_FOLDER) > AgentConfigUtil.getAgentCacheFileMaxSizeBytes()) { LOGGER.info(String.format("%s size is greater than %s bytes", CACHE_FOLDER.getAbsolutePath(), AgentConfigUtil.getAgentCacheFileMaxSizeBytes())); populate(files); // preparing cacheFiles map clear(); // clear cache files till } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } finally { cacheFiles.clear(); } }); promise.complete(); } / Processes cached files by reading and uncompressing their content, and deleting the file afterward. Supports optional chunking for partial processing. @param sortedFiles List of cache files with their timestamps @param agent Agent metadata to include in the event @param chunking Whether to process only a portion of the files

question: Show the pattern for: How does UserProfile.getAll() work?
answer:
Updates a user profile by assigning or unassigning users.

This method handles both assignment and unassignment operations by:

  • Updating the profile's user list in the database
  • Updating each affected user's profile assignment
  • Managing profile-to-user mappings in the configuration stores
@param routingContext the routing context for the request @param profileId the ID of the profile being updated @param entities the updated list of user IDs for the profile @param users the specific user IDs being assigned or unassigned @param assign true for assignment operation, false for unassignment @return a Future that completes when the update operation is finished / private Future updateItem(RoutingContext routingContext, long profileId, JsonArray entities, JsonArray users, boolean assign) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var username = routingContext.user().principal().getString(USER_NAME) != null ? routingContext.user().principal().getString(USER_NAME) : DEFAULT_USER; var remoteAddress = routingContext.request().remoteAddress().host() != null ? routingContext.request().remoteAddress().host() : SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS; Bootstrap.configDBService().update(DBConstants.TBL_USER_PROFILE, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, ID).put(VALUE, profileId), new JsonObject().put(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS, entities), username, remoteAddress, result -> UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().updateItem(profileId).onComplete(asyncResult -> { var futures = new ArrayList>(); var usersByProfile = new HashMap>(); for (var index = 0; index < users.size(); index++) { var future = Promise.promise(); try { futures.add(future.future()); var userId = users.getLong(index); var profile = assign ? profileId : DUMMY_ID; var oldProfileId = UserConfigStore.getStore().remove(userId); usersByProfile.computeIfAbsent(oldProfileId, value -> new ArrayList<>()).add(userId); Bootstrap.configDBService().update(DBConstants.TBL_USER, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, ID).put(VALUE, userId), new JsonObject().put(User.USER_PROFILE, profile), username, remoteAddress, userResult -> { try { UserConfigStore.getStore().updateItem(userId); if (assign) { UserConfigStore.getStore().updateProfile(userId, profileId); } future.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); future.fail(exception); } }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); future.fail(exception); } } Future.join(futures).onComplete(futureAsyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { updateProfile(usersByProfile).onComplete(profileAsyncResult -> { if (profileAsyncResult.succeeded()) { promise.complete(); } else { promise.fail(profileAsyncResult.cause()); } }); } else { promise.fail(asyncResult.cause()); } }); })); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Pre-processing hook for retrieving references to a user profile.

This method retrieves the users associated with a profile, applying access control based on the requesting user's permissions:

  • Admin users can see all users in the profile
  • Non-admin users can only see themselves if they're in the profile
@param routingContext the routing context for the request @param response the response object to populate with user references @return a Future containing the response with user references / @Override protected Future getReferencesPreHook(RoutingContext routingContext, JsonObject response) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var userIds = UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(CommonUtil.getLong(routingContext.request().getParam(ID))).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS); var items = new JsonArray(); if (routingContext.user().principal().getJsonArray(APIConstants.USER_PERMISSIONS).contains(USER_SETTINGS + ":" + READ_WRITE_PERMISSION)) { for (var index = 0; index < userIds.size(); index++) { items.add(UserConfigStore.getStore().getItem(userIds.getLong(index))); } } else if (userIds.contains(routingContext.user().attributes().getJsonObject("accessToken").getLong(ID))) { items.add(UserConfigStore.getStore().getItem(routingContext.user().attributes().getJsonObject("accessToken").getLong(ID))); } if (!items.isEmpty()) { response.put(Entity.USER.getName(), items); } promise.complete(response); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Pre-processing hook for retrieving entity counts for user profiles.

This method calculates the number of users in each profile, applying access control based on the requesting user's permissions:

  • Admin users see the actual count of users in each profile
  • Non-admin users see 1 if they're in the profile, 0 otherwise
@param response the response object to populate with entity counts @return a Future containing the response with entity counts / @Override protected Future getEntityCountPreHook(JsonObject response) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var roles = UserRoleConfigStore.getStore().getItemByUser(response.getLong(USER_ID)); var adminUser = false; if (roles != null && !roles.isEmpty()) { if (roles.getJsonArray(UserRole.USER_ROLE_CONTEXT).contains(USER_SETTINGS + ":" + READ_WRITE_PERMISSION)) { adminUser = true; } } var ids = UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getIds(); for (var index = 0; index < ids.size(); index++) { try { if (adminUser) { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(ids.getLong(index)).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS).size()); } else if (UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(ids.getLong(index)).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS).contains(response.getLong(USER_ID))) { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), 1); } else { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), 0); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } promise.complete(response); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Retrieves all user profiles with access control applied.

This method overrides the default getAll behavior to apply user-specific access control. Non-admin users can only see profiles they belong to, and the user list is filtered to show only themselves.

@param routingContext the routing context for the request

question: Show the pattern for: How does LogForwarder.forward() work?
answer:
A verticle responsible for forwarding logs to external systems.

The LogForwarder manages the forwarding of log events to external systems using TCP or UDP connections. It supports filtering logs based on source, source type, and group, as well as applying complex condition-based filters.

Key features:

  • Supports both TCP and UDP forwarding
  • Maintains connections to TCP destinations
  • Filters logs based on source, source type, and group
  • Applies condition-based filters for fine-grained control
  • Formats logs as JSON or raw text based on configuration

The LogForwarder listens for log events on the event bus and forwards them to the appropriate destinations based on the configured forwarders. / public class LogForwarder extends AbstractVerticle { / Newline separator for log messages / public static final String NEW_LINE_SEPARATOR = "\n"; / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(LogForwarder.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_LOG, "Log Forwarder"); / Number of TCP connection retry attempts / private static final int TCP_RETRIES = MotadataConfigUtil.getLogForwarderTCPRetries(); / Interval (in seconds) between TCP connection retry attempts / private static final int TCP_RETRY_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getLogForwarderTCPRetrySeconds(); / Set for storing qualified forwarder IDs during filtering / private final Set qualifiedItems = new HashSet<>(); / Map of log forwarders indexed by their IDs / private final Map logForwarders = new HashMap<>(); / Map of forwarder IDs indexed by source / private final Map> forwardersBySource = new HashMap<>(); / Map of forwarder IDs indexed by source type / private final Map> forwardersBySourceType = new HashMap<>(); / Map of forwarder IDs indexed by group ID / private final Map> forwardersByGroup = new HashMap<>(); / Map of TCP connections indexed by forwarder ID / private final Map tcpForwarders = new HashMap<>(); / UDP socket for sending UDP messages / private final DatagramSocket udpForwarder = Bootstrap.vertx().createDatagramSocket(new DatagramSocketOptions()); / Event engine for handling log events / private EventEngine eventEngine; @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { try { var items = LogForwarderConfigStore.getStore().getItems(); for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { logForwarders.put(items.getJsonObject(index).getLong(ID), items.getJsonObject(index)); createForwarder(items.getJsonObject(index)); } assign(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } eventEngine = new EventEngine().setEventType(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE)) .setPersistEventOffset(true).setLogger(LOGGER).setEventHandler(this::forward).start(vertx, promise); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION, message -> { var event = message.body(); var notificationType = EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.valueOf(event.getString(CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE)); switch (notificationType) { case ADD_LOG_FORWARDER -> { var item = LogForwarderConfigStore.getStore().getItem(event.getLong(ID)); logForwarders.put(event.getLong(ID), item); createForwarder(item); assign(); } case UPDATE_LOG_FORWARDER -> { //as in case of enabling disabling if its tcp connection then will be removing its connection as we don't know how much time forwarder will be disabled on enable will establish connection logForwarders.put(event.getLong(ID), LogForwarderConfigStore.getStore().getItem(event.getLong(ID))); if (logForwarders.get(event.getLong(ID)).getString(LOG_FORWARDER_STATE).equalsIgnoreCase(NO) && tcpForwarders.containsKey(event.getLong(ID))) { tcpForwarders.remove(event.getLong(ID)).close(); } else { createForwarder(logForwarders.get(event.getLong(ID))); } } case DELETE_LOG_FORWARDER -> { if (tcpForwarders.containsKey(event.getLong(ID))) { tcpForwarders.remove(event.getLong(ID)).close(); } logForwarders.remove(event.getLong(ID)); assign(); } default -> { // do nothing } } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); promise.future().onComplete(result -> LOGGER.debug(config().getString(EVENT_TYPE) + " started successfully!!!")); } / Processes a log event and forwards it to appropriate destinations.

This method is the main entry point for log event processing in the LogForwarder. It performs the following steps:

  • Retrieves the event source configuration
  • Identifies qualified forwarders based on source, source type, and groups
  • For each qualified forwarder:
    • Checks if the forwarder is enabled
    • Applies any configured filters
    • If all conditions are met, forwards the log to the destination

The method supports complex condition-based filtering, allowing for fine-grained control over which logs are forwarded to which destinations. @param event The log event to be processed and potentially forwarded

if (value != null) { buildWorklog(dataPoints, result, value, MetricPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItem(value.getLong(ID)), null); } } } } else { for (var entry : items.entrySet()) { try { keys.clear(); correlatedKeys.clear(); if (valid(entry.getValue(), context)) { var item = MetricPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItem(entry.getValue().getLong(ID)); if ((type.equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.TRACE_METRIC.getName()) && item.getString(POLICY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.TRACE_METRIC.getName())) || !type.equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.TRACE_METRIC.getName()) && !item.getString(POLICY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.TRACE_METRIC.getName())) { if (!groupingFields.isEmpty()) { groupingFields.forEach(groupingField -> { var field = CommonUtil.getString(groupingField); question: How does CommonUtil.normalizeGroupHierarchy() work?
answer:
Retrieves a list of IP addresses for the local machine's network interfaces.

This method: 1. Enumerates all network interfaces on the local machine 2. Filters out loopback, down, and virtual interfaces 3. Checks for valid hardware addresses (MAC addresses) 4. Collects IPv4 addresses with broadcast capability 5. Excludes the VIP (Virtual IP) address configured in the system

The method is useful for identifying the machine's actual network addresses for communication, monitoring, or identification purposes. @return A List of Strings containing the IP addresses of the local machine / public static List getIPAddresses() { var ipAddresses = new ArrayList(); try { var networkInterfaces = NetworkInterface.getNetworkInterfaces(); var hardwareId = new StringBuilder(); while (networkInterfaces.hasMoreElements()) { var networkInterface = networkInterfaces.nextElement(); // Skip loopback, down, and virtual interfaces if (!networkInterface.isLoopback() && networkInterface.isUp() && !networkInterface.isVirtual()) { var hardwareAddress = networkInterface.getHardwareAddress(); if (hardwareAddress != null) { // Format the MAC address hardwareId.setLength(0); for (var i = 0; i < hardwareAddress.length; i++) { hardwareId.append(String.format("%02X%s", hardwareAddress[i], (i < hardwareAddress.length - 1) ? ":" : GlobalConstants.EMPTY_VALUE)); } // Check for valid MAC address (not all zeros) if (!hardwareId.isEmpty() && !hardwareId.toString().contains("00:00:00:00")) { // Filter for IPv4 addresses with broadcast capability networkInterface.getInterfaceAddresses().stream() .filter(interfaceAddress -> !interfaceAddress.toString().contains(":") && interfaceAddress.getBroadcast() != null) .forEach(interfaceAddress -> { var ip = interfaceAddress.getAddress().toString() .replace("/", GlobalConstants.EMPTY_VALUE).trim(); // Exclude VIP address if (!MotadataConfigUtil.getVIPIPAddress().trim().equalsIgnoreCase(ip)) { ipAddresses.add(ip); } }); } } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } return ipAddresses; } / Builds a string representation of a group hierarchy in a normalized format.

This method recursively traverses a group hierarchy, starting from the given group and moving up through its parent groups. It builds a string representation with the format "RootGroup > ParentGroup > ChildGroup", where groups are separated by " > " and ordered from the root (highest level) to the leaf (lowest level).

The method uses recursion to navigate up the hierarchy: 1. If the group has a parent (FIELD_PARENT_GROUP > 0), it prepends the current group name to the accumulated name and recursively processes the parent group 2. When it reaches a group with no parent (root group), it appends the entire accumulated hierarchy to the StringBuilder @param group The group to process (typically a leaf or child group) @param builder The StringBuilder to append the normalized hierarchy string to @param name The accumulated group name hierarchy (null for the initial call)
code: public normalizeGroupHierarchy(JsonObject group, StringBuilder builder, String name) { ... }

question: How does LocalEventRouter.LocalEventRouter() work?
answer:
The LocalEventRouter class routes events to appropriate handlers based on event type and routing key.

This class is responsible for:

  • Deploying multiple event router instances for load balancing
  • Routing events to the appropriate router based on a routing key
  • Supporting different routing strategies (dynamic, round-robin)
  • Managing the lifecycle of router instances (add/remove)
  • Handling event queries and bulk operations
  • Persisting router state for recovery after restart
  • Providing statistics about event processing when enabled

The LocalEventRouter supports multiple routing strategies:

  • Dynamic Routing: Time-based routing that routes to different handlers based on time. This is useful for cases like datastore-writer where data is written minute-wise, so events from the same minute are sent to the same datastore writer.
  • Round Robin Routing: Event-based routing that distributes events evenly across all available handlers. This is useful when multiple events arrive simultaneously and need to be processed in parallel.

The router maintains a mapping between routing keys and router instances, ensuring that events with the same routing key are consistently routed to the same handler. It also supports dynamic scaling by allowing router instances to be added or removed at runtime.

Example usage: 

   // Create and deploy a LocalEventRouter with 4 instances   LocalEventRouter router = new LocalEventRouter(       "metric-events",           // Event type       "deviceId",                // Routing key       4,                         // Number of router instances       "com.mindarray.MetricHandler", // Handler class       false,                     // Non-blocking       true,                      // Enable stats       EventRouter.DYNAMIC        // Routing strategy   );     vertx.deployVerticle(router);     // Send an event to be routed   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put("deviceId", "device-123")       .put("metric", "cpu-usage")       .put("value", 75.5)       .put("timestamp", System.currentTimeMillis());     vertx.eventBus().send("metric-events", event);
/ public class LocalEventRouter extends AbstractVerticle { private static final String PROBE = "probe"; private static final String DEPLOYED_ROUTERS = "deployed.routers"; private static final DeliveryOptions DELIVERY_OPTIONS = new DeliveryOptions(); question: What does the UIActionEventHandler class do?
answer:
The UIActionEventHandler class handles events triggered by user interface actions and routes them to appropriate handlers.

This class is responsible for:

  • Processing UI-initiated events and actions
  • Routing events to appropriate handlers based on event type
  • Enriching events with additional context information
  • Managing notification delivery through various channels (email, integration channels)
  • Validating user inputs and configurations
  • Executing administrative actions (user management, configuration testing, etc.)
  • Handling file uploads and downloads

The handler acts as a bridge between the user interface and the backend systems, translating user actions into system events and routing them to the appropriate components for processing. It also handles the responses from these components and formats them for presentation to the user.

The class supports a wide range of UI actions including:

  • User authentication and authorization
  • Configuration testing (credentials, connections, etc.)
  • Report generation and export
  • Notification management
  • File uploads and downloads
  • System administration tasks

Example usage: 

   // Deploy the UIActionEventHandler   vertx.deployVerticle(new UIActionEventHandler());     // Send a UI action event   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put("action", "test-credential")       .put("credential", credentialJson)       .put("session_id", sessionId);     vertx.eventBus().send("UI_ACTION_CONFIGURATION_TEST", event, reply -> {       if (reply.succeeded()) {           // Handle successful response           JsonObject result = reply.result().body();           System.out.println("Test result: " + result.getString("status"));       } else {           // Handle failure           System.err.println("Test failed: " + reply.cause().getMessage());       }   });

question: Show the pattern for: How does DiscoveryEngine.startServiceCheckDiscovery() work?
answer:
Initiates a discovery process for a specific discovery profile.

This method generates discovery contexts based on the category and type of the discovery profile. It handles different discovery scenarios: - For SERVER, VIRTUALIZATION, NETWORK, OTHER, CLOUD, HCI, SDN, STORAGE categories or URL type: Merges credential contexts based on credential profile selection - For SERVICE_CHECK category: Sets up service check discovery - For other types: Builds contexts based only on target selection (no credentials required)

The method creates appropriate contexts for each target, sets up futures for tracking progress, and initiates the actual discovery process. @param discovery The discovery profile configuration as a JsonObject @param user The username of the user who initiated the discovery @return A Future that completes when the discovery process is initiated, or fails if initialization fails / private Future start(JsonObject discovery, String user) { var promise = Promise.promise(); var futures = new ArrayList>(); var targets = new ArrayList(); try { var discoveryType = CommonUtil.getString(discovery.remove(Discovery.DISCOVERY_TYPE)); var category = NMSConstants.Category.valueOfName(discovery.getString(Discovery.DISCOVERY_CATEGORY)); var type = NMSConstants.Type.valueOfName(CommonUtil.getString(discovery.remove(Discovery.DISCOVERY_OBJECT_TYPE))); discovery.put(Metric.METRIC_PLUGIN, NMSConstants.getMetricPlugin(type)); // timeout will be default timeout we have in our metrics db discovery.put(GlobalConstants.TIMEOUT, ObjectManagerCacheStore.getStore().getTimeoutByMetricPlugin(discovery.getString(Metric.METRIC_PLUGIN))); discovery.put(PLUGIN_ID, ObjectManagerCacheStore.getStore().getPluginIdByMetricPlugin(discovery.getString(Metric.METRIC_PLUGIN))); if (category == NMSConstants.Category.SERVER || category == NMSConstants.Category.VIRTUALIZATION || category == NMSConstants.Category.NETWORK || category == NMSConstants.Category.OTHER || category == NMSConstants.Category.CLOUD || category == NMSConstants.Category.HCI || category == NMSConstants.Category.SDN || category == NMSConstants.Category.STORAGE || category == NMSConstants.Category.CONTAINER_ORCHESTRATION || type == NMSConstants.Type.REST_API || category == NMSConstants.Category.DATABASE || type == NMSConstants.Type.URL) { var credentials = category == NMSConstants.Category.NETWORK && discovery.containsKey(DISCOVERY_CONFIG_MANAGEMENT_STATUS) && discovery.getString(DISCOVERY_CONFIG_MANAGEMENT_STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(YES) ? NMSConstants.filterCredentialProfiles(discovery, false) : CredentialProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItems(discovery.getJsonArray(Discovery.DISCOVERY_CREDENTIAL_PROFILES)); if (credentials != null && !credentials.isEmpty()) { for (var index = 0; index < credentials.size(); index++) { var credential = credentials.getJsonObject(index); credential.mergeIn(credential.getJsonObject(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_CONTEXT)); credential.remove(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_CONTEXT); } discovery.put(Discovery.DISCOVERY_CREDENTIAL_PROFILES, credentials); } else if (category == NMSConstants.Category.NETWORK && discovery.containsKey(DISCOVERY_CONFIG_MANAGEMENT_STATUS) && discovery.getString(DISCOVERY_CONFIG_MANAGEMENT_STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(YES)) { promise.fail(ErrorMessageConstants.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_NOT_PROVIDED); } if (!promise.future().isComplete()) { if (type == NMSConstants.Type.URL || type == NMSConstants.Type.REST_API) { startServiceCheckDiscovery(discovery, targets, futures, discoveryType, type); } else if (category == NMSConstants.Category.CLOUD || type == NMSConstants.Type.CISCO_MERAKI) { var context = new JsonObject(); var future = Promise.promise(); futures.add(future.future()); targets.add(context); future.complete(); } else { setTargets(discoveryType, type, discovery, targets, new JsonObject(), futures, false); } } } else if (category == NMSConstants.Category.SERVICE_CHECK) { startServiceCheckDiscovery(discovery, targets, futures, discoveryType, type); } if (!promise.future().isComplete()) { Future.join(futures).onComplete(result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { if (!targets.isEmpty()) // means targets is qualified to discover { EventBusConstants.updateEvent(DiscoveryCacheStore.getStore().getDiscoveryEventId(discovery.getLong(ID)), String.format(InfoMessageConstants.EVENT_TRACKER_EVENT_STARTED, DateTimeUtil.timestamp()), EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE_RUNNING); // for rest devices update targets in probes.... it is used when user refresh the page or come back to progress page from some other page at that time this probes will update in progress if (category != NMSConstants.Category.CLOUD && category != NMSConstants.Category.HCI && category != NMSConstants.Category.SDN && category != NMSConstants.Category.STORAGE && category != NMSConstants.Category.CONTAINER_ORCHESTRATION && category != NMSConstants.Category.DATABASE) // for cloud we don't have target wise progress hence no need to track their events in probes { var probes = new JsonObject(); var iterator = targets.iterator(); var doneProbes = 0; while (iterator.hasNext()) { var target = iterator.next(); // in future if we want to increase limit for ping discovery only need to add condition here...now no need to do any validation in API side... if ((discoveryType == null || !discoveryType.equalsIgnoreCase(DISCOVERY_TYPE_CSV) || doneProbes < DISCOVERY_CSV_MAX_PROBE_LIMIT)) { var context = new JsonObject().put(OBJECT_IP, target.getString(OBJECT_IP) != null ? target.getString(OBJECT_IP) : target.getString(OBJECT_TARGET)) .put(OBJECT_TARGET, target.getString(OBJECT_TARGET)) .put(DISCOVERY_PROGRESS, 0.0); if (target.containsKey(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_AGENT)) { context.put(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_AGENT, target.getLong(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_AGENT)); } if (!probes.containsKey(target.getString(OBJECT_TARGET))) { probes.put(target.getString(OBJECT_TARGET), new JsonArray(new ArrayList<>(1))); } probes.getJsonArray(target.getString(OBJECT_TARGET)).add(context); } doneProbes++; } DiscoveryCacheStore.getStore().addProbes(discovery.getLong(ID), probes); } DiscoveryCacheStore.getStore().init(discovery.getLong(ID), targets.size()); // update qualified targets size in cache store discovery.put(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_DISCOVERY_METHOD, discovery.containsKey(Discovery.DISCOVERY_METHOD) ? NMSConstants.DiscoveryMethod.valueOf(discovery.getString(Discovery.DISCOVERY_METHOD)).name() : NMSConstants.DiscoveryMethod.REMOTE.name()); if (discovery.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_EVENT_PROCESSORS) != null) { discovery.put(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_EVENT_PROCESSORS, discovery.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_EVENT_PROCESSORS)); } // update probes to ui EventBusConstants.publish(EventBusConstants.UI_NOTIFICATION_DISCOVERY_PROBES, new JsonObject().put(RESULT, targets).put(ID, discovery.getLong(ID))); EventBusConstants.publish(EventBusConstants.UI_NOTIFICATION_DISCOVERY_STATISTICS, DiscoveryCacheStore.getStore().getDiscoveryStatistics(discovery.getLong(ID)).put(ID, discovery.getLong(ID))); for (var target : targets) { // if discovery has tags the go with it , else check for target which might have tag from csv (multiple target might have multiple tags) discovery.put(DISCOVERY_USER_TAGS, target.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_USER_TAGS) != null ? target.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_USER_TAGS) : discovery.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_USER_TAGS)); discovery.put(DISCOVERY_GROUPS, target.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_GROUPS) != null ? target.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_GROUPS) : discovery.getJsonArray(DISCOVERY_GROUPS)); target.mergeIn(discovery) .put(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_TYPE, type.getName()).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, CommonUtil.newEventId()).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_DISCOVERY); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ADD, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CONTEXT, target) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, target.getLong(EVENT_ID)) .put(USER_NAME, user) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE_QUEUED) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_DISCOVERY)); vertx.eventBus().send(category == NMSConstants.Category.CLOUD || type == NMSConstants.Type.CISCO_MERAKI ? EventBusConstants.EVENT_ROUTER + EventBusConstants.DEFAULT_ROUTER_INDEX : EventBusConstants.EVENT_ROUTER, target); } promise.complete(); } else { promise.fail(ErrorMessageConstants.DISCOVERY_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND); } } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); promise.fail(result.cause()); } }); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(CommonUtil.formatStackTrace(exception.getCause().getStackTrace())); } return promise.future(); } / Sets up and initiates a service check discovery process.

question: How does MetricPolicyTriggerDurationCalculator.write() work?
answer:
MetricPolicyTriggerDurationCalculator tracks and calculates the duration of policy triggers and state changes.

This class: 1. Maintains information about how long policies have been in specific states 2. Tracks policy flaps (state changes) and their durations 3. Persists policy state information for high availability and recovery 4. Handles policy acknowledgments and comments 5. Provides duration data for visualization and reporting

The calculator runs as a Vert.x verticle and communicates with other components through the event bus to update and retrieve policy duration information. / public class MetricPolicyTriggerDurationCalculator extends AbstractVerticle { private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(MetricPolicyTriggerDurationCalculator.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_POLICY, "Metric Policy Trigger Duration Calculator"); private static final int POLICY_FLAP_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getPolicyFlapFlushTimerSeconds(); private final JsonObject objectPolicyStatuses = new JsonObject(); private final JsonObject policyTriggerTicks = new JsonObject(); private final AtomicBoolean policyTriggerTickDirty = new AtomicBoolean(); private final AtomicBoolean policyStatusDirty = new AtomicBoolean(); private boolean updated = false; / Starts the MetricPolicyTriggerDurationCalculator verticle. This method: 1. Loads persisted policy trigger ticks and flap durations from backup files 2. Sets up event bus handlers for duration calculation, queries, and acknowledgments 3. Initializes periodic timers for flushing data to disk 4. Registers with the high availability system for cache synchronization @param promise A promise that will be completed when startup is finished or failed if an error occurs / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { try { var flushTimerSeconds = new AtomicInteger(POLICY_FLAP_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS); var file = new File(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + PolicyEngineConstants.METRIC_POLICY_TRIGGER_TICKS); if (file.exists()) { var buffer = vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(file.getPath()); if (buffer != null && buffer.getBytes().length > 0) { policyTriggerTicks.mergeIn(new JsonObject(Buffer.buffer(CodecUtil.toBytes(buffer.getBytes())))); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s loaded from the backup file...", PolicyEngineConstants.METRIC_POLICY_TRIGGER_TICKS)); } } else { vertx.fileSystem().createFileBlocking(file.getPath()); } file = new File(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + PolicyEngineConstants.METRIC_POLICY_FLAP_DURATIONS); if (file.exists()) { var buffer = vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(file.getPath()); if (buffer != null && buffer.getBytes().length > 0) { new JsonObject(Buffer.buffer(CodecUtil.toBytes(buffer.getBytes()))).getMap().forEach((key, value) -> objectPolicyStatuses.put(key, JsonObject.mapFrom(value))); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s loaded from the backup file...", PolicyEngineConstants.METRIC_POLICY_FLAP_DURATIONS)); } } else { vertx.fileSystem().createFileBlocking(file.getPath()); } vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLICY_SEVERITY_DURATION_CALCULATE, message -> { try { if (!message.body().isEmpty()) { var event = message.body(); var key = event.getLong(ENTITY_ID) + SEPARATOR + event.getLong(ID) + SEPARATOR + (event.getValue(INSTANCE, null) != null && !CommonUtil.getString(event.getValue(INSTANCE)).isEmpty() ? event.getString(GlobalConstants.METRIC) + SEPARATOR + event.getValue(INSTANCE) : event.getString(GlobalConstants.METRIC)); LOGGER.trace(String.format("processing key : %s ",key)); if (objectPolicyStatuses.containsKey(key)) { var duration = objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).getInteger(DURATION, 0); if (!objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).getString(SEVERITY).equalsIgnoreCase(event.getString(SEVERITY))) // flap change { / There are two case 1. previous.flap.timestamp = event.timestamp (auto_clear) -> we get duration 10, we add duration in event.timestamp 2. previous.flap.timestamp > event.timestamp (polling delay) -> we get duration < difference, we add difference + 1 to maintain sequence of flap / var previousFlapTimeStamp = objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).getLong(PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP); var currentTimeStamp = event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP); var flapDiffSeconds = event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP) - previousFlapTimeStamp; if (flapDiffSeconds <= 0) { currentTimeStamp = event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP) + (duration <= Math.abs(flapDiffSeconds) ? 1 + Math.abs(flapDiffSeconds) : duration); flapDiffSeconds = currentTimeStamp - previousFlapTimeStamp; } send(objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).put(DURATION, flapDiffSeconds)); // if flap then send data to DB.. // if flap then notify to refresh respective widgets Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_VISUALIZATION_REALTIME_WIDGET_REFRESH, new JsonObject().put(EVENT_CONTEXT, new JsonObject().put(VisualizationConstants.PLUGIN, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.METRIC_POLICY_DURATION_METRIC.getName() + DASH_SEPARATOR + ObjectManagerCacheStore.getStore().getMetricName(DatastoreConstants.PluginId.METRIC_POLICY_DURATION_METRIC.getName())).put(NMSConstants.OBJECT, new JsonArray().add(CommonUtil.getString(ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getObjectId(event.getLong(ENTITY_ID))))))); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("Current severity for policy.key %s of %s is %s with %s is %d for duration %d with flapDiff %d and new Severity %s with timestamp is %d which triggered for value : %s", key, event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP), objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).getString(SEVERITY), PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, previousFlapTimeStamp, duration, flapDiffSeconds, event.getString(SEVERITY), event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP), event.getString(VALUE))); } objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).mergeIn(event).put(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_NOTE, EMPTY_VALUE).put(PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(PREVIOUS_FLAP_VALUE, event.getValue(VALUE)).remove(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_ACKNOWLEDGE); if ((event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP) - previousFlapTimeStamp) <= 0) // MOTADATA-558 in case of auto-clear and polling scheduler clashes { if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("!!Altered timestamp!! ip : %s, %s : %d, event.timestamp : %d, duration : %d,updated %s : %d", event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP), PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, previousFlapTimeStamp, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP), duration, PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, currentTimeStamp)); } objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).put(PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, currentTimeStamp); } MetricPolicyFlapDurationCacheStore.getStore().update(key, objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key)); } else { event.remove(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_RUNBOOK_ID); // as runbook id will not change if severity not changed objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).mergeIn(event); MetricPolicyFlapDurationCacheStore.getStore().update(key, objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key)); } } else { objectPolicyStatuses.put(key, event.put(DURATION, 0).put(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_NOTE, EMPTY_VALUE).put(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_RUNBOOK_ID, event.getLong(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_RUNBOOK_ID)).put(PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(PREVIOUS_FLAP_VALUE, event.getValue(VALUE))); MetricPolicyFlapDurationCacheStore.getStore().update(key, objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key)); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_VISUALIZATION_REALTIME_WIDGET_REFRESH, new JsonObject().put(EVENT_CONTEXT, new JsonObject().put(VisualizationConstants.PLUGIN, DatastoreConstants.PluginId.METRIC_POLICY_DURATION_METRIC.getName() + DASH_SEPARATOR + ObjectManagerCacheStore.getStore().getMetricName(DatastoreConstants.PluginId.METRIC_POLICY_DURATION_METRIC.getName())).put(NMSConstants.OBJECT, new JsonArray().add(CommonUtil.getString(ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getObjectId(event.getLong(ENTITY_ID))))))); } if (!policyTriggerTicks.containsKey(key)) { updated = true; policyTriggerTicks.put(key, System.currentTimeMillis()); } LOGGER.trace(String.format("flap cache store for key %s , %s ", key, objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(key).encode())); event.put(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_FIRST_TRIGGER_TICK, policyTriggerTicks.getLong(key)); if (MotadataConfigUtil.devMode()) { vertx.eventBus().publish(EVENT_METRIC_POLICY + "." + "test",new JsonObject().mergeIn(event).put(POLICY_KEY,key)); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLICY_TRIGGER_DURATION_QUERY, message -> { var request = message.body(); if (!request.isEmpty() && request.containsKey(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_KEY)) // if policy key is present then return only that policy data { message.reply(objectPolicyStatuses.getJsonObject(request.getString(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_KEY), new JsonObject())); } else { message.reply(new JsonObject().mergeIn(objectPolicyStatuses)); } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLICY_TRIGGER_TICK_QUERY, message -> message.reply(new JsonObject().mergeIn(policyTriggerTicks))); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLICY_ACKNOWLEDGE, message -> { var event = message.body(); var policy = MetricPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItem(event.getLong(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_ID)); var key = event.getLong(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_ID) + SEPARATOR + event.getLong(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_ID) + SEPARATOR + (event.getValue(INSTANCE, null) != null && !CommonUtil.getString(event.getValue(INSTANCE)).isEmpty() ? policy.getJsonObject(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_CONTEXT).getString(METRIC) + SEPARATOR + event.getValue(INSTANCE) : policy.getJsonObject(PolicyEngineConstants.POLICY_CONTEXT).getString(METRIC)); question: Show the pattern for: How does DatastoreRetentionJob.cleanup() work?
answer:
The DatastoreRetentionJob class is responsible for managing data retention in the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and performs two main tasks:

  • Triggering datastore retention by publishing an event to the event bus
  • Cleaning up cache files based on a configurable retention policy

The job is scheduled to run every day at midnight (12:00 AM) to ensure that old data is regularly purged from the system, preventing excessive disk usage and maintaining system performance. / public class DatastoreRetentionJob implements Job { / CRON expression for scheduling this job to run every day at midnight (12:00 AM) / public static final String DATASTORE_RETENTION_JOB_CRON_EXPRESSION = "0 0 0 ? "; // At 00:00:00am every day / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(DatastoreRetentionJob.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_JOB, "Datastore Retention Job"); / Executes the datastore retention job.

This method performs two main tasks:

  1. Triggers datastore event retention by publishing an event to the event bus
  2. Cleans up cache files based on the configured retention policy

The datastore retention is handled by other components that listen for the EVENT_DATASTORE_RETENTION_TRIGGER event. The cache file cleanup is handled directly by this class through the {@link #cleanup(long)} method. @param context the context in which the job is executed @throws JobExecutionException if an error occurs during job execution / @Override public void execute(JobExecutionContext context) throws JobExecutionException { try { var currentTimeMillis = System.currentTimeMillis(); // Trigger datastore event retention by publishing an event LOGGER.info("executing datastore retention job..."); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().publish(EVENT_DATASTORE_RETENTION_TRIGGER, null); // Clean up cache files based on retention policy LOGGER.info("cache file clean up job started ...."); cleanup(currentTimeMillis); LOGGER.info("cache file clean up job completed ...."); LOGGER.info("slo cycle clean up job started ...."); cleanupSLOCycles(currentTimeMillis); LOGGER.info("slo cycle clean up job completed ...."); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } / Cleans up cache files based on the configured retention policy.

This method deletes cache files that are older than the retention period configured in the system. It works by:

  1. Creating a set of dates to exclude from deletion (recent dates within the retention period)
  2. Checking each file in the cache directory
  3. Deleting files that don't match the excluded dates

The retention period is determined by {@link MotadataConfigUtil#getCacheFilesRetentionDays()}.

question: How does TraceStatCalculator.merge() work?

A verticle responsible for calculating and managing trace statistics in real-time. This class processes trace events, computes various metrics, and periodically generates service-level key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key features include:

  • Service-level KPI computation (error rates, durations, throughput)
  • Percentile calculations (P50, P99) for trace durations
  • Periodic metrics publishing to event bus
  • Integration with data store for metrics persistence

The calculator processes the following metrics:

  • Total trace count per service
  • Average trace duration
  • Error rates and success counts
  • Throughput (traces per minute)
  • Latency percentiles (P50, P99)

Statistics are calculated and flushed at configurable intervals (default: {@code trace.stat.flush.timer.seconds}). The calculator maintains separate statistics for each service and supports concurrent processing of trace events. / public class TraceStatCalculator extends AbstractVerticle { private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(TraceStatCalculator.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_TRACE, "Trace Stat Calculator"); private final DecimalFormat decimalFormat = new DecimalFormat("#.####"); // Time interval to update service stats. Default - 60 sec. private static final int TRACE_STAT_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceStatFlushTimerSeconds(); // Time interval to update service dependency in dependency manager. Default - 30 sec. private static final Integer SERVICE_DEPENDENCY_FLUSH_INTERVAL = MotadataConfigUtil.getServiceDependencyFlushTimerSeconds(); // Time to clean up the trace context after given time. Default - 1 min. private static final Integer TRACE_CONTEXT_CLEANUP_TIME = MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceContextCleanUpTimeSeconds(); private final Map statsByService = new HashMap<>(); private final Map> durationsByService = new HashMap<>(); private final Map entityStatsByService = new HashMap<>(); private final Map entityStats = new HashMap<>(); private final Map> entityDurationsByService = new HashMap<>(); private final JsonObject event = new JsonObject(); private final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder(0); private Set mappers; @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { try { mappers = new HashSet<>(); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TRACE_STAT, message -> merge(message.body())); vertx.setPeriodic(MotadataConfigUtil.getEnvironmentType().equalsIgnoreCase(ENV_TEST) ? 150 1000L : TRACE_STAT_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS 1000L, handler -> calculate()); // Timer will process trace data to build service dependency relationships and cleans up old traces at every 1 min. vertx.setPeriodic(MotadataConfigUtil.getEnvironmentType().equalsIgnoreCase(ENV_TEST) ? 5 1000 : SERVICE_DEPENDENCY_FLUSH_INTERVAL 1000L, timer -> sendServiceDependencyEvent()); // Reset trace max events counter at every second vertx.setPeriodic(1000, id -> TraceCacheStore.getStore().reset()); if (MotadataConfigUtil.getEnvironmentType().equalsIgnoreCase(ENV_TEST)) { vertx.eventBus().localConsumer("test.trace.stat", message -> message.reply(new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.SERVICE_NAME, JsonObject.mapFrom(statsByService)))).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer("test.entity.trace.stat", message -> message.reply(new JsonObject().put(TraceConstants.SERVICE_NAME, JsonObject.mapFrom(entityStatsByService)))).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer("test.trace.stat.compute.percentile", message -> message.reply(message.body().put("percentile", computePercentile(message.body().getJsonArray("data").getList(), message.body().getInteger("percentile"))))); } promise.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } } / Merges trace statistics into internal data structures for aggregation.

question: How does HTTPServer.recv() work?
answer:
Binds the HTTP server to the configured port and starts listening for WebSocket connections. Uses direct webSocketHandler approach for simplicity. @return a Future that completes when the server successfully binds. / @Override public Future bind() { var promise = Promise.promise(); var options = new HttpServerOptions() .setReuseAddress(true) .setReusePort(true) .setTcpKeepAlive(true) .setTcpNoDelay(true) .setSendBufferSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getHTTPBufferSizeBytes()) .setReceiveBufferSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getHTTPBufferSizeBytes()) .setCompressionSupported(true) .setMaxWebSocketMessageSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getHTTPBufferSizeBytes()) .setAcceptBacklog(MotadataConfigUtil.getWebSocketBacklogQueueSize()) .setIdleTimeout(MotadataConfigUtil.getHTTPIdleTimeoutSeconds()) .setSsl(MotadataConfigUtil.httpSslEnabled()); if (MotadataConfigUtil.httpSslEnabled()) { options.setSsl(true).setUseAlpn(true).setEnabledSecureTransportProtocols(Set.of("TLSv1.2", "TLSv1.3")) .setKeyCertOptions(new PemKeyCertOptions().setCertPath(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "server-cert.pem") .setKeyPath(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "server-key.pem")); } server = Bootstrap.vertx().createHttpServer(options); recv(); server.listen(config.getInteger(PORT)) .onComplete(handler -> { if (handler.succeeded()) { LOGGER.info(String.format("%s HTTP server with WebSocket opened on port %s",Bootstrap.bootstrapType(), config.getInteger(PORT))); promise.complete(); } else { LOGGER.warn(String.format("%s failed to listen on port %s",Bootstrap.bootstrapType(),config.getInteger(PORT))); LOGGER.error(handler.cause()); promise.fail(handler.cause()); } }); return promise.future(); } / Configures the HTTP server to handle WebSocket connections and sets up message processing handlers. This method establishes the core WebSocket communication infrastructure for the server.

This method performs the following operations:

  • Sets up WebSocket connection handler for incoming client connections
  • Configures binary message handler for processing data messages
  • Configures text message handler for client registration
  • Sets up connection cleanup handlers for graceful disconnection
  • Initializes periodic keep-alive mechanism

WebSocket Handlers:

  • Connection Handler: Logs new client connections and sets up per-connection handlers
  • Binary Message Handler: Processes incoming data messages and forwards them to the event bus
  • Text Message Handler: Handles client registration messages containing event topics
  • Close Handler: Manages connection cleanup and removes clients from topic mappings
  • Exception Handler: Logs WebSocket-related exceptions for debugging

Message Processing:

  • Binary messages are forwarded directly to the Vert.x event bus under the configured event type
  • Text messages are parsed as JSON to extract event topic for client registration
  • All message processing includes proper error handling and logging

Connection Management:

  • Maintains a mapping of event topics to connected WebSocket clients
  • Automatically removes disconnected clients from topic mappings
  • Cleans up round-robin indexes when topic groups become empty

This method is called internally during server binding and should not be invoked directly.

@see #bind() @see #keepAliveConnection() @see #send(String, byte[])

question: Show the pattern for: How does ZMQClient.ZMQClient() work?
answer:
ZeroMQ (ZMQ) client implementation for the Motadata transport layer.

This class provides a ZeroMQ-based transport client that supports multiple socket modes including SUB (receiver), PUSH, and PULL patterns. It implements the {@link TransportClient} interface to provide a standardized transport abstraction layer.

The client supports different ZeroMQ socket patterns:

  • SUB (Receivers): Receives messages from PUB sockets, supports topic filtering
  • PUSH: Sends messages to PULL sockets in a load-balanced manner
  • PULL: Receives messages from PUSH sockets in a round-robin fashion

Key features:

  • Configurable High Water Mark (HWM) for message queuing
  • TCP keep-alive support for connection reliability
  • Topic-based message filtering for SUB sockets
  • Thread-safe message handling with atomic operations
  • Integration with Vert.x event bus for message routing

Configuration example:

{@code   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put("SOCKET_MODE", "SUB")       .put("HOST", "localhost")       .put("PORT", 5555)       .put("EVENT_TYPE", "remote.events");     ZMQClient client = new ZMQClient(config);   client.registerMessageHandler(message -> {       // Handle received message   });   client.connect().onSuccess(v -> {       client.receive(); // Start receiving messages   });   }
@author Motadata Engineering Team @version 1.0 @since 1.0 @see TransportClient @see ZMQServer / public class ZMQClient implements TransportClient { / The underlying ZeroMQ socket instance used for communication. This socket is configured based on the socket mode specified in the configuration. / private ZMQ.Socket client; / Configuration object containing connection parameters such as host, port, socket mode, and event type. This configuration is used to establish the ZMQ connection and determine behavior. / private final JsonObject config; / Atomic boolean flag indicating whether the client should continue processing events. Used to control the message receiving loop in a thread-safe manner. / private final AtomicBoolean hasMoreEvent = new AtomicBoolean(false); / Logger instance for this ZMQ client, configured with appropriate context and component name. / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(ZMQClient.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_EVENT_BUS, "ZMQ Client", GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.AGENT.equals(Bootstrap.bootstrapType())); / The event type identifier used for routing messages to the appropriate event bus consumers. Extracted from the configuration during initialization. / private final String eventType; / Message handler consumer that processes received messages. Can be customized via {@link #registerMessageHandler(Consumer)} method. / private Consumer consumer; private Thread thread; / Constructs a new ZMQClient with the specified configuration.

The configuration object must contain the following required parameters:

  • SOCKET_MODE: The ZMQ socket mode (SUB, PUSH, or PULL)
  • HOST: The target host address to connect to
  • PORT: The target port number
  • EVENT_TYPE: The event type for message routing

The constructor initializes the default message handler to send messages to the Vert.x event bus using the specified event type.

@param config the configuration object containing connection parameters and settings. Must not be null and should contain all required parameters. @throws NullPointerException if config is null @throws IllegalArgumentException if required configuration parameters are missing

question: How does DiscoveryEngine.prepare() work?
answer:
Determines the set of targets to exclude from discovery.

This method processes the discovery configuration to identify targets that should be excluded from the discovery process. It handles different exclusion methods: - IP Range exclusion - IP List exclusion - Host List exclusion

The method returns a set of target IPs or hostnames that should be excluded from discovery. @param discovery The discovery profile configuration as a JsonObject @return A Set of String values representing targets to exclude from discovery / private Set excludeTargets(JsonObject discovery) { var filters = new HashSet(); try { if (discovery.containsKey(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGETS) && discovery.getJsonArray(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGETS) != null) { if (discovery.getString(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGET_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(DISCOVERY_TYPE_IP_ADDRESS)) { discovery.getJsonArray(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGETS).forEach(target -> filters.add(CommonUtil.getString(target))); } else if (discovery.getString(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGET_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(DISCOVERY_TYPE_IP_ADDRESS_RANGE)) { for (var index = 0; index < discovery.getJsonArray(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGETS).size(); index++) { var range = discovery.getJsonArray(Discovery.DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE_TARGETS).getString(index); var start = range.split("-")[0].trim(); var end = start.substring(0, start.lastIndexOf('.')) + "." + range.split("-")[1].trim(); if (APIUtil.validateRange(start, end)) { CommonUtil.calculateIPRange(InetAddress.getByName(start), InetAddress.getByName(end)).forEach(ip -> filters.add(CommonUtil.getString(ip))); } } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } return filters; } / Main function of discovery used to generate discovery objects based on discovery results / / Prepares the final list of discovered objects after a discovery process.

private static final Set PASSOVER_CONFIG_STORES = Set.of(AbstractConfigStore.ConfigStore.METRIC, AbstractConfigStore.ConfigStore.TAG); private static final Set PASSOVER_CACHE_STORES = Set.of(AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.OBJECT_MANAGER, AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.TAG, AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.METRIC_POLICY_FLAP_DURATION, AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.NETROUTE_POLICY_FLAP_DURATION, AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.OBJECT, AbstractCacheStore.CacheStore.TOPOLOGY); public static ConfigDBService configDBService; private static ComplianceDBService complianceDBService; private static CacheService cacheService; private static ConfigCacheService configCacheService; private static PolicyCacheService policyCacheService;
