question: Show the pattern for: How does DNSUtil.resolve() work?
answer:
DNS Utility class that provides comprehensive DNS resolution services for the Motadata platform.

This class extends {@link AbstractVerticle} and serves as the central DNS management component, handling both forward and reverse DNS lookups, DNS cache management, and DNS server profile configuration. It automatically discovers system DNS servers and provides event-driven DNS resolution services.

Key Features:

  • Automatic discovery and configuration of system DNS servers
  • Forward DNS resolution (hostname to IP)
  • Reverse DNS resolution (IP to hostname)
  • DNS cache management and flushing
  • Multiple DNS server profile support with fallback mechanism
  • Event-driven architecture for asynchronous DNS operations
  • Integration with Motadata's object management system

DNS Server Priority:

DNS servers are prioritized with automatic (system-discovered) servers taking precedence over manually configured ones. The class implements a fallback mechanism where if one DNS server fails to resolve a query, it automatically tries the next available server.

/ public class DNSUtil extends AbstractVerticle { private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(DNSUtil.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_UTIL, "DNS Util"); / Initializes the DNS resolver module and sets up the complete DNS management infrastructure.

This method serves as the entry point for the DNS utility service, performing comprehensive initialization of DNS server profiles, event bus consumers, and system integration. It automatically discovers system DNS servers and configures them as default profiles if they don't already exist.

Initialization Process:

  1. System DNS Discovery: Uses {@link ResolverConfig#getCurrentConfig()} to discover DNS servers configured in the system's network settings
  2. Profile Creation: For each discovered DNS server, checks if a profile already exists in {@code DNSServerProfileConfigStore}. If not, creates a new profile with default settings
  3. Database Persistence: Saves new DNS profiles to the database table {@code TBL_DNS_SERVER_PROFILE} with automatic resolver type
  4. Event Bus Registration: Sets up local consumers for all DNS-related events

Event Bus Consumers Registered:

  • {@code EVENT_DNS_SERVER_RESOLVER}: Triggers bulk DNS resolution for all cached IPs and objects
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_OBJECT_DELETE}: Handles cleanup when objects are deleted from the system
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_LOOKUP}: Performs forward DNS lookup for a single hostname
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_REVERSE_LOOKUP}: Performs reverse DNS lookup for a single IP address
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_CACHE_FLUSH}: Flushes both system and application DNS caches
@param promise A {@link Promise} that will be completed when initialization succeeds or fails. Success indicates that all event consumers are registered and the service is ready to handle DNS requests. Failure indicates a critical error that prevents service startup. @throws Exception If there is an unrecoverable error during startup, such as failure to access system DNS configuration or register event bus consumers / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { try { vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DNS_RESOLVER, message -> resolve(DNSCacheStore.getStore().getIps(), MotadataConfigUtil.getDNSObjectResolution() ? ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItems() : new JsonArray(), sort(), 0)); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DNS_OBJECT_DELETE, message -> delete(message.body())); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DNS_LOOKUP, message -> resolve(message, sort(), 0, false)); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DNS_REVERSE_LOOKUP, message -> resolve(message, sort(), 0, true)); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DNS_CACHE_FLUSH, message -> vertx.executeBlocking(future -> { try { var arguments = new ArrayList(); if(OS_WINDOWS) { arguments.add("cmd.exe"); arguments.add("/c"); arguments.add("ipconfig /flushdns"); } else { arguments.add("bash"); arguments.add("-c"); arguments.add("sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches"); } var processBuilder = new ProcessBuilder(arguments); processBuilder.directory(new File(CURRENT_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR)); var process = processBuilder.start(); if (CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug(String.format("DNS cache flush process %s started", process.pid())); } var output = new StringBuilder(); var bufferedReader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(process.getInputStream())); String line; while ((line = bufferedReader.readLine()) != null) { output.append(line).append(NEW_LINE); } bufferedReader.close(); process.getErrorStream().close(); process.getOutputStream().close(); process.getInputStream().close(); process.destroy(); LOGGER.debug(String.format("Output flush DNS %s",output)); if ((!output.isEmpty() && !OS_WINDOWS) || (OS_WINDOWS && !output.isEmpty() && !output.toString().contains("Successfully flushed"))) //means getting some error so will not clear records { LOGGER.warn("Failed to flush DNS cache....."); future.fail("Failed to flush DNS cache....."); } else { Bootstrap.configDBService().drop(DBConstants.TBL_DNS_RECORD, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { DNSCacheStore.getStore().clear(); LOGGER.info("DNS records flushed successfully..."); future.complete(); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); future.fail(result.cause().getMessage()); } }); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); future.fail(exception); } }, false, result -> { })).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); addSystemDNS(); promise.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } } / Resolves a single hostname or IP address using the available DNS server profiles with fallback support.

This method implements a recursive fallback mechanism that tries each DNS server profile in sequence until a successful resolution is achieved or all servers have been exhausted. It handles both forward and reverse DNS lookups based on the {@code reverseLookup} parameter.

Resolution Process:

  1. Attempts resolution using the DNS server at the current index
  2. If successful, replies to the message and optionally caches the result
  3. If failed, recursively tries the next DNS server in the list
  4. Continues until resolution succeeds or all servers are exhausted

Caching Behavior:

Successful resolutions are automatically cached in the DNS record table for future reference, improving performance for subsequent lookups of the same hostname or IP.

@param message The event bus message containing the hostname or IP to resolve @param profiles Array of DNS server profiles to use for resolution, sorted by priority @param index Current index in the profiles array (used for recursive fallback) @param reverseLookup {@code true} for reverse DNS lookup (IP to hostname), {@code false} for forward lookup (hostname to IP)

question: How does UserProfile.getAll() work?
answer:
Updates a user profile by assigning or unassigning users.

This method handles both assignment and unassignment operations by:

  • Updating the profile's user list in the database

@param routingContext the routing context for the request @param profileId the ID of the profile being updated @param entities the updated list of user IDs for the profile @param users the specific user IDs being assigned or unassigned @param assign true for assignment operation, false for unassignment @return a Future that completes when the update operation is finished / private Future updateItem(RoutingContext routingContext, long profileId, JsonArray entities, JsonArray users, boolean assign) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var username = routingContext.user().principal().getString(USER_NAME) != null ? routingContext.user().principal().getString(USER_NAME) : DEFAULT_USER; var remoteAddress = routingContext.request().remoteAddress().host() != null ? routingContext.request().remoteAddress().host() : SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS; Bootstrap.configDBService().update(DBConstants.TBL_USER_PROFILE, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, ID).put(VALUE, profileId), new JsonObject().put(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS, entities), username, remoteAddress, result -> UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().updateItem(profileId).onComplete(asyncResult -> { var futures = new ArrayList>(); var usersByProfile = new HashMap>(); for (var index = 0; index < users.size(); index++) { var future = Promise.promise(); try { futures.add(future.future()); var userId = users.getLong(index); var profile = assign ? profileId : DUMMY_ID; var oldProfileId = UserConfigStore.getStore().remove(userId); usersByProfile.computeIfAbsent(oldProfileId, value -> new ArrayList<>()).add(userId); Bootstrap.configDBService().update(DBConstants.TBL_USER, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, ID).put(VALUE, userId), new JsonObject().put(User.USER_PROFILE, profile), username, remoteAddress, userResult -> { try { UserConfigStore.getStore().updateItem(userId); if (assign) { UserConfigStore.getStore().updateProfile(userId, profileId); } future.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); future.fail(exception); } }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); future.fail(exception); } } Future.join(futures).onComplete(futureAsyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { updateProfile(usersByProfile).onComplete(profileAsyncResult -> { if (profileAsyncResult.succeeded()) { promise.complete(); } else { promise.fail(profileAsyncResult.cause()); } }); } else { promise.fail(asyncResult.cause()); } }); })); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Pre-processing hook for retrieving references to a user profile.

This method retrieves the users associated with a profile, applying access control based on the requesting user's permissions:

  • Admin users can see all users in the profile
  • Non-admin users can only see themselves if they're in the profile
@param routingContext the routing context for the request @param response the response object to populate with user references @return a Future containing the response with user references / @Override protected Future getReferencesPreHook(RoutingContext routingContext, JsonObject response) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var userIds = UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(CommonUtil.getLong(routingContext.request().getParam(ID))).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS); var items = new JsonArray(); if (routingContext.user().principal().getJsonArray(APIConstants.USER_PERMISSIONS).contains(USER_SETTINGS + ":" + READ_WRITE_PERMISSION)) { for (var index = 0; index < userIds.size(); index++) { items.add(UserConfigStore.getStore().getItem(userIds.getLong(index))); } } else if (userIds.contains(routingContext.user().attributes().getJsonObject("accessToken").getLong(ID))) { items.add(UserConfigStore.getStore().getItem(routingContext.user().attributes().getJsonObject("accessToken").getLong(ID))); } if (!items.isEmpty()) { response.put(Entity.USER.getName(), items); } promise.complete(response); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Pre-processing hook for retrieving entity counts for user profiles.

This method calculates the number of users in each profile, applying access control based on the requesting user's permissions:

@param response the response object to populate with entity counts @return a Future containing the response with entity counts / @Override protected Future getEntityCountPreHook(JsonObject response) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var roles = UserRoleConfigStore.getStore().getItemByUser(response.getLong(USER_ID)); var adminUser = false; if (roles != null && !roles.isEmpty()) { if (roles.getJsonArray(UserRole.USER_ROLE_CONTEXT).contains(USER_SETTINGS + ":" + READ_WRITE_PERMISSION)) { adminUser = true; } } var ids = UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getIds(); for (var index = 0; index < ids.size(); index++) { try { if (adminUser) { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(ids.getLong(index)).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS).size()); } else if (UserProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(ids.getLong(index)).getJsonArray(UserProfile.USER_PROFILE_USERS).contains(response.getLong(USER_ID))) { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), 1); } else { response.put(CommonUtil.getString(ids.getLong(index)), 0); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } promise.complete(response); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Retrieves all user profiles with access control applied.

question: What does the FlowProcessor class do?
answer:
Processes network flow data by enriching it with additional information and transforming it for analysis.

The FlowProcessor is a core component of the flow processing system that receives raw flow data from the FlowListener and performs the following operations:

  • Enriches flow data with geolocation information (country, city, coordinates)
  • Adds Autonomous System (AS) information to source and destination IPs
  • Decodes IP addresses and resolves them to hostnames when possible
  • Translates protocol numbers to protocol names
  • Decodes Type of Service (ToS) values
  • Interprets TCP flags
  • Maps interface indices to interface names
  • Calculates traffic metrics (bytes per second, packets per second, etc.)
  • Formats the enriched data for storage and analysis

The processor uses various configuration stores to retrieve mapping information and settings that control how flow data is processed and enriched.

After processing, the enriched flow data is published to the event bus for consumption by other components such as the FlowStatCalculator and storage systems.

question: Show the pattern for: How does ConfigDBServiceImpl.buildTuple() work?
answer:
Saves a single record to the specified table.

This method creates the table if it doesn't exist and inserts the record with automatic ID generation if not provided. The operation includes audit logging and high availability synchronization.

@param table The name of the table to save the record to @param record The JSON record to save @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive the generated record ID or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService save(String table, JsonObject record, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { saveAll(table, new JsonArray().add(record), user, remoteIP, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result().getLong(0))); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Saves multiple records to the specified table in a batch operation.

This method provides efficient batch insertion of multiple records. It creates the table if it doesn't exist, assigns IDs to records that don't have them, and performs all insertions in a single database transaction for better performance.

@param table The name of the table to save records to @param records Array of JSON records to save @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive array of generated record IDs or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService saveAll(String table, JsonArray records, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { var createdItems = new JsonArray(); // Create table if it doesn't exist createTable(table).onComplete(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { var recordIds = new JsonArray(); var tuples = new ArrayList(); // Prepare batch insert with ID assignment for (var index = 0; index < records.size(); index++) { var record = records.getJsonObject(index); // Set default entity type if not specified if (!record.containsKey(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE)) { record.put(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE, DBConstants.ENTITY_TYPE_USER); } // Generate ID if not provided var id = record.containsKey(GlobalConstants.ID) ? record.getLong(GlobalConstants.ID) : CommonUtil.newId(); tuples.add(Tuple.of(id, record.put(GlobalConstants.ID, id))); recordIds.add(id); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { CommonUtil.encryptSensitiveFields(record, cipherUtil); } createdItems.add(record); } // Execute batch insert if there are records to save if (!tuples.isEmpty()) { db.preparedQuery("INSERT INTO " + table + " (id, record) VALUES ($1, $2)") .executeBatch(tuples, asyncResult -> { try { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(recordIds)); // Sync with HA cluster if not system or observer operation if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_SYSTEM) && !remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { HAConstants.sync(table, createdItems, user, HAConstants.HASyncOperation.SAVE_ALL.getName(), BackupProfile.BackupProfileType.CONFIG_DB.getName()); } // Send audit notifications for each created item if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { for (var index = 0; index < createdItems.size(); index++) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.TRUE, null, null, createdItems.getJsonObject(index)); } } } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(asyncResult.cause())); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, asyncResult.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, exception.getMessage(), null, null); } }); } else { LOGGER.debug("request received to insert empty data"); handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(recordIds)); } } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, result.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, exception.getMessage(), null, null); } }); return this; } / Retrieves records from the specified table based on query criteria.

This method supports querying by any field in the JSON record or by ID. If no query is provided, it returns all records from the table. The method handles both single value and array value queries with IN clause support.

@param table The name of the table to query @param filter Query criteria as JsonObject with field name and value, or null for all records @param handler Handler to receive array of matching records or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService get(String table, JsonObject filter, Handler> handler) { var records = new JsonArray(); try { // Execute query with specific criteria if (filter != null && !filter.isEmpty()) { // Allow callers to skip decryption when not needed for performance //var skipDecrypt = filter.getBoolean("skip.decrypt", false); // Batch large array filters to 1000 items and merge results; otherwise use single query var fieldName = filter.getString(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME); var query = new StringBuilder(); // Build query based on field type (ID vs JSON field) query.append("SELECT record FROM ").append(table).append(" WHERE ") .append(fieldName.equalsIgnoreCase(GlobalConstants.ID) ? ID : String.format("record->>'%s'", fieldName)); var tuple = buildTuple(query, filter); db.preparedQuery(query.toString()) .execute(tuple, result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { // Extract records from result rows for (var row : result.result()) { var record = row.getJsonObject(RECORD); CommonUtil.decryptSensitiveFields(record, cipherUtil); records.add(record); } handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(records)); } else if (result.cause().getMessage().contains("does not exist")) { // Table doesn't exist, return empty result handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(records)); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); } else { // No query provided, return all records db.preparedQuery("SELECT record FROM " + table).execute(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { // Extract all records from result for (var row : result.result()) { var record = row.getJsonObject(RECORD); CommonUtil.decryptSensitiveFields(record, cipherUtil); records.add(record); } handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(records)); } else if (result.cause().getMessage().contains("does not exist")) { // Table doesn't exist, return empty result handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(records)); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } return this; } / Retrieves a single record by its ID. @param table The name of the table to query @param id The unique ID of the record to retrieve @param handler Handler to receive the record or empty JsonObject if not found @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService getById(String table, long id, Handler> handler) { getOneByQuery(table, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, GlobalConstants.ID).put(VALUE, id), result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result())); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Retrieves the first record matching the specified query criteria. @param table The name of the table to query @param filter Query criteria as JsonObject with field name and value @param handler Handler to receive the first matching record or empty JsonObject if none found @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService getOneByQuery(String table, JsonObject filter, Handler> handler) { get(table, filter, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { if (!result.result().isEmpty()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result().getJsonObject(0))); } else { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(new JsonObject())); } } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Retrieves any single record from the specified table.

This method returns the first record found in the table without any specific ordering. Useful for getting a sample record or when only one record is expected to exist.

@param table The name of the table to query @param handler Handler to receive a single record or empty JsonObject if table is empty @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService getOne(String table, Handler> handler) { db.query("SELECT FROM " + table + " LIMIT 1") .execute(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { var iterator = result.result().iterator(); if (iterator.hasNext()) { var item = iterator.next().getJsonObject(RECORD); CommonUtil.decryptSensitiveFields(item, cipherUtil); handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(item)); } else { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(new JsonObject())); } } else if (result.cause().getMessage().contains("does not exist")) { // Table doesn't exist, return empty record handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(new JsonObject())); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); return this; } / Retrieves all records from the specified table. @param table The name of the table to query @param handler Handler to receive array of all records in the table @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService getAll(String table, Handler> handler) { get(table, null, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result())); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Deletes records from the specified table based on query criteria.

This method delegates to deleteAll for consistency. System entities are protected from deletion to maintain data integrity.

@param table The name of the table to delete from @param filter Query criteria to identify records to delete @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive array of deleted record IDs or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService delete(String table, JsonObject filter, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { deleteAll(table, filter, user, remoteIP, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result())); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Deletes all records matching the specified query criteria.

This method performs a bulk delete operation with protection for system entities. It returns the deleted records and performs HA synchronization and audit logging. System entities (marked with ENTITY_TYPE_SYSTEM) are automatically excluded from deletion.

@param table The name of the table to delete from @param filter Query criteria to identify records to delete @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive array of deleted record IDs or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService deleteAll(String table, JsonObject filter, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { try { var items = new JsonArray(); var records = new JsonArray(); var query = new StringBuilder(); // Build delete query with system entity protection query.append("DELETE FROM ").append(table).append(" WHERE ").append(filter.getString(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME).equalsIgnoreCase(GlobalConstants.ID) ? "id" : String.format("record->>'%s' != '%s' AND record->>'%s'", DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE, DBConstants.ENTITY_TYPE_SYSTEM, filter.getString(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME))); var tuple = buildTuple(query, filter); query.append(" RETURNING "); db.preparedQuery(query.toString()) .execute(tuple, result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { // Collect deleted records and their IDs for (var row : result.result()) { items.add(row.getJsonObject(RECORD)); records.add(row.getLong(ID)); } // Sync with HA cluster if not system or observer operation if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_SYSTEM) && !remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { HAConstants.sync(table, filter, null, user, remoteIP, HAConstants.HASyncOperation.DELETE.getName(), BackupProfile.BackupProfileType.CONFIG_DB.getName()); } // Send audit notifications for each deleted item if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_DELETE, table, Boolean.TRUE, null, null, items.getJsonObject(index)); } } handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(records)); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_DELETE, table, Boolean.TRUE, result.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } return this; } / Drops the specified table completely from the database.

This method checks if the table exists before attempting to drop it. It performs HA synchronization and audit logging for the drop operation. Use with caution as this operation is irreversible.

@param table The name of the table to drop @param handler Handler to receive success confirmation or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService drop(String table, Handler> handler) { // Check if table exists before attempting to drop db.preparedQuery("SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_tables WHERE tablename = '" + table + "' )") .execute(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { var iterator = result.result().iterator(); if (iterator.hasNext() && iterator.next().getBoolean(0)) { // Table exists, proceed with drop db.preparedQuery("DROP TABLE " + table).execute(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { // Sync with HA cluster HAConstants.sync(table, null, null, SYSTEM_USER, SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS, HAConstants.HASyncOperation.DROP.getName(), BackupProfile.BackupProfileType.CONFIG_DB.getName()); // Send audit notification notify(SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS, SYSTEM_USER, REQUEST_DROP, table, Boolean.TRUE, null, null, null); handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture()); } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(asyncResult.cause())); } }); } else { // Table doesn't exist, consider operation successful handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture()); } } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); return this; } / Updates records in the specified table based on query criteria.

This method delegates to updateAll for consistency. It merges the provided record fields with existing records matching the query.

@param table The name of the table to update @param filter Query criteria to identify records to update @param record JSON object containing fields to update @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive array of updated record IDs or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService update(String table, JsonObject filter, JsonObject record, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { updateAll(table, filter, record, user, remoteIP, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result())); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } / Performs an upsert operation (insert or update) for a single record.

This method is strictly used during configuration database initialization. It inserts the record if it doesn't exist, or updates it if it does exist based on the record ID.

@param table The name of the table for the upsert operation @param record The JSON record to upsert @param user The username performing the operation for audit purposes @param remoteIP The remote IP address for audit and security tracking @param handler Handler to receive the record ID or error @return This service instance for method chaining / @Override public ConfigDBService upsert(String table, JsonObject record, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { this.upsertAll(table, new JsonArray().add(record), user, remoteIP, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(result.result().getLong(0))); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); } }); return this; } @Override public ConfigDBService upsertAll(String table, JsonArray records, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { var items = new JsonArray(); createTable(table).onComplete(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { var recordIds = new JsonArray(); if (records != null) { var tuples = new ArrayList(); for (var index = 0; index < records.size(); index++) { var record = records.getJsonObject(index); if (!record.containsKey(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE)) { record.put(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE, DBConstants.ENTITY_TYPE_USER); } var id = record.containsKey(GlobalConstants.ID) ? record.getLong(GlobalConstants.ID) : CommonUtil.newId(); tuples.add(Tuple.of(id, record.put(GlobalConstants.ID, id))); recordIds.add(id); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { CommonUtil.encryptSensitiveFields(record, cipherUtil); } items.add(record); } if (!tuples.isEmpty()) { db.preparedQuery("INSERT INTO " + table + " (id, record) VALUES ($1, $2) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET record = " + table + ".record || EXCLUDED.record") .executeBatch(tuples, asyncResult -> { try { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(recordIds)); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_SYSTEM) && !remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { HAConstants.sync(table, items, user, HAConstants.HASyncOperation.UPSERT.getName(), BackupProfile.BackupProfileType.CONFIG_DB.getName()); } if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.TRUE, null, null, items.getJsonObject(index)); } } } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(asyncResult.cause())); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, asyncResult.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); } else { LOGGER.debug("request received to insert empty data"); handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(recordIds)); } } else // this is the case when no entries exist, but we need to create the table (ex: agent.json) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(recordIds)); } } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(result.cause())); notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_CREATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, result.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); return this; } @Override public ConfigDBService updateAll(String table, JsonObject filter, JsonObject record, String user, String remoteIP, Handler> handler) { var oldItems = new ArrayList(); var records = new ArrayList(); this.get(table, filter, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { if (!result.result().isEmpty()) { try { var query = new StringBuilder(); var tuples = new ArrayList(); query.append("UPDATE ").append(table).append(" AS d SET record = v.record FROM ( VALUES ($1::BIGINT, $2::JSONB) ) AS v(id, record) WHERE d.id = v.id"); removeGarbageFields(item.getLong(ID), record, item.mergeIn(record), records, garbageFields); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { CommonUtil.encryptSensitiveFields(item, cipherUtil); } tuples.add(Tuple.of(item.getLong(ID), item)); } if (!tuples.isEmpty()) { db.preparedQuery(query.toString()) .executeBatch(tuples, asyncResult -> { try { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(new JsonArray(records))); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_SYSTEM) && !remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { HAConstants.sync(table, filter, record, user, remoteIP, HAConstants.HASyncOperation.UPDATE_ALL.getName(), BackupProfile.BackupProfileType.CONFIG_DB.getName()); } if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { for (var oldItem : oldItems) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_UPDATE, table, Boolean.TRUE, null, oldItem, record); } } } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(asyncResult.cause())); if (!remoteIP.equalsIgnoreCase(MOTADATA_OBSERVER)) { notify(remoteIP, user, REQUEST_UPDATE, table, Boolean.FALSE, asyncResult.cause().getMessage(), null, null); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } }); } else { LOGGER.debug("request received to update empty data"); handler.handle(Future.succeededFuture(new JsonArray(records))); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(exception)); } } else { var cause = "no result for query " + filter.encode(); LOGGER.warn(cause); handler.handle(Future.failedFuture(cause)); var records = new ArrayList(); this.get(table, filter, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { if (!result.result().isEmpty()) { try { LOGGER.debug("request received to update all multiple values for table " + table + "Size of the result :" + result.result().size()); var query = new StringBuilder(); var tuples = new ArrayList(); query.append("UPDATE ").append(table).append(" AS d SET record = v.record FROM ( VALUES ($1::BIGINT, $2::JSONB) ) AS v(id, record) WHERE d.id = v.id"); var items = result.result(); for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { var item = items.getJsonObject(index); oldItems.add(item.copy()); var garbageFields = (JsonArray) record.remove(DBConstants.GARBAGE_FIELDS); question: What does the VisualizationConstants class do?
answer:
This class defines constants, enums, and utility methods used throughout the visualization system.

VisualizationConstants serves as a central repository for:

  • String constants for visualization parameters and properties
  • Enumeration types for visualization categories, data sources, and result types
  • Utility methods for processing visualization data
  • Functions for packing and unpacking visualization results
  • Methods for filtering and qualifying entities for visualization

This class is used by all components in the visualization package to ensure consistent naming, data processing, and result formatting across the system.

The class contains several inner enum types that define specific aspects of visualizations:

  • {@link VisualizationJoinType} - Defines how data from different sources is joined
  • {@link VisualizationGrouping} - Defines grouping options for visualization data
  • {@link VisualizationDataSource} - Defines available data sources for visualizations
  • {@link VisualizationCategory} - Defines categories of visualizations
  • {@link VisualizationResultType} - Defines types of visualization results
  • {@link VisualizationTimeline} - Defines time ranges for visualizations

  • Handling configuration change notifications within the local system

  • Registering and configuring event sources
  • Managing flow sampling rates for network monitoring
  • Coordinating configuration changes across the system

  • Object additions, updates, and deletions
  • Metric additions, updates, and deletions

  • Runbook assignments

question: Show the pattern for: How does RemoteEventRouter.route() work?
answer:
Routes events to the most suitable event processor using a load balancing algorithm.

This method implements the core load balancing logic for distributing events across available event processors. It:

1. Evaluates all qualified event processors for the given event 2. Calculates a "frequency" score for each processor based on: - Current pending events - Historical latency - Available idle workers 3. Selects the processor with the lowest frequency score (least loaded) 4. Stores remaining processors for potential failover 5. Updates tracking maps and sends the event to the selected processor

If no qualified processors are available, the event is aborted with an appropriate error. @param event The event to be routed, containing event type, ID, and other metadata @param message The original message context (for reply handling, can be null)

question: What does the RemoteEventReceiver class do?
answer:
The RemoteEventReceiver class subscribes to events from remote event senders using ZeroMQ's SUB socket.

This class is responsible for:

  • Connecting to remote event senders and subscribing to specific topics
  • Filtering messages by topic based on bootstrap type (APP, AGENT, COLLECTOR, MANAGER)
  • Receiving and processing messages in a dedicated thread
  • Forwarding received messages to local handlers via the Vert.x event bus
  • Managing high-water marks to control message buffering
  • Handling connection lifecycle and error recovery

The RemoteEventReceiver connects to a specified host and port, and subscribes to topics based on the bootstrap type. It receives messages in a dedicated thread to avoid blocking the main event loop, then routes them to appropriate handlers within the system. Example usage: 

   // Create and deploy a RemoteEventReceiver   RemoteEventReceiver receiver = new RemoteEventReceiver(5555, "sender-host");   vertx.deployVerticle(receiver);     // Set up a handler for received events   vertx.eventBus().consumer("EVENT_APP", message -> {       JsonObject event = (JsonObject) message.body();       System.out.println("Received event: " + event);       // Process the event   });

question: How does MetricPoller.for() work?
answer:
A Vert.x verticle responsible for polling metrics from monitored systems and devices.

The MetricPoller class is a central component of the monitoring system that:

1. Manages worker pools for different types of metric polling: - Regular metrics (SNMP, WMI, etc.) - Availability/ping checks - Network service (port) checks

2. Schedules and executes metric polling operations based on: - Metric category (Network, Server, Database, etc.) - Metric type (regular, availability, network service) - Timeout requirements - Batch processing capabilities

3. Implements load balancing and resource management: - Tracks idle workers across different categories - Distributes polling tasks based on worker availability - Handles metric queuing and prioritization - Implements auto-scaling of worker pools when needed

4. Processes polling results and sends them to appropriate event bus addresses

The class uses Vert.x's event-driven, non-blocking architecture to efficiently handle large numbers of concurrent polling operations with minimal resource usage. / public class MetricPoller extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger instance for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(MetricPoller.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NMS, "Metric Poller"); / Worker executors for availability/ping checks / private final List availabilityWorkerExecutors = new ArrayList<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each metric category / private final Map idleWorkersByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each metric worker executor / private final Map idleMetricWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each availability worker executor / private final Map idleAvailabilityWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each network service worker executor / private final Map idleNetworkServiceWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Queued metrics organized by category and timeout value type / private final Map>> metricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Queued batch metrics organized by category and timeout value type / private final Map>> batchMetricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Counts of discarded metrics by category (due to overload or duplicates) / private final Map discardedMetricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Queued availability metrics organized by packet count / private final Map> pendingAvailabilityMetrics = new LinkedHashMap<>(); / Queued network service metrics / private final List pendingNetworkServiceMetrics = new ArrayList<>(); / Tracks duplicate metrics to avoid redundant polling operations / private final Map> duplicateMetrics = new HashMap<>(); / Current timeout value type for each metric category (used for round-robin scheduling) / private final Map metricTimeoutValueTypesByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Total count of idle metric workers across all executors / private final AtomicInteger idleMetricWorkers = new AtomicInteger(); / Total count of idle availability workers across all executors / private int idleAvailabilityWorkers; / Total count of idle network service workers across all executors / private int idleNetworkServiceWorkers = MotadataConfigUtil.getNetworkServiceWorkers() MotadataConfigUtil.getWorkers(); / Initializes the MetricPoller verticle and starts all polling operations.

This method: 1. Creates worker executor pools for different types of metric polling 2. Sets up worker allocation for different metric categories 3. Registers event bus consumers for handling metric polling requests and stats 4. Starts periodic timers for scheduling different types of metric polling: - Regular metrics (every 1000ms) - Availability/ping checks (every 500ms) - Network service checks (every 100ms)

question: What does the ZMQServer class do?
answer:
ZeroMQ (ZMQ) server implementation for the Motadata transport layer.

This class provides a ZeroMQ-based transport server that supports multiple socket modes for different messaging patterns. It implements the {@link TransportServer} interface to provide a standardized transport abstraction layer for server-side operations.

The server supports different ZeroMQ socket patterns:

  • PUB (Sender): Publishes messages to multiple SUB receivers
  • PULL: Receives messages from multiple PUSH clients in a round-robin fashion
  • PUSH: Sends messages to PULL sockets in a load-balanced manner

Key features:

  • Configurable High Water Mark (HWM) for message queuing and flow control
  • TCP keep-alive support for connection reliability
  • Automatic handling of slow receivers (XPUB_NODROP)
  • Thread-safe message handling with atomic operations
  • Integration with Vert.x event bus for message routing
  • Support for both binding and connecting modes

Configuration example:

{@code   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put("SOCKET_MODE", "PUB")       .put("HOST", "localhost")       .put("PORT", 5555)       .put("EVENT_TYPE", "remote.events");     ZMQServer server = new ZMQServer(config);   server.bind().onSuccess(v -> {       // Server is ready to accept connections       server.send("topic", "Hello World".getBytes());   });   }

Thread Safety: This class is thread-safe for concurrent access to its public methods. However, the underlying ZMQ socket operations are performed in dedicated threads.

@author Motadata Engineering Team @version 1.0 @since 1.0 @see TransportServer @see ZMQClient

question: How does TraceDatastore.send() work?
answer:
The primary responsibilities of the class include:

  • Listening for and responding to events regarding the state of the datastore (e.g., up or down).
  • Loading and closing event files based on the status and duration of the datastore being up or down.
  • Managing event retention and initiating retention operations based on retention policies.
  • Sending events to the datastore (including in High Availability (HA) setups) for persistent storage.
The class uses Vert.x's event bus to send and receive messages regarding the state and actions of the datastore. It utilizes the {@link DatastoreEngine} for event storage and processing and interacts with other components such as event processors, retention triggers, and HA sync mechanisms. Key features:
  • Responds to event "pings" that indicate whether the datastore is up or down, and adjusts the state of the event engine accordingly.
  • Tracks the duration that the datastore has been down and takes appropriate actions after a certain threshold (e.g., 30 minutes), such as closing event files from memory.
  • Handles retention operations by listening for retention triggers and executing retention logic based on configuration.
  • Supports High Availability (HA) environments, sending events either to a local datastore or to a primary datastore, depending on the mode.
  • Supports development mode for testing purposes by sending trace events to a separate test destination.
/ public class TraceDatastore extends AbstractVerticle { private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(TraceDatastore.class, MOTADATA_DATASTORE, "Trace Datastore"); private static final boolean STANDALONE_OR_PRIMARY = Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.STANDALONE.name()) || Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.PRIMARY.name()); private final AtomicLong duration = new AtomicLong(); private DatastoreEngine eventEngine; private boolean closed = false; private String uuid; private static final String PORT = CommonUtil.getString(MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceDatastoreWriterPort()); /

- Listens for the datastore "ping" events and updates status based on the event data. - If the datastore was down for over 30 minutes, it loads files and marks the datastore as active. - If the datastore is down for more than a configured time, it closes event files in memory. - Initializes the DatastoreEngine to handle event data and process events. - Listens for retention trigger events to run data retention logic. - Sets up consumers for "active" and "inactive" states of the datastore. @param promise A Promise for the start-up process. @throws Exception If an error occurs during the start-up process. / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { try { vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_DATASTORE_PING, message -> { var event = message.body(); try { if (uuid.equalsIgnoreCase(event.getString(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID))) { if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("updating status for %s : %s , event type : %s", event.getString(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID), event.getString(STATUS), config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); } if (event.getString(STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(STATUS_UP)) { if (event.getString(PORT,EMPTY_VALUE).equalsIgnoreCase(STATUS_UP)) { // if database gets up after being down more than 30 minutes then load all files if (closed) { vertx.eventBus().send(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE) + ".load", uuid); duration.set(0); closed = false; LOGGER.info(String.format("loading files for : %s ", config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); } vertx.eventBus().send(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE) + ".active", uuid); LOGGER.debug(String.format("active : type %s ", config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); } else { LOGGER.warn(String.format("port %s status is %s from datastore to APP : event type : %s ",PORT,event.getString(PORT,EMPTY_VALUE),config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); } } else { duration.getAndIncrement(); } // 180 10 = 1800 sec(30 min) . if datastore is down for more than 30 minutes // then close all event files object from in memory if (duration.get() > MotadataConfigUtil.getDatastoreFileCloseTimerSeconds()) { vertx.eventBus().send(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE) + ".close", uuid); closed = true; vertx.eventBus().send(EVENT_AUDIT_WRITE,new JsonObject().put(AUDIT_MODULE,SYSTEM_HEATH).put(AUDIT_OPERATION,VIEW) .put(AUDIT_MESSAGE,String.format(String.format(ENTITY_UPDATED, SYSTEM_HEATH) + GlobalConstants.NEW_LINE + new JsonObject().put("new.prop.value",new JsonObject() .mergeIn(RemoteEventProcessorConfigStore.getStore().flatItemsByValue(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, uuid, RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE, BootstrapType.DATASTORE.name()).getJsonObject(0)) .put(DATASTORE_UUID,uuid).put(DURATION,duration.get()) .put(EVENT_TYPE,config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE)) .put("datastore.file.close.timer.seconds",MotadataConfigUtil.getDatastoreFileCloseTimerSeconds()) .put(MANAGER_UUID,Bootstrap.getRegistrationId()).put(INSTALLATION_MODE,Bootstrap.getInstallationMode()) .put(TIME_STAMP, DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds()) .put(TIME,DateTimeUtil.getScheduledTimestamp(DateTimeUtil.currentMilliSeconds())) .put(MESSAGE, "Datastore file has been closed. Reason : Datastore is down for long time")).encodePrettily()))); duration.set(0); LOGGER.info(String.format("closing files for : %s ", config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_DATASTORE_RETENTION_TRIGGER, message -> DatastoreConstants.runRetention(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE), DateTimeUtil.currentMilliSeconds() - MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceDatastoreRetentionDays() 86400000L, LOGGER)); eventEngine = new DatastoreEngine() .setEventType(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE)) .setPersistEventOffset(true) .setEventQueueSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceDatastoreEngineQueueSize()) .setStatus(false) .setLogger(LOGGER) .setDynamicQueueSize(true) .setEventHandler(this::send) .start(vertx, promise); uuid = config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE).split(DOT_SEPARATOR_ESCAPE)[3]; vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(config().getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE) + ".inactive", message -> { LOGGER.debug(String.format("inactivate : type %s ", config().getString(EVENT_TYPE))); eventEngine.setStatus(false); }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception.getMessage()); } } / Sends the given event data to the datastore based on the current mode (Standalone/Primary or Secondary/HA).

- If the system is in Standalone or Primary mode, it sends the event to the datastore write endpoint. - If the system is in Secondary/HA mode, it sends the event to the remote event bus to sync with the primary datastore. - In both cases, the event is enriched with relevant metadata such as UUID and event topic. - In development mode, it sends the event to a test event bus for debugging purposes. @param event The event data to be sent to the datastore.

question: Show the pattern for: How does MetricPoller.setWorkers() work?
answer:
Initializes worker allocation for different metric categories.

This method: 1. Sets the total number of idle metric workers based on configuration 2. Allocates workers to each metric category based on their relative importance 3. Initializes data structures for tracking metrics by category and timeout value type

The worker allocation follows a percentage-based distribution defined in NMSConstants, where categories like Network and Server receive more workers than less critical categories like Cloud or Custom.

This method also initializes the metric queues for both regular and batch metrics, organizing them by category and timeout value type for efficient scheduling.

question: How does VisualizationMetricResponseProcessor.composeSubQueryResponse() work?
answer:
Composes and processes sub-query responses for visualization rendering.

This method is responsible for transforming raw metric data from database queries into visualization-ready format for different chart types (Histogram, Grid, etc.). It performs several key operations:

Core Functionality:

  • Data Transformation: Converts raw query results into visualization context
  • Aggregation Processing: Handles MIN, MAX, SUM, AVG aggregations for metrics
  • Entity Resolution: Resolves monitor IDs, groups, and tags for visualization grouping
  • Chart Context Creation: Builds appropriate visualization context based on category
  • Statistical Calculations: Computes grid statistics for histogram data

Supported Visualization Categories:

  • HISTOGRAM: Creates chart context with sorting and statistical aggregations
  • GRID: Creates grid context for tabular data display

Entity Grouping Support:

  • MONITOR: Groups by individual monitoring objects
  • GROUP: Groups by object groups
  • TAG: Groups by user-defined tags

Data Processing Flow:

  1. Extract visualization properties and sorting preferences
  2. Determine entity type (monitor/group/tag) from context
  3. Process raw data rows and calculate statistics if needed
  4. Resolve entity IDs and build entity collections
  5. Transform data points with aggregation support
  6. Build final visualization context and send to event bus

Error Handling:

If no data is found or processing fails, sends appropriate error messages to the visualization response event bus. @param queryId The unique identifier for the visualization query @param context The visualization context containing configuration, data sources, timeline, grouping preferences, and UI settings @param response The raw query response from the database containing result data @param category The visualization category (HISTOGRAM, GRID, etc.) @param metricColumns Metadata about metric columns including data types and categories @throws Exception If an error occurs during data processing or context creation @see VisualizationCategory @see VisualizationConstants.VisualizationGrouping @see DatastoreConstants.AggregationType

question: How does MetricPoller.send() work?
answer:
Dequeues availability metrics for processing.

This method: 1. Retrieves pending availability metrics from the queue 2. Groups them by IP address to avoid duplicate polling 3. Batches them for efficient processing (up to 200 metrics per worker) 4. Decrements the idle worker count for each batch created

The method handles duplicate IP addresses by: - Keeping only one metric for each unique IP in the batch - Storing duplicates in the duplicateMetrics map for later processing

It also implements a probing mechanism to avoid infinite loops when: - No more metrics are available - No more idle workers are available @return A list of maps, where each map contains IP-to-metric mappings for a batch / private List> dequeue() { var metrics = new ArrayList>(); var probes = 0; var batchSize = 200; //1 worker means 200 availability metrics... try { while (idleAvailabilityWorkers > 0 && probes < 5) // if probe is greater than 5 means metrics not present or worker not available { for (var pendingMetrics : pendingAvailabilityMetrics.values()) { if (idleAvailabilityWorkers > 0) { var iterator = pendingMetrics.iterator(); if (iterator.hasNext()) { var metric = new HashMap(); metrics.add(metric); var count = 0; while (count < batchSize && iterator.hasNext()) { var id = iterator.next(); if (MetricCacheStore.getStore().queuedMetric(id)) { var event = MetricCacheStore.getStore().dequeue(id); if (EventCacheStore.getStore().validItem(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID))) { count++; EventBusConstants.updateEvent(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID), String.format(InfoMessageConstants.EVENT_TRACKER_EVENT_QUALIFIED, DateTimeUtil.timestamp())); // if two same ip polls collides because of any reason than we will ping for any one & equivalent result will be sent if (metric.containsKey(event.getString(OBJECT_IP))) { duplicateMetrics.computeIfAbsent(event.getString(OBJECT_IP), value -> new ArrayList<>()); duplicateMetrics.get(event.getString(OBJECT_IP)).add(event); } else { metric.put(event.getString(OBJECT_IP), event); } } } else { abort(id); } iterator.remove(); } idleAvailabilityWorkers--; } else { probes++; } } else { probes++; } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } return metrics; } / Sends error information for multiple contexts.

This method iterates through a map of contexts and processes each one with the extract method, which formats the error information and sends it. After processing each context, it removes it from the map to free up memory and prevent duplicate processing.

The method determines the appropriate error message based on the error code: - For PROCESS_TIMEOUT errors: Uses the PROCESS_TIMED_OUT message - For other errors: Uses the INTERNAL_ERROR message @param contexts A map of target IPs to JsonObject contexts to process @param errorCode The error code to set for all contexts @param error The detailed error information (stack trace), can be null

EventPolicyInspector is the core component responsible for evaluating event policies and triggering appropriate actions based on the processed event data.

It receives pre-aggregated group statistics from EventPolicyInspector, evaluates them against defined policy conditions (e.g., threshold, range), and takes configured actions such as notifications, suppression, or runbook execution.

Additionally, it manages the lifecycle of policies — including scheduling, suppression windows, evaluation intervals, and interaction with other components like the visualization engine.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Receiving group statistics from EventPolicyAggregator
  • Evaluating policy conditions (sum, avg, count, range, etc.)
  • Triggering actions: notifications, sound alerts, runbooks, etc.
  • Handling policy lifecycle events: add, update, delete, disable
  • Supporting scheduled evaluations and integrating with visualization context

This class represents the policy execution and decision-making engine. / public class EventPolicyInspector extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger instance for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(EventPolicyInspector.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_POLICY, "Event Policy Inspector"); / Delivery options for event bus communications with 5-minute timeout / private static final DeliveryOptions DELIVERY_OPTIONS = new DeliveryOptions().setSendTimeout(300000L); / Interval in seconds for periodic policy inspection / private static final int INTERVAL_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getEventPolicyInspectionTimerSeconds(); / Maximum number of top groups to process in group-based policies / private static final int TOP_N_GROUPS = MotadataConfigUtil.getEventPolicyTopNGroups(); / Local host name/address for event source identification / private static final String LOCAL_HOST = CommonUtil.getIPAddress(); / Map of policy IDs to their context information / private final Map policies = new HashMap<>(64); / Storage for event column mappings / private final JsonObject eventColumns = new JsonObject(); / Set of policy IDs with disabled action triggers / private final Set disabledPolicyActionTriggers = new HashSet<>(); / Map of policy IDs to their grouping counter columns (for policies with group-by clauses) / private final Map groupingCounters = new HashMap<>(); / Reusable JsonObject for record construction / private final JsonObject record = new JsonObject(); / Collection of records for policy evaluation results / private final JsonArray records = new JsonArray(); / Map of policy IDs to their evaluation intervals / private final Map evaluatedPolicies = new HashMap<>(); / StringBuilder for efficient string operations with initial capacity / private final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder(1024); / Cache for frequently constructed field keys / private final Map cacheFields = new HashMap<>(32); / Map of policy IDs to their group statistics / private final Map policyGroupStats = new HashMap<>(); private final Map policyEvaluationTicks = new HashMap<>(64); / Set of mapper names / private Set mappers; / Initializes the EventPolicyInspector verticle.

It loads existing policies from the store and prepares them for evaluation. @param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done @throws Exception If an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { var policies = EventPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItems(); if (policies != null) { for (var index = 0; index < policies.size(); index++) { try { var policy = policies.getJsonObject(index); if (!policy.containsKey(POLICY_ARCHIVED) || policy.getString(POLICY_ARCHIVED).equalsIgnoreCase(NO)) { add(policy); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); //if log or flow license is enabled, then only we will inspect log, flow and APM policy. if(LicenseUtil.FLOW_ENABLED.get() || LicenseUtil.LOG_ENABLED.get() || LicenseUtil.APM_ENABLED.get()) { vertx.setPeriodic(INTERVAL_SECONDS 1000L, timer -> { for (var entry : evaluatedPolicies.entrySet()) { try { var policyId = entry.getKey(); var values = entry.getValue(); // times[0] = countdown, times[1] = original values[0] -= INTERVAL_SECONDS; if (values[0] <= 0) { if(CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug("Requesting to get data from instances, for Policy: " + this.policies.get(policyId).getString(POLICY_NAME) + " : " + policyEvaluationTicks.get(policyId) + " evaluated-polices: " + Arrays.toString(evaluatedPolicies.get(policyId))); disabledPolicyActionTriggers.remove(event.getLong(ID)); init(item, item.getLong(ID)); } } case UPDATE_POLICY -> { var item = EventPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItem(event.getLong(ID)); if (item != null) { this.policies.put(item.getLong(ID), enrich(item)); init(item, item.getLong(ID)); } } case DELETE_POLICY -> { this.policies.remove(event.getLong(ID)); disabledPolicyActionTriggers.remove(event.getLong(ID)); clear(event.getLong(ID)); } case DISABLE_POLICY_ACTION_TRIGGER -> { disabledPolicyActionTriggers.remove(event.getLong(POLICY_ID)); } }); //fOR Testing only... vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_EVENT_POLICY_TEST, message -> fetch(message.body(), "test")); // for test case sendPolicies(); promise.complete(); } private void fetch(Long policyId, String type) { var policy = policies.get(policyId); var count = MotadataConfigUtil.getLogParsers(); var eventType = EVENT_LOG; if(policy.getString(POLICY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.FLOW.getName())) { count = MotadataConfigUtil.getFlowProcessors(); eventType = EVENT_FLOW; } else if (policy.getString(POLICY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.TRACE_ANALYTICS.getName())) { count = MotadataConfigUtil.getTraceProcessors(); eventType = PolicyType.TRACE_ANALYTICS.getName(); } else if (policy.getString(POLICY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(PolicyType.NETWORK_CONFIG.getName())) { count = MotadataConfigUtil.getConfigManagementResponseProcessorWorkers(); eventType = PolicyType.NETWORK_CONFIG.getName(); } var futures = new ArrayList>(); //for testing when type is not unknown we are fetching data from the test if(!UNKNOWN.equalsIgnoreCase(type)) { eventType = type; count = 1; } for(var index = 0; index < count; index++) { var promise = Promise.promise(); futures.add(promise.future()); vertx.eventBus().request(EVENT_EVENT_POLICY_AGGREGATOR_QUERY + DOT_SEPARATOR + eventType ,policyId,message -> { try { var item = message.result(); question: How does NetRouteStatusCalculator.appendBytes() work?
answer:
Calculates and tracks the status of network routes.

This class is responsible for monitoring the status of network routes, detecting status changes, and calculating metrics related to network route availability and performance. It processes status information from network route polling operations and stores the results for analysis and visualization.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Tracking network route status over time
  • Detecting and recording status changes (flaps)
  • Calculating duration metrics for different status states
  • Storing status information in the data store
  • Sending notifications about status changes

The calculator uses a buffer-based approach to efficiently store and update status information in the data store, minimizing the overhead of frequent updates. / public class NetRouteStatusCalculator extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(NetRouteStatusCalculator.class, MOTADATA_NETROUTE, "NetRoute Status Calculator"); / Array of availability metric types (seconds and percent) / private static final JsonArray AVAILABILITY_METRICS = new JsonArray().add("seconds").add("percent"); / Interval (in seconds) for flushing status flap durations to disk / private static final int STATUS_FLAP_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getStatusFlapDurationDumpTimerSeconds(); / Interval (in seconds) for flushing network route status information / private static final int STATUS_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getNetRouteStatusFlushTimerSeconds(); / StringBuilder for building strings efficiently / private final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder(0); / JsonObject to store duration information for network route statuses / private final JsonObject durations = new JsonObject(); / Flag indicating whether the durations have been updated / private final AtomicBoolean updated = new AtomicBoolean(); / Set of mapper names for column mapping / private Set mappers; / Flag indicating whether the data is dirty and needs to be saved / private boolean dirty = false; / Initializes the NetRouteStatusCalculator verticle.

This method sets up the status tracking system for network routes. It performs the following tasks:

  • Initializes the mappers set for column mapping
  • Loads existing status flap durations from disk if available
  • Sets up periodic timers for flushing status information to disk and the data store
  • Sets up event bus consumers for handling status change notifications
The method uses two main timers:
  • Status flap flush timer - Controls how often status flap durations are saved to disk
  • Path status flush timer - Controls how often network route status information is written to the data store
@param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done / @Override public void start(Promise promise) { mappers = new HashSet<>(); var file = new File(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAP_DURATIONS); if (file.exists()) { var buffer = vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(file.getPath()); if (buffer != null && buffer.getBytes().length > 0) { durations.mergeIn(new JsonObject(Buffer.buffer(CodecUtil.toBytes(buffer.getBytes())))); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s loaded from the backup file...", NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAP_DURATIONS)); } } else { vertx.fileSystem().createFileBlocking(file.getPath()); } var statusFlapFlushTimer = new AtomicInteger(STATUS_FLAP_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS); var pathStatusFlushTimer = new AtomicInteger(STATUS_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS); vertx.setPeriodic(10 1000L, timer -> { try { statusFlapFlushTimer.set(statusFlapFlushTimer.get() - 10); pathStatusFlushTimer.set(pathStatusFlushTimer.get() - 10); var timestamp = DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds(); for (var item : NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().getItems().entrySet()) { var object = NetRouteConfigStore.getStore().getItem(item.getKey(), false); if (object != null) { var id = CommonUtil.getString(item.getKey()); durations.getMap().putIfAbsent(id, 0); durations.put(id, durations.getInteger(id) + 10); if (pathStatusFlushTimer.get() <= 0) { var buffer = Buffer.buffer(); appendBytes(buffer, timestamp, NETROUTE_STATUS_DURATION_METRIC.getName(), item.getKey()); buffer.appendIntLE(EMPTY_VALUE.length()); buffer.appendString(EMPTY_VALUE); updateScalarBatch(METRIC, APIConstants.Entity.NETROUTE.getName().toLowerCase() + "." + item.getValue().toLowerCase() + TIME, NETROUTE_STATUS_DURATION_METRIC.getName(), buffer, true, true); updateScalarBatch(STATUS, item.getValue().toUpperCase(), NETROUTE_STATUS_DURATION_METRIC.getName(), buffer, false, false); updateScalarBatch(REASON, EMPTY_VALUE, NETROUTE_STATUS_DURATION_METRIC.getName(), buffer, false, false); updateScalarBatch(DURATION, CommonUtil.getString(STATUS_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS), NETROUTE_STATUS_DURATION_METRIC.getName(), buffer, false, false); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DATASTORE_WRITE + "." + DatastoreConstants.DatastoreCategory.AVAILABILITY.getName(), buffer.getBytes()); } } } if (statusFlapFlushTimer.get() <= 0) { if (!durations.isEmpty() || updated.get()) { vertx.fileSystem().writeFileBlocking(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAP_DURATIONS, Buffer.buffer(CodecUtil.compress(new JsonObject().mergeIn(durations).encode().getBytes()))); dirty = true; } NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().dump(); updated.set(false); statusFlapFlushTimer.set(STATUS_FLAP_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS); } if (pathStatusFlushTimer.get() <= 0) { pathStatusFlushTimer.set(STATUS_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION , message -> { try { var event = message.body(); if (EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.valueOf(event.getString(EventBusConstants.CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE)) == EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.DELETE_NETROUTE) { var id = event.getLong(ID); HAConstants.notifyObserver(new JsonObject().put(HAConstants.CACHE_NAME, NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAP_DURATIONS).put(RESULT, vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAP_DURATIONS))); } if (NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().dirty()) { NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().setDirty(false); HAConstants.notifyObserver(new JsonObject().put(HAConstants.CACHE_NAME, NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAPS).put(RESULT, vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + GlobalConstants.CONFIG_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_STATUS_FLAPS))); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); promise.complete(); } / Appends common header information to a buffer for data storage.

answer: Finds applicable policies for an object based on its groups and tags.       This method aggregates policies from different mapping sources to create a complete       set of policies that should be evaluated for the object, sorting them by creation time       to ensure that newer policies take precedence.             @param groups           The groups associated with the object       @param tags             The tags associated with the object       @param objectId         ID of the object to find policies for       @param policies         Map of all available policies       @param policiesByObject Map of policies assigned directly to objects       @param policiesByGroup  Map of policies assigned to groups       @param policiesByTag    Map of policies assigned to tags       @return A map of metrics to sets of policy IDs that should be evaluated      /     public static Map<String, LinkedHashSet<Long>> qualify(JsonArray groups, JsonArray tags, long objectId, long serviceId, Map<Long, JsonObject> policies, Map<Long, Map<String, List<Long>>> policiesByObject, Map<Long, Map<String, List<Long>>> policiesByGroup, Map<Long, Map<String, List<Long>>> policiesByTag, Map<Long, Map<String, List<Long>>> policiesByService)     {         var qualifiedPolicies = new HashMap<String, LinkedHashSet<Long>>();          var keys = new HashSet<String>();          policiesByObject.getOrDefault(objectId, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->         {             if (!policyIds.isEmpty())             {                 qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);                  if(policyIds.size() > 1)        // if multiple policy of same metric then add into keys and later sort/filter                 {                     keys.add(key);                 }             }         });          if (groups != null)         {             for (var index = 0; index < groups.size(); index++)             {                 var group = groups.getLong(index);                  policiesByGroup.getOrDefault(group, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->                 {                     if (!policyIds.isEmpty())                     {                         if (qualifiedPolicies.containsKey(key))                         {                             keys.add(key);                         }                         else                         {                             if(policyIds.size() > 1)            // if multiple policy of same metric then add into keys and later sort/filter                             {                                 keys.add(key);                             }                         }                          qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);                     }                 });             }         }          if (tags != null && !tags.isEmpty() && policiesByTag != null)         {             for (var index = 0; index < tags.size(); index++)             {                 var tag = tags.getLong(index);                  policiesByTag.getOrDefault(tag, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->                 {                     if (!policyIds.isEmpty())                     {                         if (qualifiedPolicies.containsKey(key))                         {                             keys.add(key);                         }                         else                         {                             if(policyIds.size() > 1)                    // if multiple policy of same metric then add into keys and later sort/filter                             {                                 keys.add(key);                             }                         }                          qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);                     }                 });             }         }          if (policiesByService != null)         {             policiesByService.getOrDefault(serviceId, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->             {                 if (!policyIds.isEmpty())                 {                     qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);                      if (policyIds.size() > 1)                     {                         keys.add(key);                     }                 }             });         }          if (!keys.isEmpty())         {             keys.forEach(key ->             {                 var values = qualifiedPolicies.get(key);                 }             });         }          return qualifiedPolicies;     }      /       Populates email and SMS recipient sets from a JSON array of recipients.
