question: Show the pattern for: How does LocalEventRouter.LocalEventRouter() work?
answer:
The LocalEventRouter class routes events to appropriate handlers based on event type and routing key.

This class is responsible for:

  • Deploying multiple event router instances for load balancing
  • Routing events to the appropriate router based on a routing key
  • Supporting different routing strategies (dynamic, round-robin)
  • Managing the lifecycle of router instances (add/remove)
  • Handling event queries and bulk operations
  • Persisting router state for recovery after restart
  • Providing statistics about event processing when enabled

The LocalEventRouter supports multiple routing strategies:

  • Dynamic Routing: Time-based routing that routes to different handlers based on time. This is useful for cases like datastore-writer where data is written minute-wise, so events from the same minute are sent to the same datastore writer.
  • Round Robin Routing: Event-based routing that distributes events evenly across all available handlers. This is useful when multiple events arrive simultaneously and need to be processed in parallel.

The router maintains a mapping between routing keys and router instances, ensuring that events with the same routing key are consistently routed to the same handler. It also supports dynamic scaling by allowing router instances to be added or removed at runtime.

Example usage: 

   // Create and deploy a LocalEventRouter with 4 instances   LocalEventRouter router = new LocalEventRouter(       "metric-events",           // Event type       "deviceId",                // Routing key       4,                         // Number of router instances       "com.mindarray.MetricHandler", // Handler class       false,                     // Non-blocking       true,                      // Enable stats       EventRouter.DYNAMIC        // Routing strategy   );     vertx.deployVerticle(router);     // Send an event to be routed   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put("deviceId", "device-123")       .put("metric", "cpu-usage")       .put("value", 75.5)       .put("timestamp", System.currentTimeMillis());     vertx.eventBus().send("metric-events", event);
/ public class LocalEventRouter extends AbstractVerticle { private static final String PROBE = "probe"; private static final String DEPLOYED_ROUTERS = "deployed.routers"; private static final DeliveryOptions DELIVERY_OPTIONS = new DeliveryOptions(); private static final Map CONTEXTS = Map.ofEntries(Map.entry(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AVAILABILITY_CORRELATION, new JsonObject().put(APIConstants.ENTITY_TABLE, DBConstants.TBL_CORRELATION).put(PROBE, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, AIOpsConstants.CORRELATION_TYPE).put(VALUE, AIOpsConstants.CorrelationType.AVAILABILITY.getName()))), Map.entry(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DEPENDENCY + "." + AIOpsConstants.DependencyType.LOCAL_DOMAIN.getName(), new JsonObject().put(APIConstants.ENTITY_TABLE, DBConstants.TBL_DEPENDENCY).put(PROBE, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, AIOpsConstants.DEPENDENCY_TYPE).put(VALUE, AIOpsConstants.DependencyType.LOCAL_DOMAIN.getName()))), Map.entry(EventBusConstants.EVENT_DEPENDENCY + "." + AIOpsConstants.DependencyType.CROSS_DOMAIN.getName(), new JsonObject().put(APIConstants.ENTITY_TABLE, DBConstants.TBL_DEPENDENCY).put(PROBE, new JsonObject().put(DBConstants.FIELD_NAME, AIOpsConstants.DEPENDENCY_TYPE).put(VALUE, AIOpsConstants.DependencyType.CROSS_DOMAIN.getName())))); private final Logger logger; //router... private final Map routes = new HashMap<>(); private final Map routers = new HashMap<>(); private final String eventType; private final String routingKey; private final boolean blocking; private final String clazz; private final Map deployedRouters = new HashMap<>(); private final boolean enableStats; private int eventRouters; private long events = 0L; private boolean streaming = false; private int routerType = NOT_AVAILABLE; private int probes = 0; private int assignedRouters = 0; public LocalEventRouter(String eventType, String routingKey, int eventRouters, String clazz, boolean blocking) { this.eventType = eventType; this.routingKey = routingKey; this.eventRouters = eventRouters >= 0 ? eventRouters : 1; this.clazz = clazz; this.logger = new Logger(LocalEventRouter.class, MOTADATA_EVENT_BUS, String.format("Local Event Router:(%s)", eventType)); this.enableStats = false; this.blocking = blocking; } public LocalEventRouter(String eventType, String routingKey, int eventRouters, String clazz, boolean blocking, boolean enableStats) { this.eventType = eventType; this.routingKey = routingKey; this.eventRouters = eventRouters >= 0 ? eventRouters : 1; this.clazz = clazz; this.blocking = blocking; this.enableStats = enableStats; this.logger = new Logger(LocalEventRouter.class, MOTADATA_EVENT_BUS, String.format("Local Event Router:(%s)", eventType)); } / Dynamic Routing: time(second) based routing -- route to the other handler at every second -- use-case: In datastore-writer we write data minute wise so when same minute data is received it will send to same datastore so only one writer creates that file Round Robin Routing: event based routing -- route to the other handler at every event -- use-case: pmacct sends all aggregated events to AIOps at the same time. if dynamic routing is applied all events will be handled by single vertical. hence using round-robin routing

question: Show the pattern for: How does ManagerResponseProcessor.publishEvent() work?

The ManagerResponseProcessor class is responsible for processing responses and events from various system components in the Motadata application.

This class handles different types of events including:

  • Backup and restore operations
  • Application lifecycle events (start, stop, restart)
  • Upgrade events
  • State change notifications
  • Manager upgrade events

The ManagerResponseProcessor maintains communication with remote event processors through periodic heartbeats and processes their responses. It also manages notifications for various system events and updates the status of operations in the system.

This class extends Vert.x's AbstractVerticle to leverage the event-driven, non-blocking programming model for handling concurrent operations efficiently. / public class ManagerResponseProcessor extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(ManagerResponseProcessor.class, MOTADATA_APP_MANAGER, "Manager Response Processor"); / Flag indicating if a write operation is pending / private boolean writePending = false; / Flag indicating if the data has been modified and needs to be saved / private boolean dirty = false; private final String REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_MAIL_NOTIFICATION_TIMER_SECONDS = "remote.event.processor.mail.notification.timer.seconds"; / Initializes the ManagerResponseProcessor verticle.

This method sets up periodic tasks for:

  • Writing pending data to storage
  • Sending heartbeats to remote event processors
  • Maintaining connections with datastores

It also registers event bus handlers for processing various types of events including backup, start, stop, restart, delete, upgrade, state change, and manager upgrade events. @param promise the promise to complete when initialization is done @throws Exception if an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { vertx.setPeriodic(30000, timer -> { write(); for (var remoteEventProcessor : RemoteEventProcessorConfigStore.getStore().flatMap().values()) { if (!remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(BootstrapType.DATASTORE.name())) { // send heartbeat to collector publishEvent(new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TOPIC).put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID)) .put(ID, remoteEventProcessor.getLong(ID)).put(EVENT_TYPE, EVENT_REMOTE_PROCESSOR_HEARTBEAT)); } else { // this DATASTORE_CONNECTION_TOPIC separate topic is for sending heartbeat/keep alive to 'all' datastore Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EVENT_PUBLICATION_DATASTORE_WRITE, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, DATASTORE_CONNECTION_ALIVE_TOPIC) .put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TOPIC, DATASTORE_OPERATION_TOPIC) .put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID)) .put(EVENT_CONTEXT, Buffer.buffer().appendByte(DatastoreConstants.OperationType.CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE.getName()).getBytes())); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EVENT_PUBLICATION_DATASTORE_READ, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, DATASTORE_CONNECTION_ALIVE_TOPIC) .put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TOPIC, DATASTORE_QUERY_TOPIC) .put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID)) .put(EVENT_CONTEXT, Buffer.buffer().appendByte(DatastoreConstants.OperationType.CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE.getName()).getBytes())); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EVENT_PUBLICATION_DATASTORE_WRITE, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, DATASTORE_BROKER_OPERATION_TOPIC) .put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID)) .put(EVENT_CONTEXT, Buffer.buffer().appendByte(DatastoreConstants.OperationType.CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE.getName()).getBytes())); if (CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug(String.format("keep alive request send to datastore : uuid %s and mode %s ", remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID), remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_INSTALLATION_MODE))); } } // send heartbeat to collector manager publishEvent(new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, EventBusConstants.MOTADATA_MANAGER_TOPIC).put(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID)) .put(ID, remoteEventProcessor.getLong(ID)).put(EVENT_TYPE, EVENT_MOTADATA_MANAGER_HEARTBEAT).put(SYSTEM_BOOTSTRAP_TYPE, remoteEventProcessor.getString(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE))); } }); update(); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION , message -> { var event = message.body(); if (EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.valueOf(event.getString(EventBusConstants.CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE)) == ChangeNotificationType.UPDATE_CACHE && dirty) { dirty = false; HAConstants.notifyObserver(new JsonObject().put(HAConstants.CACHE_NAME, "remote-event-processor-cache").put(RESULT, vertx.fileSystem().readFileBlocking(REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_CACHE_PATH))); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_MANAGER_RESPONSE_PROCESSOR, message -> { var event = message.body(); var systemBootstrapType = event.getString(SYSTEM_BOOTSTRAP_TYPE); // based on Bootstrap Type will process the response if (systemBootstrapType.equalsIgnoreCase(BootstrapType.APP.name())) { switch (event.getString(EVENT_TYPE)) { case EVENT_DATABASE_BACKUP -> processBackupEvent(event); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("received agent manager event %s", CommonUtil.removeSensitiveFields(response, true))); } switch (response.getString(EVENT_TYPE)) { case EVENT_AGENT_START -> processStartEvent(response); case EVENT_AGENT_DISABLE, EVENT_AGENT_ENABLE -> { var asyncPromise = Promise.promise(); if (STATUS_SUCCEED.equalsIgnoreCase(response.getString(STATUS)) && AgentConfigStore.getStore().getItem(response.getLong(ID)) == null) { var agentID = AgentConfigStore.getStore().getAgentId(event.getString(AGENT_UUID)); question: What does the CustomJob class do?
answer:
The CustomJob class is responsible for executing user-defined jobs in the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and handles the execution of various types of scheduled jobs based on their configuration. It processes different job types differently, dispatching them to the appropriate handlers via the event bus.

The job execution flow is as follows:

  1. Retrieve job context from the job execution context
  2. Load the scheduler configuration from the store
  3. Prepare the job context by merging configuration and job data
  4. Check if the job is enabled and not already running
  5. Execute the job based on its type

The class handles various job types including database compaction, license quota reset, system log retention, discovery, maintenance, runbook execution, topology, rediscovery, policy operations, reports, database backups, and compliance policy checks.

question: What does the SlackNotification class do?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Slack notifications.

This class handles Slack notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Slack Web API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Slack channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Slack service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Slack API requests
  • Automatic image upload and attachment for messages with images

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Checks if image upload is required and handles file upload if needed
  6. Sends HTTP requests to the Slack API for each channel
  7. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  8. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding
  • {@code imageAttached} (optional): Boolean flag indicating if image upload is required

The message content is provided as a complete Slack Block Kit JSON template from the PolicyEngine, with all variables already substituted. This class simply adds the channel information and sends the message to the Slack API.

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is experiencing issues.

question: How does HTTPServer.HTTPServer() work?
answer:
HttpServer is a Vert.x-based HTTP server implementation with direct WebSocket transport support. It uses the webSocketHandler approach where any HTTP request can be upgraded to WebSocket, eliminating the need for clients to open local HTTP servers.

This implementation follows the direct WebSocket approach where:

  • Server accepts WebSocket upgrades on any HTTP request
  • Clients connect using WebSocket protocol directly

Processing events using worker executors 4. Managing worker allocation for different request types 5. Handling batch processing for supported plugin types 6. Sending responses back through the event bus

Similar to eventsByPluginEngineRequest but specifically for requests that support batching. / private final Map> batchEventsByPluginEngineRequest = new EnumMap<>(PluginEngineConstants.PluginEngineRequest.class); / Worker executor for processing plugin events asynchronously. Used to determine when to disable the timer to save CPU cycles. / private int eventProbes; / Flag indicating whether the periodic timer for processing events is active. STATUS_TIME_OUT : STATUS_FAIL; for (var target : targets) { if (eventIdsByTarget.containsKey(CommonUtil.getString(target))) { for (var id : eventIdsByTarget.get(CommonUtil.getString(target))) { send(contexts.remove(id).put(STATUS, status).put(ERROR_CODE, errorCode)); } } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); // Compliance requests need a longer timeout (600 seconds by default) case COMPLIANCE -> WorkerUtil.spawnWorker(contexts, context, eventIds, context.getInteger(TIMEOUT, 600), // Use 600 seconds as default timeout for compliance false, pluginEngine, System.currentTimeMillis(), true); // Runbook requests use either the specified timeout or the configured batch timeout case RUNBOOK -> WorkerUtil.spawnWorker(contexts, context, eventIds, // Use context timeout if provided, otherwise use the configured batch timeout context.containsKey(TIMEOUT) ? context.getInteger(TIMEOUT, 60) : MotadataConfigUtil.getPluginEngineProbeBatchTimeoutSeconds(), false, pluginEngine, System.currentTimeMillis(), true); // Default handling for other request types default -> WorkerUtil.spawnWorker(contexts, context, eventIds, // GO engine uses batch timeout, PYTHON engine uses context timeout or 60 seconds pluginEngine == PluginEngineConstants.PluginEngine.GO ? question: What does the DatastoreRetentionJob class do?

The DatastoreRetentionJob class is responsible for managing data retention in the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and performs two main tasks:

question: Show the pattern for: How does SlackNotification.OK() work?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Slack notifications.

This class handles Slack notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Slack Web API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Slack channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Slack service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Slack API requests
  • Automatic image upload and attachment for messages with images

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Checks if image upload is required and handles file upload if needed
  6. Sends HTTP requests to the Slack API for each channel
  7. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  8. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding
  • {@code imageAttached} (optional): Boolean flag indicating if image upload is required

The message content is provided as a complete Slack Block Kit JSON template from the PolicyEngine, with all variables already substituted. This class simply adds the channel information and sends the message to the Slack API.

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is experiencing issues. / public class SlackNotification extends Notification { / Logger for Slack notification operations / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(SlackNotification.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NOTIFICATION, "Slack Notification"); / Circuit breaker to handle Slack service failures.

The circuit breaker:

  • Opens after 5 consecutive failures
  • Considers a request failed if it takes more than 30 seconds
  • Stays open for 60 seconds before attempting to reset
  • Tracks failures over a 30-minute rolling window
  • Calls the fallback handler when open
/ private final CircuitBreaker circuitBreaker = CircuitBreaker.create("slack-service-circuit-breaker", Bootstrap.vertx(), new CircuitBreakerOptions() .setMaxFailures(5) // number of failure before opening the circuit .setTimeout(30000) // consider a failure if the operation does not succeed in time .setFallbackOnFailure(true) // do we call the fallback on failure .setResetTimeout(60000) // time spent in open state before attempting to re-try .setFailuresRollingWindow(TimeUnit.MINUTES.toMillis(30)) ).openHandler(handler -> LOGGER.warn(ErrorMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_FAILED)).closeHandler(handler -> LOGGER.info(InfoMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_RESTORED)).fallback(handler -> handler.initCause(new Exception(ErrorMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_FAILED))); / Processes and sends Slack notifications based on the provided event data.

This method orchestrates the entire Slack notification workflow:

  • Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the store
  • Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  • Processes each channel in parallel using futures
  • Applies severity-based color coding to message content
  • Handles image upload if required by the message payload
  • Sends messages to Slack API with proper authentication
  • Tracks successful deliveries and handles failures

The method uses circuit breaker protection to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is unavailable or experiencing issues. @param event A JsonObject containing the Slack notification parameters:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS} - JSON array of channel IDs
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT} - Message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} - Severity level for color coding (optional)
  • {@code imageAttached} - Boolean flag for image upload (optional)
@return A Promise that resolves to a JsonObject containing the result of the Slack notification attempt with the following structure:
  • {@link GlobalConstants#STATUS} - Status of the operation ({@link GlobalConstants#STATUS_SUCCEED} or {@link GlobalConstants#STATUS_FAIL})
  • {@link GlobalConstants#ERROR_CODE} - Error code indicating success or failure type
  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#RECIPIENTS} - List of successfully notified channel IDs
  • {@link GlobalConstants#MESSAGE} - Error message if operation failed
  • {@link GlobalConstants#ERROR} - Stack trace if operation failed
@throws Exception If any unexpected error occurs during notification processing / @Override public Promise notify(JsonObject event) { var promise = Promise.promise(); // Retrieve Slack integration configuration from the store var slack = IntegrationConfigStore.getStore().getItemsByValue( Integration.INTEGRATION_TYPE, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationType.SLACK.getName() ).getJsonObject(0); // Execute the Slack sending logic with circuit breaker protection circuitBreaker.execute(future -> { try { var futures = new ArrayList>(); var recipients = new ArrayList(); if (event.containsKey(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS) && event.getJsonArray(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS) != null && slack != null) { var channels = event.getJsonArray(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS); // Process each channel in parallel channels.forEach(channel -> { var result = Promise.promise(); futures.add(result.future()); var item = IntegrationProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(Long.parseLong(channel.toString())); if (item != null) { // Get the channel context and build the Slack API URL var context = item.getJsonObject(IntegrationProfile.INTEGRATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT); var url = slack.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getString(GlobalConstants.TARGET, EMPTY_VALUE) + SLACK_MESSAGE_END_POINT; var credentialProfile = CredentialProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(slack.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getLong(IntegrationProfile.INTEGRATION_CREDENTIAL_PROFILE)); var content = EMPTY_VALUE; if (event.containsKey(SEVERITY) && !event.getString(SEVERITY).isEmpty()) { content = new StringSubstitutor(new JsonObject().put(SEVERITY_COLOR, SlackColorCode.valueOf((event.getString(SEVERITY).toUpperCase())).getColorCode()).getMap()).replace(event.getString(Notification.CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT)); question: Show the pattern for: How does DependencyMapper.isValid() work?
answer:
Validates a single row from the dependency mapper CSV import.

Checks performed:

  • Row must have exactly 5 columns.
  • The link layer value (row[4]) must be either ENABLE or DISABLE (case-insensitive).
  • All columns except the child interface (row[3]) must be non-null and non-empty.
  • Parent and child devices (row[0] and row[2]) must exist in the object store.
  • Parent device must be of NETWORK category.
  • If a child interface is provided, both parent and child interfaces must be valid for their respective devices.
Logs warnings for invalid data and returns false if any check fails. @param row The CSV row as a String array. @return true if the row is valid, false otherwise.

question: What does the LocalEventRouter class do?
answer:
The LocalEventRouter class routes events to appropriate handlers based on event type and routing key.

This class is responsible for:

  • Deploying multiple event router instances for load balancing
  • Routing events to the appropriate router based on a routing key
  • Supporting different routing strategies (dynamic, round-robin)
  • Managing the lifecycle of router instances (add/remove)
  • Handling event queries and bulk operations
  • Persisting router state for recovery after restart
  • Providing statistics about event processing when enabled

The LocalEventRouter supports multiple routing strategies:

  • Dynamic Routing: Time-based routing that routes to different handlers based on time. This is useful for cases like datastore-writer where data is written minute-wise, so events from the same minute are sent to the same datastore writer.
  • Round Robin Routing: Event-based routing that distributes events evenly across all available handlers. This is useful when multiple events arrive simultaneously and need to be processed in parallel.

The router maintains a mapping between routing keys and router instances, ensuring that events with the same routing key are consistently routed to the same handler. It also supports dynamic scaling by allowing router instances to be added or removed at runtime.

Example usage: 

   // Create and deploy a LocalEventRouter with 4 instances   LocalEventRouter router = new LocalEventRouter(       "metric-events",           // Event type       "deviceId",                // Routing key       4,                         // Number of router instances       "com.mindarray.MetricHandler", // Handler class       false,                     // Non-blocking       true,                      // Enable stats       EventRouter.DYNAMIC        // Routing strategy   );     vertx.deployVerticle(router);     // Send an event to be routed   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put("deviceId", "device-123")       .put("metric", "cpu-usage")       .put("value", 75.5)       .put("timestamp", System.currentTimeMillis());     vertx.eventBus().send("metric-events", event);

This class is responsible for handling the responses received from network route polling operations. It processes the raw data, calculates metrics, builds the network topology, and stores the results for further analysis and visualization.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Processing raw network route polling responses
  • Calculating latency and other metrics between network hops
  • Building a hierarchical representation of the network topology
  • Enriching the data with additional information
  • Storing the processed data for analysis and visualization
  • Sending events and notifications about network route status

The processor handles complex network path analysis, including handling of timeouts, packet loss calculation, and link transit probability computation. / public class NetRouteResponseProcessor extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(NetRouteResponseProcessor.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NETROUTE, "NetRoute Response Processor"); / Delivery options for event bus messages / private static final DeliveryOptions DELIVERY_OPTIONS = new DeliveryOptions(); / Set of metric names to extract from network route polling results / private static final Set METRICS = Set.of(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName(), NetRouteMetrics.RECEIVED.getName(), NETROUTE_HOP_CONNECTED_LINK, SEVERITIES); / TreeSet to store and sort severity levels / private final TreeSet severities = new TreeSet<>(); / Initializes the NetRouteResponseProcessor verticle.

This method sets up an event bus consumer to listen for network route polling responses. When a response is received, it processes the data, calculates metrics, and stores the results for further analysis and visualization. @param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done / @Override public void start(Promise promise) { // Set up an event bus consumer to listen for network route polling responses vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_NETROUTE_POLL_RESPONSE, message -> { var event = message.body(); try { // Log debug information if enabled if (CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug(String.format("NetRoute %s result received at %s with status : %s ", event.getString(NETROUTE_NAME), event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP), event.getString(STATUS))); } // Process successful responses that contain result data if (event.containsKey(STATUS) && event.getString(STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(STATUS_SUCCEED) && event.containsKey(RESULT)) { var id = event.getLong(ID); // Update the timestamp of the last successful poll NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().updateMetricPollTimestamp(id, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)); var result = event.getJsonObject(RESULT); LOGGER.info(String.format("NetRoute %s result status : %s ", event.getString(NETROUTE_NAME), result.getString(STATUS))); // Update the network route status in the cache store NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().updateItem(id, result.getString(STATUS, STATUS_UNKNOWN), event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds())); // Create a response object with the source-to-destination result var response = new JsonObject().put(NetRouteConstants.NetRouteType.SOURCE_TO_DESTINATION.getName(), new JsonArray().add(result)); // Processing the NetRoute response. // Since we probe multiple times, the result contains an array of hop lists, // where each hop has metrics such as latency (best, worst, avg), packet loss, NAT, MPLS, etc. // we have to calculate metrics for the 'links' between consecutive hops, rather than individual hops. // For example, if the hops are (A, B, C, D), we compute and store metrics for the links (A → B), (B → C), and (C → D). // Latency for a link is computed as: `Latency(B) - Latency(A)`. If a node times out, its latency and packet loss are considered as 0. // Also overlapping links from multiple results are merged to avoid duplicates link and required for policy inspection. var items = result.getJsonArray(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_ROUTES); result.remove(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_ROUTES); if (items != null && !items.isEmpty()) { var source = ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItemByAgentId(event.getLong(NETROUTE_SOURCE)).getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP); var target = event.getJsonArray(NETROUTE_DESTINATION_IP).getString(0); var objects = new HashSet(); var connections = new HashMap(); // for overlapped links. (unique link -> metric) var links = new JsonArray(); var hopInfo = NetRouteCacheStore.getStore().getHopRegistryInfo(id); for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { var hops = items.getJsonObject(index).getJsonArray(NetRouteMetrics.HOPS.getName()); if (hops != null) { var sourceHop = new JsonObject().put(NETROUTE_SOURCE, source); for (var hopIndex = 0; hopIndex < hops.size(); hopIndex++) { try { var destinationHop = hops.getJsonObject(hopIndex); var hosts = !destinationHop.getJsonArray(NetRouteMetrics.HOSTS.getName()).isEmpty() ? destinationHop.getJsonArray(NetRouteMetrics.HOSTS.getName()).getJsonObject(0) : null; var destinationIP = hosts != null ? hosts.getString(NetRouteMetrics.IP.getName()) : NETROUTE_TIMEOUT_HOP + DASH_SEPARATOR + destinationHop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.TTL.getName()); var unreachable = destinationIP.contains(NETROUTE_TIMEOUT_HOP); var sourceIP = sourceHop.getString(NETROUTE_SOURCE); // first hop which will be our motadata machine, so just create the link , no need to calculate latency if (!sourceIP.equalsIgnoreCase(source)) { if (!unreachable) { calculateLatency(destinationHop, sourceHop); } else { // if last node which is actual destination, is timeout node, then we'll update the last link and metric based on the over all (Source-to-destination) result // this might happen if destination server is not responding to UDP packet. if (hopIndex == hops.size() - 1) { destinationHop.put(NetRouteMetrics.BEST.getName(), CommonUtil.getFloat(result.getFloat(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_MIN_LATENCY))) .put(NetRouteMetrics.WORST.getName(), CommonUtil.getFloat(result.getFloat(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_MAX_LATENCY))).put(NetRouteMetrics.AVG.getName(), CommonUtil.getFloat(result.getFloat(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_LATENCY))) .put(NetRouteMetrics.LOST_PACKET_PERCENT.getName(), CommonUtil.getFloat(result.getFloat(NetRouteConstants.NETROUTE_PACKET_LOST_PERCENT))).put(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName(), sourceHop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())).put(NetRouteMetrics.RECEIVED.getName(), sourceHop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())) .put(NetRouteMetrics.HOSTS.getName(), new JsonArray().add(new JsonObject().put(NetRouteMetrics.IP.getName(), target).put(NetRouteMetrics.HOSTNAME.getName(), target))); destinationIP = target; unreachable = false; calculateLatency(destinationHop, sourceHop); } else { destinationHop.put(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName(), sourceHop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())).put(NetRouteMetrics.RECEIVED.getName(), sourceHop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())); if (!connections.containsKey(connection)) { links.add(link); } enrich(link, destinationHop); link.put(NETROUTE_SOURCE, sourceIP).put(NetRoute.NETROUTE_DESTINATION, unreachable ? } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_NETROUTE_POLICY_RESPONSE, message -> { var event = message.body(); try { LOGGER.info(String.format("NetRoute %s policy result received at %s ", event.getString(NETROUTE_NAME), event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP))); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("NetRoute policy response received: %s", event.encode())); } var result = event.getJsonObject(RESULT); var object = result.getJsonArray(NetRouteConstants.NetRouteType.SOURCE_TO_DESTINATION.getName()).getJsonObject(0); severities.clear(); if (object.containsKey(SEVERITIES) && !object.getJsonArray(SEVERITIES).isEmpty()) { severities.addAll(object.getJsonArray(SEVERITIES).getList()); object.put(SEVERITY, severities.last().ordinal()); // store the highest severity } else { object.put(SEVERITY, Severity.UNKNOWN.ordinal()); } object.put(STATUS, StatusType.valueOf(object.getString(STATUS).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)).ordinal()); object.remove(SEVERITIES); // send to db send(object.put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(NETROUTE_ID, event.getLong(NETROUTE_ID)), true); var source = ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItemByAgentId(event.getLong(NETROUTE_SOURCE)).getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP); if (result.getJsonArray(NetRouteConstants.NetRouteType.HOP_BY_HOP.getName()) != null) { // build a recursive result from raw entries to store in DB var hops = result.getJsonArray(NetRouteConstants.NetRouteType.HOP_BY_HOP.getName()); var connections = new HashMap>(); // ttl -> (source -> [destinations]) //Source IP and the packet sent to this source var nodes = new HashMap(); var links = new HashMap(); for (var index = 0; index < hops.size(); index++) { var hop = hops.getJsonObject(index); var ttl = hop.getInteger(NETROUTE_HOP_TTL); // ttl can be considered as level connections.computeIfAbsent(ttl, value -> new HashMap<>()); connections.get(ttl).computeIfAbsent(hop.getString(NETROUTE_SOURCE), value -> new JsonArray()).add(hop); nodes.put(hop.getString(NETROUTE_DESTINATION_IP), nodes.getOrDefault(hop.getString(NETROUTE_DESTINATION_IP), 0) + hop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())); var link = hop.getString(NETROUTE_SOURCE) + DASH_SEPARATOR + hop.getString(NETROUTE_DESTINATION_IP); links.put(link, links.getOrDefault(link, 0) + hop.getInteger(NetRouteMetrics.SENT.getName())); } nodes.put(source, event.getInteger(NETROUTE_MAX_PROBE_ATTEMPTS) event.getInteger(NETROUTE_MAX_PROBE_PACKETS));                                             }                                              var start = Math.max(cycleStartTime, correctionStartTime);                                              var end = Math.min(cycleEndTime, correctionEndTime); hour < 23; hour++)                                                 {                                                     if (!hours.contains(hour))                                                     {                                                         timestamps.add(new long[]{date.atTime(hour, 0).atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toEpochSecond()                                                                 , date.atTime(hour + 1, 0).atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toEpochSecond()});                                                 }                                             }                                         }                                     }                                     else                                     {                                         LOGGER.warn("business hour is not configured");                                     }                                 }                                 case REPEATING ->                                 {                                     var repeatEnds = context.getString(CorrectionProfile.REPEAT_ENDS); question: How does TagRule.validateBulkCreate() work?
answer:
Extracts and separates static and dynamic tags from the request body.

This method expects the request body (from {@code routingContext.body().asJsonObject()}) to contain a JsonArray under the key {@link #TAG_RULE_TAGS}. Each element in that array may be:

  • a static tag (stored as-is), or
  • a dynamic tag following the {@code PATTERN} (example: {@code host:{object.host}}).
Behavior:
  1. Iterate over the incoming tags.
  2. If a tag matches {@code PATTERN}, extract the left-hand side as the dynamic tag key and the inner token as the dynamic tag value and add to {@code TAG_RULE_DYNAMIC_TAGS}.
  3. Otherwise collect the tag as a static tag and resolve it using {@link TagConfigStore#getStore()#addItems(JsonArray, String, String)} which returns the stored representation (hash/ids) for static tags.
  4. Update the original request body in-place with resolved static tags and dynamic tags.
The returned JsonObject is the same object as the request body (modified in-place) and is annotated as non-null. @param routingContext Vert.x routing context containing the request body @return modified request body JsonObject with {@code TAG_RULE_TAGS} and {@code TAG_RULE_DYNAMIC_TAGS} populated / @NotNull private static JsonObject setTags(RoutingContext routingContext) { var dynamicTags = new JsonObject(); var staticTags = new JsonArray(); var requestBody = routingContext.body().asJsonObject(); var tags = requestBody.getJsonArray(TAG_RULE_TAGS); if (!tags.isEmpty()) { for (var index = 0; index < tags.size(); index++) { var tag = tags.getString(index); var matcher = PATTERN.matcher(tag); if (matcher.find() && matcher.groupCount() == 2) { if (matcher.group(1) != null && !matcher.group(1).isEmpty() && matcher.group(2) != null && !matcher.group(2).isEmpty()) { dynamicTags.put(matcher.group(1), matcher.group(2)); } } else { staticTags.add(tag); } } } requestBody.put(TAG_RULE_TAGS, TagConfigStore.getStore().addItems(staticTags, Tag.TagType.OBJECT.getName(), DBConstants.ENTITY_TYPE_USER)); requestBody.put(TAG_RULE_DYNAMIC_TAGS, dynamicTags); return requestBody; } / Will return the count of entities tagged by the rule. / @Override protected Future getEntityCountPreHook(JsonObject response) { var future = Promise.promise(); try { var items = TagRuleConfigStore.getStore().getItems(); var futures = new ArrayList>(); for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++) { var item = items.getJsonObject(index); var promise = Promise.promise(); futures.add(promise.future()); Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().request(EVENT_TAG_RULE_RUN, item.put(TagRule.TAG_RULE_TEST, true), reply -> { try { if (reply.succeeded()) { var result = reply.result().body(); } } else { promise.complete(item.getLong(ID) + HASH_SEPARATOR + 0); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.complete(item.getLong(ID) + HASH_SEPARATOR + 0); } }); } Future.all(futures).onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { var result = new JsonObject(); for (var item : asyncResult.result().list()) { var tokens = CommonUtil.getString(item).split(HASH_SEPARATOR); result.put(tokens[0], CommonUtil.getInteger(tokens[1])); } future.complete(result); } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); } }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } return future.future(); } @Override protected Future afterGetAll(JsonArray items, RoutingContext routingContext) { try { for (var index = 0;   • If no unique checks are required, the handler chain proceeds immediately by calling {@code routingContext.next()}. Otherwise it waits for all uniqueness checks to complete and sends any error response returned by those checks or proceeds on success.

question: How does StreamingBroadcaster.broadcast() work?
answer:
The StreamingBroadcaster is responsible for broadcasting streaming data to connected clients.

This class works in conjunction with the StreamingEngine to:

  • Manage streaming sessions for different types of streaming data
  • Apply filtering logic to streaming data based on client preferences
  • Enrich streaming data with additional context information
  • Broadcast streaming data to the appropriate clients
  • Enforce limits on the number of concurrent streaming sessions

The StreamingBroadcaster supports multiple types of streaming (defined in {@link StreamingEngine.StreamingType}) and maintains separate session maps for each type to ensure proper isolation and management.

This class is implemented as a Vert.x verticle and uses the Vert.x event bus for communication with other components in the system. / public class StreamingBroadcaster extends AbstractVerticle { / Maximum number of concurrent streaming sessions allowed per streaming type / public static final int MAX_STREAMING_SESSIONS = 5; / Logger instance for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(StreamingBroadcaster.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_STREAMING, "Streaming Broadcaster"); / Cache of column mappings for metric data / private final JsonObject columns = new JsonObject(); / Map of active streaming sessions organized by streaming type / private final Map> sessionsByType = new EnumMap<>(StreamingEngine.StreamingType.class); // stream type -> uuid -> object id / Initializes the StreamingBroadcaster verticle and sets up event bus handlers.

This method:

  • Initializes session maps for each streaming type
  • Sets up event bus handlers for column mapper updates
  • Sets up event bus handlers for streaming events (start, stop, broadcast)
  • Loads initial column mappings for metric data
@param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done @throws Exception If an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { // Initialize session maps for each streaming type for (var type : StreamingEngine.StreamingType.values()) { sessionsByType.put(type, new HashMap<>()); } // Set up handler for column mapper updates vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_COLUMN_MAPPER_UPDATE, message -> { try { var event = message.body(); // Update column mappings when metric columns are updated if (event.getString(CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.UPDATE_METRIC_COLUMN.name())) { update(event.getString(DatastoreConstants.MAPPER).split(GlobalConstants.COLUMN_SEPARATOR, -1)); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); // Set up handler for streaming events vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(config().getString(EVENT_TYPE), message -> { try { var event = message.body(); var eventType = event.getString(EVENT_TYPE); // Route events to appropriate handlers based on event type if (eventType.equalsIgnoreCase(EVENT_STREAMING_START)) { start(event); // Start a new streaming session } else if (eventType.equalsIgnoreCase(EVENT_STREAMING_STOP)) { stop(event); // Stop an existing streaming session } else if (eventType.equalsIgnoreCase(EVENT_STREAMING_BROADCAST)) { broadcast(event); // Broadcast data to streaming clients } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); // Load initial column mappings for metric data Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().request(EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_COLUMN_MAPPER_QUERY, "", reply -> { if (reply.succeeded()) { columns.mergeIn(reply.result().body().getJsonObject(DatastoreConstants.METRIC_COLUMNS)); } }); // Initialization complete promise.complete(); } / Broadcasts streaming data to clients based on their session configuration and filtering preferences.

This method:

  • Determines the streaming type from the context
  • Retrieves the session configuration for the client
  • Applies filtering logic based on the streaming type and session configuration
  • Enriches the data with additional context if needed
  • Publishes the data to the client if it passes all filters
@param context The streaming data context to broadcast

question: Show the pattern for: How does MotadataAppManager.stop() work?
answer:
Switches over configuration settings and restarts relevant verticles.

This method performs a configuration change and verticle restart sequence:

  • Updates the configuration file with new parameters from the event
  • Reloads the configuration settings
  • Undeploys the RemoteEventReceiver verticle
  • Undeploys the RemoteEventSender verticle
  • Redeploys both verticles with the new configuration

This method is primarily used during high availability operations or when system configuration changes require component restarts. @param event the JSON object containing configuration changes to apply @return a Future that completes when the switchover operation is finished / private Future switchOver(JsonObject event) { // First change configuration settings, then restart verticles to apply changes var promise = Promise.promise(); try { // Locate the configuration file var file = new File(CURRENT_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR + CONFIG_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR + MOTADATA_CONFIG_FILE); // Read the current configuration var configs = new JsonObject(FileUtils.readFileToString(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); // Merge the new configuration changes from the event // This preserves existing settings while updating only those specified in the event configs.mergeIn(event.getJsonObject(EVENT_CONFIG_CHANGE, new JsonObject())); // Write the updated configuration back to the file // Using encodePrettily() for human-readable JSON formatting vertx.fileSystem().writeFileBlocking(file.getPath(), Buffer.buffer(configs.encodePrettily().getBytes())); // Reload the configuration settings into memory loadConfigs(MOTADATA_CONFIG_FILE, false); // Log the configuration changes LOGGER.info(String.format("file %s updated with new parameters %s", file.getName(), event.getJsonObject(EVENT_CONFIG_CHANGE))); LOGGER.info(String.format("new updated motadata json %s ", MotadataConfigUtil.getConfigs().encode())); // Begin the verticle restart sequence // Step 1: Undeploy the RemoteEventReceiver verticle Bootstrap.undeployVerticle(RemoteEventReceiver.class.getSimpleName()).onComplete(result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { // Step 2: Undeploy the RemoteEventSender verticle // The verticle name includes the port number for uniqueness Bootstrap.undeployVerticle( RemoteEventSender.class.getSimpleName() + " " + MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventSenderPort() ).onComplete(response -> { if (response.succeeded()) { // Step 3: Redeploy the RemoteEventSender with the new configuration Bootstrap.startEngine(new RemoteEventSender(new JsonObject().put(TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL, MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventProtocol()).put(SOCKET_MODE, EventBusConstants.SocketMode.PUSH) .put(PORT,MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventSenderPort()).put(HOST,CommonUtil.getRemoteEventSender())), RemoteEventSender.class.getSimpleName() + " " + MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventSenderPort(), null) .onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { // Step 4: Redeploy the RemoteEventReceiver with the new configuration Bootstrap.startEngine(new RemoteEventReceiver(new JsonObject().put(TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL, MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventProtocol()).put(SOCKET_MODE, SocketMode.SUB) .put(PORT,MotadataConfigUtil.getMotadataManagerEventReceiverPort()).put(HOST,CommonUtil.getRemoteEventReceiver()).put(EVENT_TYPE,EVENT_PUBLICATION)), RemoteEventReceiver.class.getSimpleName(), null) .onComplete(asyncResponse -> { if (asyncResponse.succeeded()) { // All verticles redeployed successfully promise.complete(); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s %s restart successfully", RemoteEventReceiver.class.getSimpleName(), RemoteEventSender.class.getSimpleName())); } else { // RemoteEventReceiver redeployment failed LOGGER.warn(asyncResponse.cause()); // Note: We don't fail the promise here, which means the operation // is considered partially successful even if this step fails } }); } else { // RemoteEventSender redeployment failed LOGGER.warn(asyncResult.cause()); // Note: We don't fail the promise here, which means the operation // is considered partially successful even if this step fails } }); } else { // RemoteEventSender undeployment failed LOGGER.error(response.cause()); // Note: We don't fail the promise here, which means the operation // is considered partially successful even if this step fails } }); } else { // RemoteEventReceiver undeployment failed LOGGER.error(result.cause()); // Note: We don't fail the promise here, which means the operation // is considered partially successful even if this step fails } }); } catch (Exception exception) { // Log any exceptions during the configuration update LOGGER.error(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Recursively stops a series of system components.

The method completes the provided promise when all components have been processed, or if an error occurs during the stopping process. @param types an array of component types to stop @param promise the promise to complete when all components are stopped @param index the current index in the types array

String.valueOf(event.remove(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING + ConfigConstants.FILE)) : EMPTY_VALUE; var startupConfigFileContent = event.containsKey(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.STARTUP + ConfigConstants.FILE) ? String.valueOf(event.remove(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.STARTUP + ConfigConstants.FILE)) : EMPTY_VALUE; updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_LAST_BACKUP_STATUS, STATUS_SUCCEED) .put(Configuration.CONFIG_LAST_ACTION_STATUS, STATUS_SUCCEED); // Check the conflict between startup with running var value = detectConflicts(runningConfigFileContent, startupConfigFileContent); updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_WITH_STARTUP_CONFLICT_STATUS, value); if (ConfigConflictStatus.CONFLICT.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(value)) { policyEngine.processEvent(getPolicyEvent(event).put(PolicyEvaluationType.CONFIG_CONFLICT.getName(), PolicyConflictType.STARTUP_RUNNING_CONFLICT.getName()) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_VERSION, updatedConfig.getInteger(CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_STARTUP_CURRENT_VERSION, 0)) .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION, updatedConfig.getInteger(CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_CURRENT_VERSION, 0)) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_BACKUP_TYPE, ConfigFileType.STARTUP.getName()) // 0 - Startup enum .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_BACKUP_TYPE, ConfigFileType.RUNNING.getName())); // 1 - Running enum } updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_WITH_BASELINE_CONFLICT_STATUS, ConfigConstants.ConfigConflictStatus.NA.getName()); // Check the conflict between baseline with running if (event.containsKey(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_BASELINE_VERSION) && event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_BASELINE_VERSION) != DUMMY_NUMERIC_VALUE) { var baselineRunningFileContent = CodecUtil.toString(ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().getRecentBaselineBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT))); value = detectConflicts(runningConfigFileContent, baselineRunningFileContent); updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_WITH_BASELINE_CONFLICT_STATUS, value); if (value.equalsIgnoreCase(ConfigConflictStatus.CONFLICT.getName())) { // Send notification when conflict detected between running and baseline policyEngine.processEvent(getPolicyEvent(event).put(PolicyEvaluationType.CONFIG_CONFLICT.getName(), PolicyConflictType.BASELINE_RUNNING_CONFLICT.getName()) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_VERSION, event.getInteger(CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_BASELINE_VERSION, 0)) .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION, updatedConfig.getInteger(CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_CURRENT_VERSION, 0)) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_BACKUP_TYPE, ConfigFileType.BASELINE.getName()) // 2 - Baseline enum .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_BACKUP_TYPE, ConfigFileType.RUNNING.getName())); // 1 - Running enum } } } else { LOGGER.warn(result.cause().getMessage()); updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_LAST_ACTION_ERROR_MESSAGE, result.cause().getMessage()); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); LOGGER.warn(String.format("Failed to process operation : %s, object : %s, reason : %s", operation, event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP), exception.getMessage())); updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_LAST_ACTION_ERROR_MESSAGE, "Internal Error while processing."); } finally { promise.complete(updatedConfig); } }); } else if (operation.equals(ConfigConstants.ConfigOperation.INFO)) { updatedConfig.put(Configuration.CONFIG_INFO, event.getJsonObject(RESULT)); promise.complete(updatedConfig); } else { promise.complete(updatedConfig); } return promise.future(); } / Method responsible to save backup result -> Method will read the backup file content to store it in the config backup result collection -> For NONE Protocol, We will get the file content in the event So, We will write that content to file first so that it will be used while sending it to FTP, TFTP etc.. @param event Backup Event @param updatedConfig Update Config Object @param type Backup Type @param result Result @return Future to indicate whether backup is success or failed. / private Future readBackupFile(JsonObject event, JsonObject updatedConfig, ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType type, JsonObject result) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { if (result.containsKey(type.getName() + ConfigConstants.CONFIG_STATUS) && result.getString(type.getName() + ConfigConstants.CONFIG_STATUS).equals(STATUS_SUCCEED)) { var backupFile = new File(ConfigConstants.CONFIG_MANAGEMENT_DEFAULT_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR + result.getString(type.getName())); var content = result.containsKey(type.getName() + ConfigConstants.BACKUP_FILE_CONTENT) ? CommonUtil.getString(result.remove(type.getName() + ConfigConstants.BACKUP_FILE_CONTENT)) : EMPTY_VALUE; // Writing backup content to file when file transfer protocol is "NONE". Latter on, it will be used while uploading to FTP,SFTP ... if (event.containsKey(ConfigConstants.FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL) && event.getString(ConfigConstants.FILE_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL).equals(StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.NONE.getName()) && !content.isEmpty()) { FileUtils.writeStringToFile(backupFile, content, StandardCharsets.UTF_8); } if (backupFile.exists()) { var key = type.equals(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING) ? Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_CURRENT_VERSION : Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_STARTUP_CURRENT_VERSION; var version = event.getInteger(key, ConfigConstants.BACKUP_FILE_DEFAULT_VERSION); var valid = true; event.put(type + ConfigConstants.FILE, content); var previousFileContent = type.equals(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING) ? ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().getRecentRunningBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT)) != null ? CodecUtil.toString(ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().getRecentRunningBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT))) : EMPTY_VALUE : ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().getRecentStartUpBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT)) != null ? CodecUtil.toString(ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().getRecentStartUpBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT))) : EMPTY_VALUE; if (!previousFileContent.isEmpty() && StringUtils.compare(content, previousFileContent) != 0) { ++version; // Add conflict detection for changed config files and process the event policyEngine.processEvent(getPolicyEvent(event).put(PolicyEvaluationType.CONFIG_CONFLICT.getName(), type.equals(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING) ? PolicyConflictType.RUNNING_CONFLICT.getName() : PolicyConflictType.STARTUP_CONFLICT.getName()) .put(CONFIG_ACTION_EXECUTION_OUTPUT, event.getString(CONFIG_OPERATION_OUTPUT, EMPTY_VALUE)) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_VERSION, version - 1) .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION, version) .put(CONFIG_PREVIOUS_BACKUP_TYPE, type.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(ConfigBackupType.RUNNING.getName()) ? ConfigFileType.RUNNING.getName() : ConfigFileType.STARTUP.getName()) // 1 - Running enum, 0 - Startup enum .put(CONFIG_CURRENT_BACKUP_TYPE, type.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(ConfigBackupType.RUNNING.getName()) ? ConfigFileType.RUNNING.getName() : ConfigFileType.STARTUP.getName())); } else { valid = previousFileContent.isEmpty(); } updatedConfig.put(key, version); if (valid) { // Will be saving min. version which will be updated by retention job in the future. UI will only show version between min and current version in drop down if (version == ConfigConstants.BACKUP_FILE_DEFAULT_VERSION) { updatedConfig.put(type.equals(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING) ? Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_RUNNING_MIN_VERSION : Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_STARTUP_MIN_VERSION, ConfigConstants.BACKUP_FILE_DEFAULT_VERSION); } var item = new JsonObject().put(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT, event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT)) .put(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_CONTENT, CodecUtil.compress(content)) .put(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_TIME, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TIMESTAMP)); //Storing config backup result .. Bootstrap.configDBService().save(String.format(type.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(ConfigConstants.ConfigBackupType.RUNNING.getName()) ? DBConstants.TBL_CONFIG_RUNNING_RESULT : DBConstants.TBL_CONFIG_STARTUP_RESULT, version), item, event.containsKey(User.USER_NAME) ? event.getString(User.USER_NAME) : SYSTEM_USER, event.containsKey(REMOTE_ADDRESS) ? event.getString(REMOTE_ADDRESS) : SYSTEM_REMOTE_ADDRESS, asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { LOGGER.info(String.format("Configuration result added successfully for file type : %s , for the object : %s ", type.getName(), event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_NAME))); try { switch (type) { case RUNNING -> ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().updateRecentRunningBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT), item.getBinary(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_CONTENT)); case STARTUP -> ConfigurationCacheStore.getStore().updateRecentStartUpBackupRecords(event.getInteger(Configuration.CONFIG_OBJECT), item.getBinary(Configuration.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_CONTENT)); } if (event.containsKey(Configuration.CONFIG_STORAGE_PROFILE) && StorageProfileConfigStore.getStore().existItem(event.getLong(Configuration.CONFIG_STORAGE_PROFILE))) { save(StorageProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(event.getLong(Configuration.CONFIG_STORAGE_PROFILE)) .put(DEST_FILE_NAME, backupFile.getName()) .put(SRC_FILE_PATH, backupFile.getAbsolutePath())); } else { if (CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug(String.format("Deleting file : %s, object : %s", type.getName(), event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_NAME))); } FileUtils.deleteQuietly(backupFile); } promise.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception.getMessage()); } } else { promise.fail(String.format(ErrorMessageConstants.CONFIG_RESULT_ADD_FAILED, type.getName(), event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_NAME), asyncResult.cause().getMessage())); } }); } else { if (CommonUtil.debugEnabled()) { LOGGER.debug(String.format("Deleting file : %s, object : %s as no changes detected", type.getName(), event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_NAME))); } FileUtils.deleteQuietly(backupFile); promise.complete(); } } else { promise.fail(String.format(ErrorMessageConstants.CONFIG_BACKUP_FILE_NOT_FOUND, result.getString(type.getName()), event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP))); } } else { if (result.containsKey(type.getName() + ConfigConstants.CONFIG_STATUS)) { promise.fail(String.format("Found failed backup status for the object : %s", event.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_IP))); } else { promise.complete(); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception.getMessage()); } return promise.future(); } private void save(JsonObject item) { if (item.containsKey(StorageProfile.STORAGE_PROFILE_CONTEXT)) { item.mergeIn(item.getJsonObject(StorageProfile.STORAGE_PROFILE_CONTEXT)).remove(StorageProfile.STORAGE_PROFILE_CONTEXT); } item.put(DELETE_SRC_FILE, YES) .put(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_ENTITIES, new JsonArray().add(item.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_TARGET))) .put(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_EVENT_PROCESSORS, new JsonArray().add(RemoteEventProcessorConfigStore.getStore().flatItemsByValue(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE, BootstrapType.APP.name(), RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_INSTALLATION_MODE, Bootstrap.getInstallationMode()).getJsonObject(0).getLong(ID))); // routing key var protocol = StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.valueOfName(item.getString(StorageProfile.STORAGE_PROFILE_PROTOCOL)); if (StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.FTP == protocol || StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.TFTP == protocol || StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.SFTP == protocol) { var id = Runbook.getStorageProfileRunbookId(protocol); if (id != GlobalConstants.DUMMY_ID) { vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_RUNBOOK, item.put(ID, id)); } } else if (StorageProfile.StorageProtocol.LOCAL == protocol) { CommonUtil.copy(item); if (item.containsKey(MESSAGE)) { LOGGER.warn(item.getString(MESSAGE)); } } } / This method performs pre-validation on a given event based on the specified configuration operation.

- It checks if the discovery process has already succeeded. - If the discovery or backup operation has already succeeded, it verifies the backup status for each configuration type. - For each configuration type: - If the backup status is successful, it retrieves or reads the backup file content. - If the file transfer protocol is "NONE", it retrieves the content from the event; otherwise, it reads the content from the file system. - It checks if the content is non-empty, setting `isValid` accordingly.

- If validation fails (`isValid` is false), the event status is set to failure, and appropriate error details are added to the event. @param event The JSON object representing the event to be validated. @param operation The specific configuration operation being performed (e.g., DISCOVERY, BACKUP).

question: Show the pattern for: How does JobScheduler.JobScheduler() work?
answer:
The JobScheduler class is responsible for managing and coordinating all scheduled jobs in the Motadata platform.

This class provides functionality for:

  • Initializing the Quartz scheduler
  • Scheduling system jobs that run automatically
  • Scheduling custom jobs defined by users
  • Managing job lifecycle (creation, execution, deletion)
  • Handling job notifications

The JobScheduler uses the Quartz scheduler library to manage job scheduling and execution. It maintains separate job groups for system jobs and custom jobs, and provides methods for scheduling, removing, and triggering jobs.

This class is designed as a singleton with static methods and cannot be instantiated directly. / public class JobScheduler { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(JobScheduler.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_JOB, "Job Scheduler"); / Job group identifier for LDAP server synchronization jobs / private static final String LDAP_SERVER_SYNC_JOB = "ldap-server-sync-job"; / Job group identifier for system jobs / private static final String SYSTEM_JOB = "system-job"; / Job group identifier for custom jobs / private static final String CUSTOM_JOB = "custom-job"; / Job group identifier for triggered custom jobs / private static final String TRIGGER_CUSTOM_JOB = "trigger-custom-job"; / The Quartz scheduler instance / private static Scheduler scheduler = null; / Private constructor to prevent instantiation.

question: How does SNMPTrapProcessor.SNMPTrapProcessor() work?

The SNMPTrapProcessor class is responsible for processing SNMP trap messages received from network devices.

This class handles the following operations:

  • Initializing and starting the SNMP trap listener
  • Processing incoming SNMP trap messages
  • Parsing trap PDUs and extracting relevant information
  • Forwarding traps to configured destinations
  • Generating alerts based on link up/down traps
  • Maintaining a cache of interface names for correlation

question: How does ObjectConfigStore.populateItemsByProfile() work?
answer:
Populates the itemsByProfile map with profile IDs as keys and sets of object IDs as values. This method processes all provided user profiles and maps each profile to the objects that are accessible based on the profile's group configuration.

The itemsByProfile map structure:

  • Key: Profile ID (Long)
  • Value: Set of object internal IDs (Set<Long>) that belong to the profile's groups

Processing logic:

  • For each profile, retrieves the groups defined in the profile context (ENTITIES field)
  • Uses {@link #getItemsByGroups(JsonArray)} to find all objects belonging to those groups
  • If objects are found, creates/updates the profile's entry in the map
  • If no objects are found and the profile exists in the map, clears the profile's set

This method is typically called during:

  • System initialization to build the initial profile-to-object mappings
  • Profile updates when profile group configurations change
  • Bulk refresh operations to rebuild the entire map

Note: This method processes all profiles at once. For single object updates

@param profiles a JsonArray containing user profile objects to process

question: What does the MicrosoftTeamsNotification class do?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Microsoft Teams notifications.

This class handles Microsoft Teams notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Microsoft Teams API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Teams channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Teams service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Teams API requests

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Teams integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Teams integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Sends HTTP requests to the Teams API for each channel
  6. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  7. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Teams card format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Microsoft Teams service is experiencing issues.

question: What does the ShutdownUtil class do?
answer:
Utility class for managing file-based shutdown mechanisms on Windows systems.

This class provides a cross-process shutdown coordination mechanism specifically designed for Windows environments where multiple Motadata processes need to be gracefully terminated. It implements a file-based signaling system that allows external processes, services, or system administrators to trigger controlled application shutdown.

Key Features:

  • File-based shutdown watcher that monitors for shutdown signals
  • Periodic monitoring with configurable intervals (default: 1 second)
  • Asynchronous file operations using Vert.x file system API
  • Graceful shutdown coordination across multiple processes
  • Windows-specific implementation with OS validation

Workflow:

  1. Initialize shutdown watcher using {@link #initShutdownWatcher()}
  2. Watcher periodically checks for shutdown file existence and content
  3. External processes write shutdown signal using {@link #writeShutdownSignal()}
  4. When "shutdown" keyword is detected, application terminates gracefully

File Structure: 

   {CURRENT_DIR}/shutdown/shutdown.ctx

Usage Example: 

   // Initialize shutdown watcher (typically in Bootstrap)   ShutdownUtil.initShutdownWatcher(vertx);     // Trigger shutdown from another process   ShutdownUtil.writeShutdownSignal(vertx)       .onSuccess(v -> logger.info("Shutdown signal sent"))       .onFailure(throwable -> logger.error("Failed to send shutdown signal", throwable));

Thread Safety: This class uses static methods and maintains internal state through static variables. The {@code running} flag is used to coordinate shutdown across multiple timer instances.

Platform Compatibility: Currently supports Windows systems only. Non-Windows platforms will log a debug message and skip initialization.

question: What does the FlowCacheProcessor class do?
answer:
Manages the caching of flow data to improve performance and handle high volumes of flow information.

The FlowCacheProcessor is responsible for efficiently managing flow data in memory and on disk. It implements mechanisms for storing, retrieving, and processing flow data to handle high volumes of network traffic information without overwhelming system resources.

Key responsibilities of this class include:

  • Initializing and managing flow cache files on disk
  • Buffering flow data in memory before writing to disk
  • Processing cached flow data in batches
  • Monitoring flow rates and ensuring they stay within license limits
  • Implementing efficient data structures for flow data storage
  • Managing the lifecycle of flow cache files

The FlowCacheProcessor works closely with other components in the flow package:

  • It receives flow data from the FlowProcessor
  • It provides cached data to the FlowStatCalculator for statistical analysis
  • It interacts with the license system to ensure flow processing stays within licensed limits

This class is deployed as a Vert.x verticle and integrates with the event bus system for communication with other components.

question: What does the LDAPSyncJob class do?
answer:
The LDAPSyncJob class is responsible for synchronizing LDAP users with the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and is annotated with {@link DisallowConcurrentExecution} to ensure that only one instance of this job runs at a time. The job synchronizes user information from an LDAP server with the Motadata platform's user database.

The job is scheduled to run at configurable intervals, determined by the LDAP server configuration. The CRON expression used for scheduling is parameterized with placeholders (@@, ##) that are replaced with actual values when the job is scheduled.

The synchronization process ensures that user information in the Motadata platform remains consistent with the LDAP directory, which is often the authoritative source for user data in enterprise environments.

question: Show the pattern for: How does ObjectConfigStore.updateItemsByUser() work?
answer:
Updates the itemsByProfile and itemsByUser maps for a specific object ID based on group membership. This method evaluates whether the given object qualifies for access by various user profiles and users based on the groups the object belongs to.

The method performs two main operations:

  • Profile-based access: For GROUP-scoped profiles, checks if the object belongs to any of the profile's groups and updates the itemsByProfile map accordingly
  • User-based access: For users, checks if the object belongs to any of the user's groups and updates the itemsByUser map accordingly. The default user (ID = 1) has access to all objects

Access qualification logic:

  • For profiles: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the profile's groups (ENTITIES)
  • For users: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the user's groups (USER_GROUPS)
  • Default user: Always has access to all objects regardless of group membership

This method should be called when:

  • An object's groups are modified (added/removed)
  • A new object is added to the system with group assignments
  • Object group membership changes that affect user/profile access
@param objectId the internal ID of the object to evaluate for profile and user access

question: What does the ZMQClient class do?
answer:
ZeroMQ (ZMQ) client implementation for the Motadata transport layer.

This class provides a ZeroMQ-based transport client that supports multiple socket modes including SUB (receiver), PUSH, and PULL patterns. It implements the {@link TransportClient} interface to provide a standardized transport abstraction layer.

The client supports different ZeroMQ socket patterns:

  • SUB (Receivers): Receives messages from PUB sockets, supports topic filtering
  • PUSH: Sends messages to PULL sockets in a load-balanced manner
  • PULL: Receives messages from PUSH sockets in a round-robin fashion

Key features:

  • Configurable High Water Mark (HWM) for message queuing
  • TCP keep-alive support for connection reliability
  • Topic-based message filtering for SUB sockets
  • Thread-safe message handling with atomic operations
  • Integration with Vert.x event bus for message routing

Configuration example:

{@code   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put("SOCKET_MODE", "SUB")       .put("HOST", "localhost")       .put("PORT", 5555)       .put("EVENT_TYPE", "remote.events");     ZMQClient client = new ZMQClient(config);   client.registerMessageHandler(message -> {       // Handle received message   });   client.connect().onSuccess(v -> {       client.receive(); // Start receiving messages   });   }
@author Motadata Engineering Team @version 1.0 @since 1.0 @see TransportClient @see ZMQServer

question: How does ZMQServer.ZMQServer() work?
answer:
ZeroMQ (ZMQ) server implementation for the Motadata transport layer.

This class provides a ZeroMQ-based transport server that supports multiple socket modes for different messaging patterns. It implements the {@link TransportServer} interface to provide a standardized transport abstraction layer for server-side operations.

The server supports different ZeroMQ socket patterns:

  • PUB (Sender): Publishes messages to multiple SUB receivers
  • PULL: Receives messages from multiple PUSH clients in a round-robin fashion
  • PUSH: Sends messages to PULL sockets in a load-balanced manner

Key features:

  • Configurable High Water Mark (HWM) for message queuing and flow control
  • TCP keep-alive support for connection reliability
  • Automatic handling of slow receivers (XPUB_NODROP)
  • Thread-safe message handling with atomic operations
  • Integration with Vert.x event bus for message routing
  • Support for both binding and connecting modes

Configuration example:

{@code   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put("SOCKET_MODE", "PUB")       .put("HOST", "localhost")       .put("PORT", 5555)       .put("EVENT_TYPE", "remote.events");     ZMQServer server = new ZMQServer(config);   server.bind().onSuccess(v -> {       // Server is ready to accept connections       server.send("topic", "Hello World".getBytes());   });   }

Thread Safety: This class is thread-safe for concurrent access to its public methods. However, the underlying ZMQ socket operations are performed in dedicated threads.

@author Motadata Engineering Team @version 1.0 @since 1.0 @see TransportServer @see ZMQClient / public class ZMQServer implements TransportServer { / Configuration object containing server parameters such as host, port, socket mode, and event type. This configuration is used to establish the ZMQ server binding and determine behavior. / private final JsonObject config; / The underlying ZeroMQ socket instance used for server operations. This socket is configured based on the socket mode specified in the configuration. / private ZMQ.Socket server; / The event type identifier used for routing messages to the appropriate event bus consumers. Extracted from the configuration during initialization. / private final String eventType; / Atomic boolean flag indicating whether the server should continue processing events. Used to control the message receiving loop in a thread-safe manner. / private final AtomicBoolean hasMoreEvent = new AtomicBoolean(true); private Thread receiver; / Logger instance for this ZMQ server, configured with appropriate context and component name. / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(ZMQServer.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_EVENT_BUS, "ZMQ Server", GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.AGENT.equals(Bootstrap.bootstrapType())); / Constructs a new ZMQServer with the specified configuration.

The configuration object must contain the following required parameters:

  • SOCKET_MODE: The ZMQ socket mode (PUB, PULL, or PUSH)
  • HOST: The host address to bind to (for binding modes)
  • PORT: The port number to bind to or connect to
  • EVENT_TYPE: The event type for message routing

The constructor initializes the server configuration but does not establish the actual ZMQ socket connection. Call {@link #bind()} to start the server.

@param config the configuration object containing server parameters and settings. Must not be null and should contain all required parameters. @throws NullPointerException if config is null @throws IllegalArgumentException if required configuration parameters are missing
