A Vert.x verticle responsible for polling metrics from monitored systems and devices.

The MetricPoller class is a central component of the monitoring system that:

1. Manages worker pools for different types of metric polling: - Regular metrics (SNMP, WMI, etc.) - Availability/ping checks - Network service (port) checks

2. Schedules and executes metric polling operations based on: - Metric category (Network, Server, Database, etc.) - Metric type (regular, availability, network service) - Timeout requirements - Batch processing capabilities

3. Implements load balancing and resource management: - Tracks idle workers across different categories - Distributes polling tasks based on worker availability - Handles metric queuing and prioritization - Implements auto-scaling of worker pools when needed

4. Processes polling results and sends them to appropriate event bus addresses

/ Worker executors for availability/ping checks / private final List availabilityWorkerExecutors = new ArrayList<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each metric category / private final Map idleWorkersByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each metric worker executor / private final Map idleMetricWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each availability worker executor / private final Map idleAvailabilityWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Tracks the number of idle workers for each network service worker executor / private final Map idleNetworkServiceWorkersByExecutor = new HashMap<>(); / Queued metrics organized by category and timeout value type / private final Map>> metricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Queued batch metrics organized by category and timeout value type / private final Map>> batchMetricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Counts of discarded metrics by category (due to overload or duplicates) / private final Map discardedMetricsByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Queued availability metrics organized by packet count / private final Map> pendingAvailabilityMetrics = new LinkedHashMap<>(); / Queued network service metrics / private final List pendingNetworkServiceMetrics = new ArrayList<>(); / Tracks duplicate metrics to avoid redundant polling operations / private final Map> duplicateMetrics = new HashMap<>(); / Current timeout value type for each metric category (used for round-robin scheduling) / private final Map metricTimeoutValueTypesByCategory = new EnumMap<>(Category.class); / Total count of idle metric workers across all executors / private final AtomicInteger idleMetricWorkers = new AtomicInteger(); / Total count of idle availability workers across all executors / private int idleAvailabilityWorkers; / Total count of idle network service workers across all executors / private int idleNetworkServiceWorkers = MotadataConfigUtil.getNetworkServiceWorkers() MotadataConfigUtil.getWorkers(); / Initializes the MetricPoller verticle and starts all polling operations.

This method: 1. Creates worker executor pools for different types of metric polling 2. Sets up worker allocation for different metric categories 3. Registers event bus consumers for handling metric polling requests and stats 4. Starts periodic timers for scheduling different types of metric polling: - Regular metrics (every 1000ms) - Availability/ping checks (every 500ms) - Network service checks (every 100ms)

question: How does ObjectConfigStore.updateItemsByUser() work?
answer:
Updates the itemsByProfile and itemsByUser maps for a specific object ID based on group membership. This method evaluates whether the given object qualifies for access by various user profiles and users based on the groups the object belongs to.

The method performs two main operations:

  • Profile-based access: For GROUP-scoped profiles, checks if the object belongs to any of the profile's groups and updates the itemsByProfile map accordingly
  • User-based access: For users, checks if the object belongs to any of the user's groups and updates the itemsByUser map accordingly. The default user (ID = 1) has access to all objects

Access qualification logic:

  • For profiles: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the profile's groups (ENTITIES)
  • For users: Object qualifies if any of its groups match any of the user's groups (USER_GROUPS)
  • Default user: Always has access to all objects regardless of group membership

This method should be called when:

  • An object's groups are modified (added/removed)
  • A new object is added to the system with group assignments
  • Object group membership changes that affect user/profile access
@param objectId the internal ID of the object to evaluate for profile and user access

question: What does the FlowCacheCleanupJob class do?
answer:
The FlowCacheCleanupJob class is responsible for cleaning up outdated flow cache files in the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and performs regular cleanup of flow cache files to prevent excessive disk usage and maintain system performance. Flow cache files store network flow data temporarily and need to be periodically cleaned up to avoid accumulation of stale data.

The job performs the following tasks:

  1. Reads the flow-cache directory to list files
  2. Extracts timestamps from filenames (last 12 characters in yyyyMMddHHmm format)
  3. Deletes files older than 1 hour to ensure only recent data is kept
  4. Sends a cleanup event with the list of deleted files
  5. Sends a notification to clear cache from all event collectors

The job is scheduled to run every 6 hours to ensure regular cleanup of flow cache files.

Implementation note: This job was enhanced as part of MOTADATA-5435 to support the flow back-pressure mechanism.

DELIVERY_OPTIONS.setSendTimeout(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(event.getLong(REQUEST_TIMEOUT))) : DELIVERY_OPTIONS.setSendTimeout(300000L), reply -> { try { if (reply.succeeded()) { var response = reply.result().body(); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("runbook result : %s", response != null ? CommonUtil.removeSensitiveFields(response, true) : null)); } // publish this event for each ncm device inorder to reflect this change in ncm explorer if (event.containsKey(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_CATEGORY) && event.getString(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_CATEGORY).equalsIgnoreCase(Runbook.RunbookCategory.CONFIG.getName())) { EventBusConstants.publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CONFIG_REQUEST_STATE_CHANGE, new JsonObject().put(ConfigConstants.CONFIG_OPERATION, ConfigConstants.ConfigOperation.RUNBOOK.getName()).put(ID, ConfigurationConfigStore.getStore().getIdByObjectId(ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getObjectId(event.getLong(ID)))).put(NMSConstants.STATE, NMSConstants.STATE_NOT_RUNNING)); } complete(response, manual); if (notify) { if (reply.succeeded()) { if (response != null && response.getString(STATUS) != null && !response.getString(STATUS).equalsIgnoreCase(STATUS_SUCCEED)) { ErrorMessageConstants.extractErrorCode(response, ErrorMessageConstants.RUNBOOK_EXECUTION_FAILED, null, null, null); } promise.complete(response); } else { ErrorMessageConstants.extractErrorCode(event.put(ERRORS, new JsonArray(new ArrayList(1)).add(reply.cause())), ErrorMessageConstants.RUNBOOK_EXECUTION_FAILED, null, null, null); promise.complete(event); } } } else { LOGGER.warn(reply.cause().getMessage()); event.put(STATUS, STATUS_FAIL).put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR).put(MESSAGE, reply.cause().getMessage()); if (!promise.future().isComplete()) { promise.complete(event); } complete(event, manual); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); event.put(STATUS, STATUS_FAIL).put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR).put(MESSAGE, CommonUtil.formatStackTrace(exception.getStackTrace())); if (!promise.future().isComplete()) { promise.complete(event); } complete(event, manual); } }); return promise.future(); } / Handles the completion of a runbook execution.

question: Show the pattern for: How does SMSNotification.SMSNotification() work?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending SMS notifications.

This class handles SMS notifications by sending HTTP requests to a configured SMS gateway service. It supports:

  • Sending SMS messages to multiple recipients in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle SMS service failures
  • Proxy server configuration for SMS gateway access
  • URL templating for different SMS gateway providers
  • Configurable timeout for SMS gateway requests

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves SMS gateway configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that the gateway URL and recipients are specified
  3. Sends HTTP requests to the SMS gateway for each recipient
  4. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link Notification#SMS_NOTIFICATION_RECIPIENTS}: JsonArray of recipient phone numbers
  • {@link Notification#SMS_NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE}: The text message to send
  • {@link GlobalConstants#TIMEOUT} (optional): Timeout in seconds for the HTTP request

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the SMS gateway service is experiencing issues. / public class SMSNotification extends Notification { / Logger for SMS notification operations / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(SMSNotification.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NOTIFICATION, "SMS Notification"); / Circuit breaker to handle SMS service failures.

The circuit breaker:

  • Opens after 5 consecutive failures
  • Considers a request failed if it takes more than 30 seconds
  • Stays open for 60 seconds before attempting to reset
  • Calls the fallback handler when open
/ private final CircuitBreaker circuitBreaker = CircuitBreaker.create("sms-service-circuit-breaker", Bootstrap.vertx(), new CircuitBreakerOptions() .setMaxFailures(5) // number of failure before opening the circuit .setTimeout(30000) // consider a failure if the operation does not succeed in time .setFallbackOnFailure(true) // do we call the fallback on failure .setResetTimeout(60000) // time spent in open state before attempting to re-try ).openHandler(handler -> LOGGER.warn(ErrorMessageConstants.SMS_SERVICE_FAILED)).closeHandler(handler -> LOGGER.info(InfoMessageConstants.SMS_SERVICE_RESTORED)).fallback(handler -> handler.initCause(new Exception(ErrorMessageConstants.SMS_SERVICE_FAILED))); / Default constructor for SMSNotification.

question: Show the pattern for: How does DailyMiscJobs.cleanupFlapCache() work?
answer:
The DailyMiscJobs class is responsible for executing various daily maintenance tasks.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and is annotated with @DisallowConcurrentExecution to ensure that only one instance of this job runs at a time. It performs several maintenance tasks that need to be executed daily:

  • Resetting the event ID counter
  • Running log retention to clean up old logs
  • Cleaning up the flap cache based on retention policy
  • Triggering configuration backup cleanup

The job is scheduled to run every day at midnight (12:00 AM). / @DisallowConcurrentExecution public class DailyMiscJobs implements Job { / CRON expression for scheduling this job to run every day at midnight (12:00 AM) / static final String DAILY_MISC_JOBS_CRON_EXPRESSION = "0 0 0 ?"; // execute on every day 12:00 AM / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(DailyMiscJobs.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_JOB, "System Job"); / Executes the daily maintenance tasks.

This method is called by the Quartz scheduler when the job is triggered. It performs the following tasks:

  1. Resets the event ID counter to prevent overflow
  2. Runs log retention to delete old log files based on retention policy
  3. Cleans up the flap cache based on retention policy
  4. Triggers configuration backup cleanup
@param context the context in which the job is executed / @Override public void execute(JobExecutionContext context) { // Reset the event ID counter LOGGER.info("resetting event id counter...."); CommonUtil.resetEventId(); LOGGER.info("event id counter reset done successfully..."); // Run log retention LOGGER.info(String.format("running log retention job for system boot sequence %s", Bootstrap.bootstrapType())); LogUtil.runLogRetention(Bootstrap.bootstrapType() == GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.AGENT ? AgentConfigUtil.getAgentLogRetentionDays() : MotadataConfigUtil.getLogRetentionDays()); LOGGER.info("log retention job completed successfully..."); // Clean up flap cache LOGGER.info("flap cache retention job started..."); cleanupFlapCache(MotadataConfigUtil.getFlapCacheRetentionDays()); LOGGER.info("flap cache retention job completed successfully..."); // Trigger configuration backup cleanup Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CONFIG_BACKUP_CLEANUP, DataRetentionPolicyConfigStore.getStore().getItem(GlobalConstants.DEFAULT_ID) .getJsonObject(DataRetentionPolicy.DATA_RETENTION_POLICY_CONTEXT) .getJsonObject("CONFIG")); if (!MotadataConfigUtil.devMode()) { // manage SLO profile cycles at every midnight Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_SLO_CYCLE_QUALIFY, new JsonObject()); } } / Cleans up flap cache files based on the specified retention period.

This method deletes flap cache files that are older than the specified retention period. It calculates the cutoff date based on the retention days and deletes any files created before that date. The creation time of each file is extracted from its filename.

Implementation note: This method was added as part of MOTADATA-970 to define code for retaining files within a specific timeline. @param retentionDays the number of days to retain flap cache files (files older than this will be deleted)

question: How does TraceMetricProcessor.addEventSource() work?
answer:
Updates the configuration for all registered plugins based on the provided event source IP address.

This method performs the following:

  • Iterates over each plugin in the {@code plugins} list.
  • If the environment is {@code ENV_TEST}, uses a hardcoded IP ("172.16.8.135") to fetch the configuration item.
  • Otherwise, uses the given {@code eventSource} IP to fetch the corresponding configuration item.
  • Updates the plugin with the retrieved configuration item using {@link ObjectConfigStore}.

This allows plugins to be dynamically updated with environment-specific configuration based on the source of incoming events. @param eventSource the IP address of the event source, used to retrieve the relevant configuration item.

question: How does TopologyEngine.for() work?
answer:
TopologyEngine is responsible for discovering and managing network topology relationships.

This class handles:

  • Network topology discovery using various protocols (SNMP, CDP, LLDP, etc.)
  • Building dependency maps between network devices
  • Tracking connections between network elements
  • Managing worker allocation for topology discovery jobs
  • Processing topology discovery events and responses
  • Notifying users about topology discovery results

The engine supports both Layer 2 (L2) and Layer 3 (L3) topology discovery and can handle various network protocols. It implements a worker pool model to efficiently process topology discovery requests in parallel while managing system resources. / public class TopologyEngine extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger instance for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(TopologyEngine.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NMS, "Topology Engine"); / Delivery options for event bus messages with a 10-minute timeout / private static final DeliveryOptions DELIVERY_OPTIONS = new DeliveryOptions().setSendTimeout(600000L); / Worker executor for processing topology discovery jobs with a 60-minute timeout / private final WorkerExecutor workerExecutor = Bootstrap.vertx().createSharedWorkerExecutor("Topology Engine", MotadataConfigUtil.getTopologyWorkers(), 60L, TimeUnit.MINUTES); / Map to store topology discovery events by event ID / private final Map events = new HashMap<>(); / Map to organize topology discovery events by plugin type / private final Map> eventsByPluginType = new EnumMap<>(NMSConstants.TopologyPluginType.class); / Map to track the number of idle workers for each topology plugin type / private final Map idleWorkersByPluginType = new EnumMap<>(NMSConstants.TopologyPluginType.class); / Counter for tracking the total number of idle workers across all plugin types / private final AtomicInteger idleWorkers = new AtomicInteger(MotadataConfigUtil.getTopologyWorkers()); / Map to organize network protocols by link layer (L2 or L3) / private final Map protocolsByLinkLayer = new HashMap<>(); / Map to track connections between network devices / private final Map connections = new HashMap<>(); / Counter for tracking consecutive empty event checks to determine when to stop the timer / private int eventProbes = 0; / Flag indicating whether the periodic timer for processing events is active / private boolean timeHandlerActive = false; / Initializes the TopologyEngine verticle.

This method: 1. Sets up data structures to organize protocols by link layer (L2/L3) 2. Initializes event tracking and worker allocation for different plugin types 3. Registers event bus consumers for topology events and statistics 4. Sets up a periodic timer to process pending topology discovery events 5. Configures worker allocation for different topology plugin types

The method handles different types of topology discovery events based on their plugin type and manages worker allocation to ensure efficient resource usage. @param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done @throws Exception If an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { for (var entry : LEVELS_BY_NETWORK_PROTOCOLS.entrySet()) { var linkLayer = entry.getValue().equals(AIOpsConstants.DependencyLevel.SIX.getName()) ? TopologyLinkLayer.L2.getName() : TopologyLinkLayer.L3.getName(); protocolsByLinkLayer.computeIfAbsent(linkLayer, value -> new JsonArray()).add(entry.getKey()); } for (var topologyType : NMSConstants.TopologyPluginType.values()) { eventsByPluginType.put(topologyType, new ArrayList<>()); idleWorkersByPluginType.put(topologyType, NMSConstants.getTopologyWorkersByPluginType(topologyType)); } vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ENGINE_STATS, message -> { if (MotadataConfigUtil.devMode()) { vertx.eventBus().publish(Bootstrap.bootstrapType() == GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.COLLECTOR || Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.SECONDARY.name()) ? EventBusConstants.EVENT_REMOTE : EventBusConstants.EVENT_ENGINE_STATS_RESPONSE, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_ENGINE_STATS) .put(EventBusConstants.ENGINE_TYPE, EVENT_TOPOLOGY) .put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, Bootstrap.getRegistrationId()) .put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE, Bootstrap.bootstrapType().name()).put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_INSTALLATION_MODE, Bootstrap.getInstallationMode()) .put(HealthUtil.HEALTH_STATS, new JsonObject().put(HealthUtil.PENDING_EVENTS, events.size()) .put(HealthUtil.IDLE_WORKERS, idleWorkers.get()))); } else { vertx.eventBus().send(Bootstrap.bootstrapType() == GlobalConstants.BootstrapType.COLLECTOR || Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.SECONDARY.name()) ? EventBusConstants.EVENT_REMOTE : EventBusConstants.EVENT_ENGINE_STATS_RESPONSE, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_ENGINE_STATS) .put(EventBusConstants.ENGINE_TYPE, EVENT_TOPOLOGY) .put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_UUID, Bootstrap.getRegistrationId()) .put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TYPE, Bootstrap.bootstrapType().name()).put(RemoteEventProcessor.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_INSTALLATION_MODE, Bootstrap.getInstallationMode()) .put(HealthUtil.HEALTH_STATS, new JsonObject().put(HealthUtil.PENDING_EVENTS, events.size()) .put(HealthUtil.IDLE_WORKERS, idleWorkers.get()))); } }); if (Bootstrap.bootstrapType() == BootstrapType.APP && (Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.STANDALONE.name())) || Bootstrap.getInstallationMode().equalsIgnoreCase(InstallationMode.PRIMARY.name())) { vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPOLOGY_RUN, message -> { try { var event = message.body(); if (event != null && !event.isEmpty()) { var schedulerId = event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_SCHEDULER); LOGGER.info(String.format("request received to schedule topology for scheduler id %s", schedulerId)); if (!event.containsKey(TopologyPlugin.TOPOLOGY_PLUGIN_DISCOVERY)) { vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_PUBLICATION, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION) .put(EventBusConstants.CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE, EventBusConstants.ChangeNotificationType.RUN_TOPOLOGY.name()) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPIC, EventBusConstants.REMOTE_EVENT_PROCESSOR_TOPIC) .put(ID, schedulerId) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_SCHEDULER, schedulerId)); } vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ADD, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, TopologyCacheStore.getStore().getEventId(schedulerId)) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPOLOGY_RUN) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE_QUEUED) .put(USER_NAME, event.containsKey(USER_NAME) ? event.getString(USER_NAME) : DEFAULT_USER) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CONTEXT, event).mergeIn(event)); var objects = ObjectConfigStore.getStore().getItems(event.getJsonArray(TopologyPlugin.TOPOLOGY_PLUGIN_ENTRY_POINTS)); if (objects != null && !objects.isEmpty()) { EventBusConstants.updateEvent(TopologyCacheStore.getStore().getEventId(schedulerId), String.format(InfoMessageConstants.EVENT_TRACKER_EVENT_STARTED, DateTimeUtil.timestamp()), EventBusConstants.EVENT_STATE_RUNNING); var probes = 0; var runbook = getNextHopRunbook(); var qualifiedPlugins = qualify(); var credentials = new HashMap(); MetricConfigStore.getStore().flatMap().values().stream().filter(item -> item.getString(Metric.METRIC_PLUGIN).equalsIgnoreCase(NMSConstants.MetricPlugin.SNMP_DEVICE.getName())) .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(item -> item.getLong(Metric.METRIC_OBJECT), Collectors.mapping(item -> item.getLong(Metric.METRIC_CREDENTIAL_PROFILE), Collectors.toList()))) .forEach((key, value) -> credentials.put(key, value.getFirst())); var qualifiedObjects = new HashSet(); var qualifiedProtocols = event.getJsonArray(TOPOLOGY_PROTOCOLS); for (var index = 0; index < objects.size(); index++) { var object = objects.getJsonObject(index); LOGGER.info(String.format("seed ip is : %s ", object.getString(OBJECT_IP))); var status = ObjectStatusCacheStore.getStore().getItem(object.getLong(ID)); if (object.getString(AIOpsObject.OBJECT_STATE).equalsIgnoreCase(NMSConstants.State.ENABLE.name()) && (status == null || status.equalsIgnoreCase(STATUS_UP))) { probes++; TopologyCacheStore.getStore().addParent(object.getString(OBJECT_IP)); probe(object, qualifiedObjects, runbook, credentials, qualifiedPlugins, event, object.getString(OBJECT_IP), qualifiedProtocols); } } if (probes == 0) { LOGGER.info(String.format("topology scheduler aborted, reason: %s", ErrorMessageConstants.OBJECT_ERROR)); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPOLOGY_STOP, event.put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_NO_ITEM_FOUND).put(MESSAGE, String.format(ErrorMessageConstants.TOPOLOGY_RUN_ERROR, ErrorMessageConstants.OBJECT_ERROR))); } } else { LOGGER.info(String.format("topology scheduler aborted, reason: %s", TOPOLOGY_ENTRY_POINT_MISSING)); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPOLOGY_STOP, event.put(ERROR_CODE, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_NO_ITEM_FOUND).put(MESSAGE, String.format(ErrorMessageConstants.TOPOLOGY_RUN_ERROR, TOPOLOGY_ENTRY_POINT_MISSING))); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); } vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TOPOLOGY_COMPLETE, message -> { try { var event = message.body(); var dependencies = TopologyCacheStore.getStore().getDependencies(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_SCHEDULER)); // processing all dependencies one by one where destination port is not available if (dependencies != null && !dependencies.isEmpty()) { if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("dependencies cache after running topology on scheduler id %s is %s", event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_SCHEDULER), dependencies.encode())); } / dependencies will be like & from this we will process the dependencies whose destination port value is empty. { "6``||``172.16.8.2``||``172.16.8.2``||``28``||``172.16.10.47": "24", "6``||``172.16.10.47``||``172.16.10.47``||``19``||``172.16.10.43": "10119", "6``||``172.16.10.47``||``172.16.10.47``||``20``||``172.16.10.43": "" }

question: Show the pattern for: How does TransportProvider.getServer() work?
answer:
Creates and returns a transport server implementation based on the provided configuration.

This factory method examines the configuration to determine which transport server implementation to instantiate. The transport protocol is specified in the configuration using the {@link EventBusConstants#TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL} key.

Currently supported transport server implementations:

  • {@link ZMQServer} - For ZeroMQ transport protocol

The configuration object should contain all necessary parameters for the specific transport implementation, such as:

  • Host address to bind to
  • Port number
  • Socket mode (PUB, PULL, etc.)
  • Protocol-specific options (high water mark, etc.)

Example configuration for ZMQ server:

{@code       JsonObject config = new JsonObject()           .put(TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL, TransportProtocol.ZMQ.getValue())           .put("host", "")           .put("port", 5555)           .put("socket_mode", SocketMode.PUB);       }
@param config a JsonObject containing the transport server configuration @return a TransportServer implementation based on the specified protocol @throws IllegalArgumentException if the specified protocol is not supported or if the configuration is invalid @see TransportServer @see ZMQServer @see EventBusConstants.TransportProtocol

question: How does VisualizationMetricManager.if() work?
answer:
Filters and qualifies entities for metric visualization based on specified criteria.

This method processes the visualization context and filters entities based on:

  • Group membership
  • Tag associations
  • Instance types
  • Plugin compatibility
  • Archive status

The method handles both regular metrics and instance-based metrics differently, applying appropriate filtering logic for each case. For instance-based metrics, it can build entity keys for more precise data retrieval. @param context The visualization context containing filter criteria @param userId userId of the user @param qualifiedObjects Objects that qualify for inclusion @param pluginIds Plugin IDs to consider for qualification @param filteredGroupEntities Entities filtered by group @param filteredTagEntities Entities filtered by tag @param buildEntityKey Whether to build entity keys for instance metrics @param instanceEntityKey Whether to use instance-specific entity keys @param archived Whether to include archived entities @return A map containing qualified entities and related metadata / private Map qualifyEntities(JsonObject context, long userId, Set qualifiedObjects, JsonArray pluginIds, Set filteredGroupEntities, Set filteredTagEntities, boolean buildEntityKey, boolean instanceEntityKey, boolean archived) { Map qualifiedEntities = null; try { var column = context.getString(DATA_POINT); Map entities = null; Map entityKeys = null; JsonObject filteredEntities; var pluginEntities = new HashMap>(); var plugins = new HashSet<>(); // Determine if this is an instance-based metric by checking for instance separator in the column name var instanceMetric = column.contains(INSTANCE_SEPARATOR); // Get instance keys from context or use empty array if not present var instanceKeys = context.getJsonArray(FILTER_KEYS, new JsonArray()); // Set default entity type to "all" if not specified if (!context.containsKey(ENTITY_TYPE)) { context.put(ENTITY_TYPE, "all"); } // Initialize plugin entities map with metric names for valid plugin IDs for (var pluginId : pluginIds) { if (MetricConfigStore.getStore().getMetricName(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId)) != null) { // Create mapping of plugin ID + metric name to set of entity IDs pluginEntities.computeIfAbsent(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId) + DASH_SEPARATOR + MetricConfigStore.getStore().getMetricName(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId)), value -> new HashSet<>()); } } // Filter entities based on groups, objects, and tags var items = filterEntities(context, userId, qualifiedObjects, filteredGroupEntities, filteredTagEntities, LOGGER, archived); // Process qualified items if they exist if (items != null && !items.isEmpty()) { // Initialize entity maps entities = new HashMap<>(); entityKeys = new HashMap<>(); // Special handling for instance-based metrics with keys or entity key building requirements if ((!instanceKeys.isEmpty() || buildEntityKey || (instanceEntityKey && !filteredTagEntities.isEmpty())) && instanceMetric) { // Remove availability plugin ID as it's handled separately if (pluginIds.contains(NMSConstants.AVAILABILITY_PLUGIN_ID)) { pluginIds.remove(NMSConstants.AVAILABILITY_PLUGIN_ID); // Availability plugin not needed for instance metrics } / Handle instance entity keys when result grouping and instance type are the same. This allows for more precise filtering by matching tag-based instances.

This method determines how many times the system should attempt to detect a process during startup or monitoring operations. The number of attempts varies based on the bootstrap type: - For APP, COLLECTOR, EVENT_COLLECTOR, FLOW_COLLECTOR, and EVENT_PROCESSOR, it uses the value from MotadataConfigUtil - For AGENT, it uses the value from AgentConfigUtil - For DATASTORE, it uses a datastore-specific value from MotadataConfigUtil - For other bootstrap types, it uses a default value of 60 attempts

question: What does the MetricConfigStore class do?
answer:
Update multiple metric entries in the in-memory store and propagate necessary side-effects.

This method performs the following steps for each metric in the provided {@code metrics} array:

  • Fetches previous metric states for the supplied {@code ids} to determine state transitions.
  • Replaces/updates the metric entry in the local {@code this.items} store.
  • Detects state transitions and:
    • Sends {@code EVENT_METRIC_ENABLE} when a metric transitions from DISABLE to ENABLE.
    • Sends {@code EVENT_METRIC_DISABLE} when a metric transitions from ENABLE to DISABLE.
    • Adds the metric to {@code MetricCacheStore} when enabled and not discovered via INLINE discovery.
  • Updates any matching entry in {@code metricsByObject} to reflect new metric fields.
  • Calls {@code updateItems(metric, false, false)} to refresh instance/plugin mappings and related caches.
  • Publishes a change notification {@code EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION} for each updated metric.

All exceptions are caught and logged; callers should not expect exceptions to be propagated. @param metrics JsonArray of metric JsonObjects to be updated in the store @param ids JsonArray of metric ids used to lookup previous states for comparison

This method is the core processing function of the FlowProcessor. It takes a raw flow event, enriches it with additional information, and forwards it to various components for storage, analysis, and visualization.

The processing steps include:

  • Handling remote events from flow collectors
  • Managing sampling rates for interfaces
  • Enriching flow data with source and destination information
  • Decoding IP addresses and resolving them to hostnames
  • Adding geolocation information (country, city, coordinates)
  • Translating protocol numbers to protocol names
  • Mapping application ports to application names
  • Decoding Type of Service (ToS) values
  • Interpreting TCP flags
  • Calculating traffic metrics
  • Formatting the enriched data for storage and analysis

After processing, the enriched flow data is:

  • Sent to the event policy system for policy evaluation
  • Forwarded to the FlowStatCalculator for statistical analysis
  • Written to the datastore for storage and visualization

question: Show the pattern for: How does MetricConfigStore.updateAll() work?
answer:
Update multiple metric entries in the in-memory store and propagate necessary side-effects.

This method performs the following steps for each metric in the provided {@code metrics} array:

  • Fetches previous metric states for the supplied {@code ids} to determine state transitions.
  • Replaces/updates the metric entry in the local {@code this.items} store.
  • Detects state transitions and:
    • Sends {@code EVENT_METRIC_ENABLE} when a metric transitions from DISABLE to ENABLE.
    • Sends {@code EVENT_METRIC_DISABLE} when a metric transitions from ENABLE to DISABLE.
    • Adds the metric to {@code MetricCacheStore} when enabled and not discovered via INLINE discovery.
  • Updates any matching entry in {@code metricsByObject} to reflect new metric fields.
  • Calls {@code updateItems(metric, false, false)} to refresh instance/plugin mappings and related caches.
  • Publishes a change notification {@code EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION} for each updated metric.

All exceptions are caught and logged; callers should not expect exceptions to be propagated. @param metrics JsonArray of metric JsonObjects to be updated in the store @param ids JsonArray of metric ids used to lookup previous states for comparison

question: What does the SoundNotification class do?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for playing sound notifications.

This class handles sound notifications by publishing events to the UI layer, which is responsible for actually playing the sound. This approach allows the server-side notification system to trigger audio alerts in the user interface without having to directly interact with audio hardware.

The notification process:

  1. Publishes the notification event to the UI notification channel
  2. The UI layer receives the event and plays the appropriate sound
  3. Reports success or failure of the notification attempt

The notification event may contain parameters that control which sound to play, volume level, repetition count, etc., depending on what the UI layer supports.

This implementation uses Vert.x's event bus to communicate with the UI layer.

question: Show the pattern for: How does VisualizationMetricManager.if() work?
answer:
Filters and qualifies entities for metric visualization based on specified criteria.

This method processes the visualization context and filters entities based on:

  • Group membership
  • Tag associations
  • Instance types
  • Plugin compatibility
  • Archive status

The method handles both regular metrics and instance-based metrics differently, applying appropriate filtering logic for each case. For instance-based metrics, it can build entity keys for more precise data retrieval. @param context The visualization context containing filter criteria @param userId userId of the user @param qualifiedObjects Objects that qualify for inclusion @param pluginIds Plugin IDs to consider for qualification @param filteredGroupEntities Entities filtered by group @param filteredTagEntities Entities filtered by tag @param buildEntityKey Whether to build entity keys for instance metrics @param instanceEntityKey Whether to use instance-specific entity keys @param archived Whether to include archived entities @return A map containing qualified entities and related metadata / private Map qualifyEntities(JsonObject context, long userId, Set qualifiedObjects, JsonArray pluginIds, Set filteredGroupEntities, Set filteredTagEntities, boolean buildEntityKey, boolean instanceEntityKey, boolean archived) { Map qualifiedEntities = null; try { var column = context.getString(DATA_POINT); Map entities = null; Map entityKeys = null; JsonObject filteredEntities; var pluginEntities = new HashMap>(); var plugins = new HashSet<>(); // Determine if this is an instance-based metric by checking for instance separator in the column name var instanceMetric = column.contains(INSTANCE_SEPARATOR); // Get instance keys from context or use empty array if not present var instanceKeys = context.getJsonArray(FILTER_KEYS, new JsonArray()); // Set default entity type to "all" if not specified if (!context.containsKey(ENTITY_TYPE)) { context.put(ENTITY_TYPE, "all"); } // Initialize plugin entities map with metric names for valid plugin IDs for (var pluginId : pluginIds) { if (MetricConfigStore.getStore().getMetricName(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId)) != null) { // Create mapping of plugin ID + metric name to set of entity IDs pluginEntities.computeIfAbsent(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId) + DASH_SEPARATOR + MetricConfigStore.getStore().getMetricName(CommonUtil.getInteger(pluginId)), value -> new HashSet<>()); } } // Filter entities based on groups, objects, and tags var items = filterEntities(context, userId, qualifiedObjects, filteredGroupEntities, filteredTagEntities, LOGGER, archived); // Process qualified items if they exist if (items != null && !items.isEmpty()) { // Initialize entity maps entities = new HashMap<>(); entityKeys = new HashMap<>(); // Special handling for instance-based metrics with keys or entity key building requirements if ((!instanceKeys.isEmpty() || buildEntityKey || (instanceEntityKey && !filteredTagEntities.isEmpty())) && instanceMetric) { // Remove availability plugin ID as it's handled separately if (pluginIds.contains(NMSConstants.AVAILABILITY_PLUGIN_ID)) { pluginIds.remove(NMSConstants.AVAILABILITY_PLUGIN_ID); // Availability plugin not needed for instance metrics } / Handle instance entity keys when result grouping and instance type are the same. This allows for more precise filtering by matching tag-based instances.

question: Show the pattern for: How does ShutdownUtil.checkShutdownFile() work?
answer:
Checks the shutdown file for the presence of shutdown signal and triggers application exit.

This private method is called periodically by the shutdown watcher to examine the shutdown file. It performs asynchronous file operations to: 1. Check if the shutdown file exists 2. Read the file content if it exists 3. Compare the content with the expected "shutdown" keyword 4. Trigger immediate application termination (System.exit(0)) if keyword matches 5. Log appropriate messages for different scenarios (file found, keyword match/mismatch)

The method uses Vert.x's asynchronous file system API with Future composition to handle file operations without blocking the event loop.

question: Show the pattern for: How does Bootstrap.deleteMetricAgentCacheFiles() work?
answer:
Hot swaps a verticle by undeploying and redeploying it without stopping the application.

This method performs a runtime replacement of a verticle by: 1. Undeploying the existing verticle instance using its class name 2. Creating a new instance of the same verticle class 3. Deploying the new instance with the same configuration

Hot swapping is useful for applying changes to a verticle's implementation without restarting the entire application, such as during development or when applying patches to a running system.

The method logs the hot swap operation and handles both successful and failed scenarios appropriately. @param clazz The class of the verticle to hot swap @return A Future that completes when the verticle has been successfully restarted, or fails with the cause if either undeployment or deployment fails / public static Future restartVerticle(Class clazz) { var promise = Promise.promise(); LOGGER.info("hot swapping " + clazz.getSimpleName()); undeployVerticle(clazz.getSimpleName()).onComplete(result -> { try { if (result.succeeded()) { LOGGER.info("starting engine " + clazz.getSimpleName()); startEngine(clazz.getConstructor().newInstance(), clazz.getSimpleName(), null).onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { promise.complete(); } else { promise.fail(asyncResult.cause()); } }); } else { promise.fail(result.cause()); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } }); return promise.future(); } / Cleans up metric agent cache files during application startup.

This method deletes the cache directory for non-agent bootstrap types to prevent false disk utilization warnings when the system restarts. The issue addressed is:

When a health agent reports disk utilization above 90% and the Motadata service is stopped, the cache folder retains this data. Upon restart, the agent might report disk utilization above 90% again based on this stale data, even if the actual disk utilization has changed.

By clearing the cache directory during startup (except for AGENT bootstrap type), the method ensures that disk utilization reports are based on fresh data rather than stale cached information.

This functionality was implemented as part of MOTADATA-970.

question: Show the pattern for: How does ObjectConfigStore.populateItemsByUser() work?
answer:
Populates the itemsByUser map with user IDs as keys and sets of object IDs as values. This method processes all provided users and maps each user to the objects that are accessible based on the user's group membership.

The itemsByUser map structure:

  • Key: User ID (Long)
  • Value: Set of object internal IDs (Set<Long>) that belong to the user's groups

Processing logic:

  • For the default user (ID = 1): Grants access to all objects in the system
  • For regular users: Retrieves the groups defined in the user's USER_GROUPS field
  • Uses {@link #getItemsByGroups(JsonArray)} to find all objects belonging to those groups
  • If objects are found, creates/updates the user's entry in the map
  • If no objects are found and the user exists in the map, clears the user's set

Special handling:

  • Default User: The default user (ID = 1) has unrestricted access to all objects, regardless of group membership
  • Empty Groups: Users with no groups assigned will have an empty set or cleared entry

This method is typically called during:

  • System initialization to build the initial user-to-object mappings
  • User updates when user group assignments change
  • Bulk refresh operations to rebuild the entire map

Note: This method processes all users at once. For single object updates

@param users a JsonArray containing user objects to process

question: How does FlowCacheProcessor.close() work?
answer:
The `close` method is responsible for safely closing the currently open file and deleting it from the file system once processing is complete.

## Execution Flow: 1. Check if a File is Open: - If `fileReader` is `null`, it means no file is currently being read, so the method does nothing. 2. Attempt to Close the File: - Calls `fileReader.close()` inside a `try` block to release system resources. - Logs a trace message indicating the file has been closed successfully. 3. Delete the File from the File System: - If `file` is not `null`, it retrieves its reference. - Uses Vert.x asynchronous file system API to delete the file. - Logs a success message if the file is deleted, or logs an error if deletion fails. 4. Exception Handling: - Catches any exceptions that may occur during file closing or deletion and logs the error. 5. Cleanup in the `finally` Block: - Ensures `fileReader` and `file` are set to `null` to free references and prevent accidental reuse.

question: Show the pattern for: How does LAMAIntegration.process() work?
answer:
Integration class for LAMA (Live Analytics and Monitoring Application) system.

This class provides comprehensive functionality to: - Send hardware, network, and database metrics to LAMA API endpoints - Handle authentication with member-based token management - Process different metrics types based on trade API endpoints - Manage separate sequence IDs for each metrics type (hardware, network, database) - Handle token expiration and automatic re-authentication - Process integration events from the event bus with proper error handling

The integration supports multiple metrics types: - Hardware Metrics: Client connectivity and performance data - Network Metrics: Interface traffic utilization and ping latency data - Database Metrics: MySQL replication status and queue size data

Key features: - Member-based token storage to reduce redundant authentication - Automatic token refresh on expiration (response codes 801/802) - Sequence ID error handling and correction (response code 704) - Robust error handling with detailed logging - Thread-safe operations using AtomicInteger for sequence management @author AI Assistant @since 16-Sep-2025 / public class LAMAIntegration extends AbstractVerticle { / Web client for HTTP requests / private final WebClient webClient = WebClientUtil.getWebClient(); / Event bus reply topic for LAMA integration / private final String REPLY_TOPIC = IntegrationType.LAMA.getName() + DOT_SEPARATOR + EVENT_INTEGRATION + EVENT_REPLY; / Member-based token storage (Member ID -> Token) / private final HashMap tokens = new HashMap<>(); / Profile interval storage (Profile ID -> Interval) / private final HashMap intervals = new HashMap<>(); / Separate sequence IDs for each metrics type - starts from 1 and increments for each request Using AtomicInteger for thread-safe operations in multithreaded environment / private final AtomicLong hardwareSequenceId = new AtomicLong(1); private final AtomicLong networkSequenceId = new AtomicLong(1); private final AtomicLong databaseSequenceId = new AtomicLong(1); / Each special day contains date, start time, end time, and remark / private final HashMap>> specialDays = new HashMap<>(); / Date formatter for parsing special day dates (dd-MM-yyyy format) / private final DateTimeFormatter DATE_FORMATTER = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("dd-MM-yyyy"); / Time formatter for parsing special day times (HH:mm format) / private final DateTimeFormatter TIME_FORMATTER = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm"); / Logger instance for LAMA integration operations / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(LAMAIntegration.class, INTEGRATION_DIR, "LAMA Integration"); private static final Pattern PATTERN_SEQUENCE = Pattern.compile("error : Invalid Sequence ID. The SequenceId should be (\\d+)", Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE); / Event engine for processing integration events / private EventEngine eventEngine; / Interval for relative timeline of query in minutes / private static final int INTERVAL = MotadataConfigUtil.getIntegrationLAMAIntervalMinutes(); / Starts the LAMA integration verticle and initializes the event engine. Sets up event processing for LAMA integration operations. @param promise Promise to complete when startup is finished @throws Exception if startup fails / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { var eventEnginePromise = Promise.promise(); eventEngine = new EventEngine() .setEventType(IntegrationType.LAMA.getName() + DOT_SEPARATOR + EVENT_INTEGRATION) .setEventQueueSize(MotadataConfigUtil.getIntegrationEventQueueSize()) .setBlockingEvent(true) .setLogger(LOGGER) .setEventHandler(this::process) .start(vertx, eventEnginePromise); eventEnginePromise.future().onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { var ids = new HashSet<>(); IntegrationConfigStore.getStore().getItems().forEach(result -> { var item = JsonObject.mapFrom(result); if (item.containsKey(INTEGRATION_TYPE) && IntegrationType.LAMA.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(item.getString(INTEGRATION_TYPE))) { item.mergeIn(item.getJsonObject(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT)).remove(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT); if (ids.add(item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_MEMBER_ID))) { login(item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_MEMBER_ID), item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_LOGIN_ID),item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_PASSWORD), item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SECRET_KEY), item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_AUTH_API), item.getLong(ID)).onComplete(results -> { if (results.succeeded()) { LOGGER.trace("LAMA token generated successfully for profile id: " + item.getLong(ID)); } else { LOGGER.warn("Failed to generate LAMA token for profile id: " + item.getLong(ID) + " because of : " + results.cause()); } }); } intervals.put(item.getLong(ID), CommonUtil.getLong(item.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_INTERVAL))); // Initialize special days configuration if present if (item.containsKey(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS)) { updateSpecialDays(item.getLong(ID), item.getJsonArray(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS)); } } }); vertx.setPeriodic(60 1000L, timer -> // Periodic Timer of 1 min for LAMA integration { // Use iterator to safely modify map during iteration and avoid redundant operations var iterator = intervals.entrySet().iterator(); while (iterator.hasNext()) { var entry = iterator.next(); var newValue = entry.getValue() - 1; if (newValue <= 0) { // Send event and remove from map Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().send(EVENT_LAMA_INTEGRATION, new JsonObject().put(ID, entry.getKey())); iterator.remove(); } else { entry.setValue(newValue); // Update the value } } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_CHANGE_NOTIFICATION, message -> { switch (ChangeNotificationType.valueOf(message.body().getString(CHANGE_NOTIFICATION_TYPE))) { case ADD_INTEGRATION_PROFILE, UPDATE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE -> { try { var event = message.body(); if (event.containsKey(ID) && event.getValue(ID) != null) { if (event.containsKey(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT)) { var context = event.getJsonObject(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT); login(context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_MEMBER_ID), context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_LOGIN_ID), context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_PASSWORD), context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SECRET_KEY), context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_AUTH_API), event.getLong(ID)).onComplete(result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { LOGGER.info("LAMA token generated successfully for profile id: " + event.getLong(ID)); } else { LOGGER.warn("Failed to generate LAMA token for profile id: " + event.getLong(ID) + " because of : " + result.cause()); } }); intervals.put(event.getLong(ID), CommonUtil.getLong(context.getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_INTERVAL))); // Handle special days configuration if (context.containsKey(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS) && context.getJsonArray(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS) != null && !context.getJsonArray(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS).isEmpty()) { updateSpecialDays(event.getLong(ID), context.getJsonArray(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_SPECIAL_DAYS)); } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } case DELETE_INTEGRATION_PROFILE -> { try { var event = message.body(); if (event.containsKey(ID) && event.getValue(ID) != null && event.containsKey(INTEGRATION_TYPE) && IntegrationType.LAMA.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(event.getString(INTEGRATION_TYPE))) { intervals.remove(event.getLong(ID)); removeSpecialDays(event.getLong(ID)); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } } }); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_LAMA_INTEGRATION, message -> { try { var event = message.body(); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("received event : %s", event.encode())); } var id = event.getLong(ID); var item = IntegrationConfigStore.getStore().getItem(id); if (item != null && !item.isEmpty()) { intervals.put(id, CommonUtil.getLong(item.getJsonObject(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getString(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_INTERVAL))); // Check if current time is within a special day period for this profile if (CommonUtil.validBusinessHour(item.getJsonObject(INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getLong(INTEGRATION_PROFILE_MONITOR_HOUR)) || isWithinSpecialDayPeriod(id)) { vertx.eventBus().send(IntegrationType.LAMA.getName() + DOT_SEPARATOR + EVENT_INTEGRATION, item); } else { LOGGER.trace(String.format("Skipping metrics collection for profile %d due to no valid business hour", event.getLong(ID))); } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); promise.complete(); } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResult.cause()); promise.fail(asyncResult.cause()); } }); } / Stops the LAMA integration verticle and shuts down the event engine. @param promise Promise to complete when shutdown is finished @throws Exception if shutdown fails / @Override public void stop(Promise promise) throws Exception { eventEngine.stop(vertx, promise); } / Processes integration events and sends metrics data to LAMA endpoints.

This method: 1. Extracts the trade API endpoint from the event 2. Determines the metrics type based on the endpoint: - metrics/application → Hardware metrics (getClientConnectivity) - metrics/hardware → Network metrics (getNetworkConnectivity) - metrics/network → Network metrics (getNetworkConnectivity) - metrics/database → Database metrics (getDatabaseMetrics) 3. Processes the metrics and sends them to LAMA 4. Updates the profile sync status and timestamps 5. Sends a response back to the event bus when processing is complete

The method handles various scenarios including: - Authentication token management and refresh - Sequence ID error handling and correction - Robust error handling with detailed logging - Member-based token sharing across profiles @param event The event object containing profile information for LAMA integration

question: How does SlackNotification.OK() work?
answer:
Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Slack notifications.

This class handles Slack notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Slack Web API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Slack channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Slack service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Slack API requests
  • Automatic image upload and attachment for messages with images

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Checks if image upload is required and handles file upload if needed
  6. Sends HTTP requests to the Slack API for each channel
  7. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  8. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding
  • {@code imageAttached} (optional): Boolean flag indicating if image upload is required

The message content is provided as a complete Slack Block Kit JSON template from the PolicyEngine, with all variables already substituted. This class simply adds the channel information and sends the message to the Slack API.

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is experiencing issues. / public class SlackNotification extends Notification { / Logger for Slack notification operations / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(SlackNotification.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_NOTIFICATION, "Slack Notification"); / Circuit breaker to handle Slack service failures.

The circuit breaker:

  • Opens after 5 consecutive failures
  • Considers a request failed if it takes more than 30 seconds
  • Stays open for 60 seconds before attempting to reset
  • Tracks failures over a 30-minute rolling window
  • Calls the fallback handler when open
/ private final CircuitBreaker circuitBreaker = CircuitBreaker.create("slack-service-circuit-breaker", Bootstrap.vertx(), new CircuitBreakerOptions() .setMaxFailures(5) // number of failure before opening the circuit .setTimeout(30000) // consider a failure if the operation does not succeed in time .setFallbackOnFailure(true) // do we call the fallback on failure .setResetTimeout(60000) // time spent in open state before attempting to re-try .setFailuresRollingWindow(TimeUnit.MINUTES.toMillis(30)) ).openHandler(handler -> LOGGER.warn(ErrorMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_FAILED)).closeHandler(handler -> LOGGER.info(InfoMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_RESTORED)).fallback(handler -> handler.initCause(new Exception(ErrorMessageConstants.SLACK_SERVICE_FAILED))); / Processes and sends Slack notifications based on the provided event data.

This method orchestrates the entire Slack notification workflow:

  • Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the store
  • Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  • Processes each channel in parallel using futures
  • Applies severity-based color coding to message content
  • Handles image upload if required by the message payload
  • Sends messages to Slack API with proper authentication
  • Tracks successful deliveries and handles failures

The method uses circuit breaker protection to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is unavailable or experiencing issues. @param event A JsonObject containing the Slack notification parameters:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS} - JSON array of channel IDs
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT} - Message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} - Severity level for color coding (optional)
  • {@code imageAttached} - Boolean flag for image upload (optional)
@return A Promise that resolves to a JsonObject containing the result of the Slack notification attempt with the following structure:
  • {@link GlobalConstants#STATUS} - Status of the operation ({@link GlobalConstants#STATUS_SUCCEED} or {@link GlobalConstants#STATUS_FAIL})
  • {@link GlobalConstants#ERROR_CODE} - Error code indicating success or failure type
  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#RECIPIENTS} - List of successfully notified channel IDs
  • {@link GlobalConstants#MESSAGE} - Error message if operation failed
  • {@link GlobalConstants#ERROR} - Stack trace if operation failed
@throws Exception If any unexpected error occurs during notification processing / @Override public Promise notify(JsonObject event) { var promise = Promise.promise(); // Retrieve Slack integration configuration from the store var slack = IntegrationConfigStore.getStore().getItemsByValue( Integration.INTEGRATION_TYPE, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationType.SLACK.getName() ).getJsonObject(0); // Execute the Slack sending logic with circuit breaker protection circuitBreaker.execute(future -> { try { var futures = new ArrayList>(); var recipients = new ArrayList(); if (event.containsKey(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS) && event.getJsonArray(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS) != null && slack != null) { var channels = event.getJsonArray(PolicyEngineConstants.CHANNELS); // Process each channel in parallel channels.forEach(channel -> { var result = Promise.promise(); futures.add(result.future()); var item = IntegrationProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(Long.parseLong(channel.toString())); if (item != null) { // Get the channel context and build the Slack API URL var context = item.getJsonObject(IntegrationProfile.INTEGRATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT); var url = slack.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getString(GlobalConstants.TARGET, EMPTY_VALUE) + SLACK_MESSAGE_END_POINT; var credentialProfile = CredentialProfileConfigStore.getStore().getItem(slack.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getLong(IntegrationProfile.INTEGRATION_CREDENTIAL_PROFILE)); var content = EMPTY_VALUE; if (event.containsKey(SEVERITY) && !event.getString(SEVERITY).isEmpty()) { content = new StringSubstitutor(new JsonObject().put(SEVERITY_COLOR, SlackColorCode.valueOf((event.getString(SEVERITY).toUpperCase())).getColorCode()).getMap()).replace(event.getString(Notification.CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT)); } else { content = event.getString(Notification.CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT); } var payload = new JsonObject(content).put("channel", context.getString(CHANNEL, EMPTY_VALUE)); var imageAttached = payload.getBoolean("imageAttached", false); var imagePayload = new JsonObject(); if(imageAttached) { imagePayload.put("image_url", payload.getValue("image_url")).put("alt_text", payload.getValue("alt_text")); payload.remove("image_url"); payload.remove("alt_text"); payload.remove("imageAttached"); } WebClientUtil.getWebClient().postAbs(url) .putHeader("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8") .timeout(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(slack.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).getLong(GlobalConstants.TIMEOUT, 60L))) .bearerTokenAuthentication(credentialProfile.getJsonObject(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_CONTEXT).getString("access_token")) .sendJson(payload) .onComplete(asyncResponse -> { if (asyncResponse.succeeded()) { var httpResponse = asyncResponse.result(); if (httpResponse.statusCode() == HttpStatus.SC_OK) { var responseBody = httpResponse.bodyAsJsonObject(); if (responseBody.getBoolean("ok", false)) { if(imageAttached) { uploadImage(imagePayload.getString("image_url"), imagePayload.getString("alt_text", "uploaded-image"), credentialProfile.getJsonObject(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_CONTEXT).getString("access_token"), payload.getString("channel")) .onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { recipients.add(channel.toString()); result.complete(); } else { LOGGER.warn("Image upload failed: " + asyncResult.cause()); promise.fail("Image upload failed: " + asyncResult.cause()); } }); } else { recipients.add(channel.toString()); result.complete(); } } else { var error = responseBody.getString("error", "Unknown error"); LOGGER.warn(responseBody.encodePrettily()); result.fail(String.format("Slack API error: %s", error)); } } else { LOGGER.warn(String.format("invalid status code received in sending message : %s", httpResponse.statusCode())); result.fail(String.format("invalid status code received in sending message : %s", httpResponse.statusCode())); } } else { LOGGER.error(asyncResponse.cause()); result.fail(asyncResponse.cause()); } }); } }); return promise; } / Uploads an image file to Slack using the external upload API and returns the file ID.

This method orchestrates the complete image upload process to Slack in three sequential steps:

  1. Retrieves an upload URL from Slack's {@code files.getUploadURLExternal} API
  2. Uploads the binary file data to the obtained upload URL
  3. Completes the upload process using Slack's {@code files.completeUploadExternal} API

The method handles the entire file upload workflow including:

  • Constructing the file path from the uploads directory
  • Calculating file size for the upload request
  • Generating a filename with PNG extension using the provided alt text
  • Managing the asynchronous upload sequence with proper error handling
  • Providing detailed logging for each step of the upload process

The uploaded image can then be referenced in Slack messages using the returned file ID. @param image The filename of the image to upload, located in the uploads directory @param fileName The alternative text description for the image, used for accessibility and as the basis for the uploaded filename @param accessToken The Slack OAuth access token for authenticating API requests @return A Future that resolves to the Slack file ID string if the upload is successful, or fails with an error message if any step in the upload process fails @throws Exception If the image file cannot be read or accessed, or if any network or API error occurs during the upload process @see #getUploadURL(String, long, String) For the first step of obtaining upload URL @see #uploadFileBinary(String, String, String) For the binary upload step @see #completeFileUpload(String, String, String) For finalizing the upload process @since 1.0 / private Future uploadImage(String image, String fileName, String accessToken, String channel) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { var filePath = GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "uploads" + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + image; getUploadURL(fileName + ".png", Files.size(Paths.get(filePath)), accessToken) .compose(result -> uploadFileBinary(result.getString("upload_url"), filePath, result.getString("file_id"))) .compose(fileId -> completeFileUpload(fileId, accessToken, channel)) .onComplete(asyncResult -> { if (asyncResult.succeeded()) { LOGGER.info("Image uploaded successfully. File ID: " + asyncResult.result()); promise.complete(asyncResult.result()); } else { LOGGER.warn("Image upload failed: " + asyncResult.cause()); promise.fail(asyncResult.cause()); } }); } catch (Exception e) { LOGGER.warn("Error processing image upload: " + e.getMessage()); promise.fail("Error reading image file: " + e.getMessage()); } return promise.future(); } private Future getUploadURL(String filename, long fileSize, String accessToken) { Promise promise = Promise.promise(); WebClientUtil.getWebClient().postAbs("https://slack.com/api/files.getUploadURLExternal") .putHeader("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken) .putHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded") .sendForm(MultiMap.caseInsensitiveMultiMap() .add("filename", filename) .add("length", String.valueOf(fileSize))) .onComplete(uploadUrlResult -> { if (uploadUrlResult.succeeded() && uploadUrlResult.result().statusCode() == HttpStatus.SC_OK) { var response = uploadUrlResult.result().bodyAsJsonObject(); if (response.getBoolean("ok", false)) { LOGGER.info("get uploaded URL" + uploadUrlResult.result().body()); promise.complete(response); } else { LOGGER.warn("Slack uploaded URL failed: " + uploadUrlResult.cause()); promise.fail("Slack upload URL error: " + response.getString("error", "Unknown error")); } } else { LOGGER.warn("Upload failed: " + uploadUrlResult.cause()); promise.fail("Get upload URL failed: " + (uploadUrlResult.succeeded() ? "HTTP " + uploadUrlResult.result().statusCode() : uploadUrlResult.cause().getMessage())); } }); return promise.future(); } private Future uploadFileBinary(String uploadUrl, String filePath, String fileId) { Promise promise = Promise.promise(); try { WebClientUtil.getWebClient().postAbs(uploadUrl) .putHeader("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream") .sendBuffer(Buffer.buffer(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(filePath)))) .onComplete(uploadResult -> { if (uploadResult.succeeded() && uploadResult.result().statusCode() == HttpStatus.SC_OK) { LOGGER.info("File binary uploaded successfully to URL: " + uploadUrl); promise.complete(fileId); } else { LOGGER.warn("File binary upload failed: " + uploadResult.cause()); promise.fail("File binary upload failed: " + (uploadResult.succeeded() ? "HTTP " + uploadResult.result().statusCode() : uploadResult.cause().getMessage())); } }); } catch (Exception e) { LOGGER.fatal("Error processing file binary: " + e.getMessage()); promise.fail("Error reading file bytes: " + e.getMessage()); } return promise.future(); } private Future completeFileUpload(String fileId, String accessToken, String channel) { Promise promise = Promise.promise(); WebClientUtil.getWebClient().postAbs("https://slack.com/api/files.completeUploadExternal") .putHeader("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken) .putHeader("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8") .sendJsonObject(new JsonObject() .put("channel_id", channel) .put("files", new JsonArray().add(new JsonObject().put("id", fileId))) ).onComplete(completeResult -> { if (completeResult.succeeded() && completeResult.result().statusCode() == HttpStatus.SC_OK) { var response = completeResult.result().bodyAsJsonObject(); if (response.getBoolean("ok", false)) { LOGGER.info("File complete upload completed successfully. File ID: " + fileId); promise.complete(response.getJsonArray("files").getJsonObject(0).getString("id")); } else { LOGGER.warn("File upload failed: " + completeResult.cause()); promise.fail("Complete upload error: " + response.getString("error", "Unknown error")); } } else { LOGGER.warn("Complete upload failed: " + completeResult.cause()); promise.fail("Complete upload failed: " + (completeResult.succeeded() ? "HTTP " + completeResult.result().statusCode() : completeResult.cause().getMessage())); } }); return promise.future(); } / Enumeration of color codes used for Slack message attachments based on severity.

question: Show the pattern for: How does TransportProvider.getClient() work?
answer:
Creates and returns a transport client implementation based on the provided configuration.

This factory method examines the configuration to determine which transport client implementation to instantiate. The transport protocol is specified in the configuration using the {@link EventBusConstants#TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL} key.

Currently supported transport client implementations:

  • {@link ZMQClient} - For ZeroMQ transport protocol

The method also checks for the {@link EventBusConstants#AUTO_RECONNECT} flag in the configuration. If set to true, the returned client will be wrapped in an {@link TransportReconnectClient} to provide automatic reconnection capabilities.

The configuration object should contain all necessary parameters for the specific transport implementation, such as:

  • Host address to connect to
  • Port number
  • Socket mode (SUB, PUSH, etc.)
  • Protocol-specific options (high water mark, etc.)

question: What does the DiscoveryEngine class do?
answer:
The DiscoveryEngine class is responsible for managing discovery operations within the Motadata platform. It extends the AbstractVerticle class provided by Vert.x to enable asynchronous and concurrent event-driven behavior.

Key Responsibilities: - Handles discovery-related events such as discovery run and completion. - Manages worker executors for executing discovery tasks. - Tracks discovery events and idle worker statuses by discovery profile. - Publishes updates and notifications to the event bus for UI and other system components.

Internal Components: - workerExecutor: A shared worker executor for performing discovery-related tasks asynchronously. - discoveryEvents: A map that tracks discovery events corresponding to different discovery profiles. - idleWorkersByDiscovery: A map that tracks idle worker count for each running discovery profile. - eventProbes: An integer that represents the number of probes related to events (internal usage). - timeHandlerActive: A flag to indicate whether a time handler is currently active.

Event Bus Consumers: 1. EVENT_ENGINE_STATS: Responds to requests for engine statistics such as pending events and idle workers. 2. EVENT_DISCOVERY_RUN: Handles events to initiate discovery process for specified discovery profiles. Coordinates with other system components for event routing and notification handling. 3. EVENT_DISCOVERY_COMPLETE: Processes completion of a discovery process. Handles tasks such as mapping previous results, saving discovery outcomes, and cleaning up old results.

Error Handling: - Errors and exceptions encountered during the discovery process are logged and propagated to appropriate event handlers for further processing. - Notifications for failed or incomplete discovery executions are sent to the event bus for UI updates or retry mechanisms.

System Interactions: - Publishes notifications about discovery state changes to the UI and other components. - Interacts with the system's configuration stores (e.g., DiscoveryConfigStore, DiscoveryCacheStore) for retrieving and updating discovery configurations and metadata. - Handles health statistics publishing and monitoring for scheduled or manually triggered tasks.

question: Show the pattern for: How does MetricPolicyFlapDurationCacheStore.update() work?
answer:
Initializes the cache store by loading policy status data from the event bus.

This method sends a request to the metric policy trigger duration query event bus address and populates the cache with the received data. It handles any exceptions that might occur during initialization. @return A Future that completes when initialization is done or fails with an exception / @Override public Future initStore() { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { // Clear existing data before initialization flaps.clear(); // Request policy status data from the event bus Bootstrap.vertx().eventBus().request( EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLICY_TRIGGER_DURATION_QUERY, new JsonObject(), reply -> { if (reply.succeeded()) { try { // Process the reply and populate the cache var body = reply.result().body(); if (body != null) { body.getMap().forEach((key, value) -> { if (key != null && value instanceof JsonObject) { // Convert JsonObject to ConcurrentHashMap and cache it flaps.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new ConcurrentHashMap<>()).putAll(setFlapContext((JsonObject) value)); // Cache the duration value separately for quicker access flapDurations.put(key, ((JsonObject) value).getInteger(PolicyEngineConstants.DURATION)); } }); } LOGGER.info("Metric Policy Flap Duration Cache Store initialized successfully with " + flaps.size() + " entries"); promise.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } } else { LOGGER.error(reply.cause()); promise.fail(reply.cause()); } }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } return promise.future(); } / Extracts and structures essential policy status fields from the input JSON object.

This method creates a thread-safe map containing key policy data such as trigger ticks, timestamps, durations, acknowledgments, and notes. Default values are used if any field is missing to ensure consistency and avoid nulls. @param flapContext The source JSON object containing policy status information @return A thread-safe map (ConcurrentHashMap) with extracted and normalized policy fields / private ConcurrentHashMap setFlapContext(JsonObject flapContext) { var context = new ConcurrentHashMap(); context.put(POLICY_FIRST_TRIGGER_TICK, flapContext.getLong(POLICY_FIRST_TRIGGER_TICK, 0L)); context.put(NMSConstants.PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, flapContext.getLong(NMSConstants.PREVIOUS_FLAP_TIMESTAMP, 0L)); context.put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TIMESTAMP, flapContext.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TIMESTAMP, 0L)); context.put(DURATION, flapContext.getInteger(DURATION, 0)); context.put(GlobalConstants.SEVERITY, flapContext.getString(GlobalConstants.SEVERITY)); context.put(POLICY_NOTE, flapContext.getString(POLICY_NOTE, GlobalConstants.EMPTY_VALUE)); context.put(POLICY_ACKNOWLEDGE, flapContext.getString(POLICY_ACKNOWLEDGE, GlobalConstants.EMPTY_VALUE)); return context; } / Updates the policy status for a given key.
