Deploys a standard (non-worker) verticle in the Vert.x environment.

This method: 1. Checks if the verticle should be deployed based on the current bootstrap type 2. Verifies that the verticle hasn't already been deployed 3. Deploys the verticle with standard (non-worker) deployment options 4. Tracks the deployment ID in the deployedVerticles map

The method is used for verticles that perform non-blocking operations and should run on the Vert.x event loop threads. @param verticle The AbstractVerticle instance to deploy @param name A unique name for the verticle (used for logging and tracking) @param bootstrapType The bootstrap type for which this verticle should be deployed, or null to deploy regardless of bootstrap type @return A Future that completes when the verticle is deployed, or fails with the cause of deployment failure / public static Future startEngine(AbstractVerticle verticle, String name, GlobalConstants.BootstrapType bootstrapType) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { if (bootstrapType == null || bootstrapType != Bootstrap.bootstrapType()) { if (!DEPLOYED_VERTICLES.containsKey(name)) { VERTX.deployVerticle(verticle, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { DEPLOYED_VERTICLES.put(name, result.result()); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s started successfully...", name)); promise.complete(); } else { LOGGER.fatal(String.format("failed to start %s...", name)); promise.fail(result.cause()); } }); } else { LOGGER.info(String.format("%s is already deployed...", name)); promise.complete(); } } else { promise.complete(); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception.getCause()); } return promise.future(); } / Deploys a worker verticle in the Vert.x environment.

This method: 1. Checks if the verticle should be deployed based on the current bootstrap type 2. Verifies that the verticle hasn't already been deployed 3. Deploys the verticle with worker deployment options (multi-threaded worker) 4. Tracks the deployment ID in the deployedVerticles map

Worker verticles are used for operations that might block the event loop, such as CPU-intensive tasks or blocking I/O operations. They run on dedicated worker threads rather than the Vert.x event loop threads. @param verticle The AbstractVerticle instance to deploy as a worker @param name A unique name for the verticle (used for logging and tracking) @param bootstrapType The bootstrap type for which this verticle should be deployed, or null to deploy regardless of bootstrap type @return A Future that completes when the verticle is deployed, or fails with the cause of deployment failure / public static Future startWorkerEngine(AbstractVerticle verticle, String name, GlobalConstants.BootstrapType bootstrapType) { var promise = Promise.promise(); try { if (bootstrapType == null || bootstrapType != Bootstrap.bootstrapType()) { if (!DEPLOYED_VERTICLES.containsKey(name)) { VERTX.deployVerticle(verticle, new DeploymentOptions().setThreadingModel(ThreadingModel.WORKER).setWorkerPoolSize(1).setWorkerPoolName("wp." + name), result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { DEPLOYED_VERTICLES.put(name, result.result()); LOGGER.info(String.format("%s started successfully...", name)); promise.complete(); } else { LOGGER.fatal(String.format("failed to start %s...", name)); promise.fail(result.cause()); } }); } else { LOGGER.info(String.format("%s is already deployed...", name)); promise.complete(); } } else { promise.complete(); } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception.getCause()); } return promise.future(); } / Deploys a standard (non-worker) verticle in the Vert.x environment with event type configuration.

This method: 1. Checks if the verticle should be deployed based on the current bootstrap type 2. Verifies that the verticle hasn't already been deployed 3. Deploys the verticle with standard (non-worker) deployment options and event type configuration 4. Tracks the deployment ID in the deployedVerticles map

This method retrieves and logs various system attributes through JMX, including: - Operating system name and version - System architecture - Available processors - Memory usage (committed, free physical, free swap) - File descriptor counts - CPU load and time - Total memory and swap space

The information is collected using the platform MBean server and the OperatingSystem MBean, then formatted and logged at INFO level. This is useful for troubleshooting performance issues and understanding the environment in which the application is running.

question: Show the pattern for: How does FlowProcessor.decodeIP() work?
answer:
Decodes an IP address and enriches the flow data with geolocation and AS information.

This method takes an IP address and enriches the flow data with additional information:

  • Geolocation information (country, city, latitude, longitude)
  • Autonomous System (AS) information
  • Domain information if available

The method uses a Bloom filter to avoid redundant lookups for IP addresses that have already been processed, improving performance for high-volume flow processing. @param ipAddress the IP address to decode @param flow the flow data to enrich with decoded information @param flowType the type of flow (source or destination)

question: What does the APIServer class do?
answer:
Creates a new SSO user in the system if they don't already exist. This method is called during SSO authentication to ensure the SSO user has a corresponding local user account.

The method performs the following: 1. Retrieves username from ActiveUserCacheStore using the provided ID
2. Checks if user already exists in UserConfigStore
3. If user doesn't exist:
- Creates new user with SSO user type
- Sets default read-only role and empty preferences
- Saves to database and updates UserConfigStore

question: What does the TransportReconnectClient class do?
answer:
A decorator for TransportClient that provides automatic reconnection capabilities.

This class implements the TransportClient interface and wraps another TransportClient implementation, adding automatic reconnection functionality. It periodically checks the connection status and attempts to reconnect if the connection has been idle for longer than the configured timeout period.

Key features:

  • Transparent delegation to the underlying transport client
  • Periodic connection health checks
  • Automatic reconnection when connection is lost
  • Connection timeout based on message activity
  • Port availability verification before reconnection attempts

The reconnection logic works by:

  1. Tracking the timestamp of the last received message
  2. Periodically checking if the time since the last message exceeds the timeout
  3. Verifying that the remote endpoint is reachable
  4. Closing the existing connection and establishing a new one

Example usage:

{@code   // Create a base transport client   TransportClient baseClient = new ZMQClient(config);     // Wrap it with auto-reconnect functionality   TransportClient client = new AutoReconnectClient(baseClient, config);     // Use the client normally - reconnection is handled automatically   client.connect();   client.registerMessageHandler(message -> {       // Process message   });   client.receive();   }

Alternatively, use the TransportProvider factory method:

{@code   // Create a client with auto-reconnect enabled   JsonObject config = new JsonObject()       .put(TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL, TransportProtocol.ZMQ.getValue())       .put(AUTO_RECONNECT, true)       .put("host", "localhost")       .put("port", 5555);   TransportClient client = TransportProvider.getClient(config);   }
@author Motadata Engineering Team @version 1.0 @since 1.0 @see TransportClient @see TransportProvider @see ZMQClient

question: Show the pattern for: How does ServiceNowIntegration.syncAttributes() work?
answer:
Synchronizes ServiceNow attributes with the local system.

This method: 1. Ensures only one synchronization job runs at a time using the RUNNING flag 2. Retrieves credential information for authentication 3. Constructs the base URL for ServiceNow API calls 4. Initiates parallel synchronization of different attribute types: - Categories and subcategories - Services - Technicians - Impact levels - Urgency levels 5. Updates the integration configuration in the database when all synchronizations complete

The method uses a Future.join pattern to run all synchronization tasks in parallel and update the database only when all tasks have completed.

question: How does FlowStatCalculator.merge() work?
answer:
FlowStatCalculator is responsible for collecting, aggregating, and reporting flow statistics from network flow data processing.

Key responsibilities: - Collecting flow statistics from pmacct (NetFlow/sFlow accounting daemon) - Aggregating flow data from multiple FlowProcessor instances - Calculating per-second flow rates and volume metrics - Writing flow statistics to the datastore for visualization and analysis - Handling remote flow statistics from collector instances - Managing column mappers for datastore schema

The calculator operates in two modes: 1. APP mode: Receives aggregated stats from collectors and writes to datastore 2. COLLECTOR mode: Fetches raw pmacct data and sends to APP instance

/ public class FlowStatCalculator extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(FlowStatCalculator.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_FLOW, "Flow Stat Calculator"); / Timer interval (in seconds) for flushing flow statistics Default: 2 min/ private static final int FLOW_STAT_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS = MotadataConfigUtil.getFlowStatFlushTimerSeconds(); / Map storing per-source flow statistics [count, volume_bytes] / private final Map stats = new HashMap<>(); / StringBuilder for building column mapper strings efficiently / private final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder(0); / Set of column mappers to track datastore schema changes / private Set mappers; / Total aggregated flow events count / private long events = 0L; / Total aggregated flow volume in bytes / private long eventVolumeBytes = 0L; / Reusable JsonObject for event data to reduce object allocation / private final JsonObject event = new JsonObject(); / Path to NetFlow pmacct daemon pipe / private static final String NFACCTD_PIPE_PATH = GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "NetFlow.pipe"; / Path to sFlow pmacct daemon pipe / private static final String SFACCTD_PIPE_PATH = GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + "sFlow.pipe"; / Total flows processed from pmacct output (used for EPS calculation) / private final AtomicLong totalFlowsProcessed = new AtomicLong(0); / Initializes the FlowStatCalculator verticle.

This method: 1. Sets up event bus consumers for flow statistics from processors and remote collectors 2. Starts periodic timer for fetching pmacct data and writing statistics 3. Configures different behavior based on bootstrap type (APP vs COLLECTOR)

In APP mode: Receives aggregated stats from collectors and writes to datastore In COLLECTOR mode: Fetches raw pmacct data and sends to APP instance @param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done @throws Exception If an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise promise) throws Exception { // Initialize column mappers set for datastore schema tracking mappers = new HashSet<>(); LOGGER.info("Starting pmacct License Monitor"); // Set up periodic timer to fetch pmacct data and process statistics vertx.setPeriodic(FLOW_STAT_FLUSH_TIMER_SECONDS 1000L, h -> fetch()); // Configure APP mode behavior - receives stats from remote collectors if(Bootstrap.bootstrapType().name().equalsIgnoreCase(BootstrapType.APP.name())) { // Consumer for remote flow statistics from collector instances vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_FLOW_REMOTE_STAT, message -> { var item = message.body(); if(item != null && item.containsKey(TOTAL_FLOWS)) { // Track total flows for EPS calculation totalFlowsProcessed.addAndGet(item.getLong(TOTAL_FLOWS)); if(CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace("Event Received from Collector, Merging Data... " + totalFlowsProcessed); } } }); } // Consumer for local flow processor statistics vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_FLOW_PROCESSOR_STAT, message -> { var item = message.body(); if(item != null) { // Merge statistics from local flow processors merge(item.getJsonObject(RESULT)); // Aggregate flow counts and volume bytes if(item.getLong(AGGREGATED_FLOWS) != null && item.getLong(AGGREGATED_VOLUME_BYTES) != null) { events+= item.getLong(AGGREGATED_FLOWS); eventVolumeBytes += item.getLong(AGGREGATED_VOLUME_BYTES); if(CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace("Flow Processor Stats Collected..."); } } } }); promise.complete(); } / Merges incoming stats map into the local stats map. For each source, the count and volume values are added to existing totals. Uses compute() method for thread-safe atomic updates. @param stats JsonObject containing per-source statistics to merge

answer:
Calculates rate metrics (changes over time) for counter-type metrics.

This method: 1. Retrieves the previous value and timestamp for the metric 2. Calculates the time difference between the current and previous measurements 3. Calculates the rate (change per second) based on the value difference and time difference 4. Handles counter resets (when the current value is less than the previous value) 5. Stores the calculated rate in the rateMetrics JsonObject 6. Updates the context map with the current value and timestamp for future calculations

question: Show the pattern for: How does AgentManager.run() work?
answer:
The AgentManager class is responsible for managing agent operations and communication.

This verticle handles various agent management tasks including:

  • Agent discovery and rediscovery operations
  • Polling agents for data
  • Running commands on agents
  • Sending configuration updates to agents
  • Managing agent log uploads and downloads
  • Handling secure communication with agents

The AgentManager acts as a bridge between the Motadata system and the distributed agents, facilitating command execution, data collection, and configuration management. It ensures secure and reliable communication with agents across the network.

This class works closely with other components in the agent package, particularly AgentEventProcessor, to provide comprehensive agent management capabilities. / public class AgentManager extends AbstractVerticle { / Logger for this class / private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(AgentManager.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_AGENT, "Agent Manager", true); / Initializes the AgentManager verticle and sets up event bus consumers for agent operations.

This method configures multiple event bus consumers to handle different types of agent operations:

  • Agent log upload and download
  • Remote command execution and communication
  • Agent discovery and rediscovery
  • Polling agents for data
  • Running commands on agents
  • Sending configuration updates to agents

Each consumer is responsible for handling a specific type of agent operation and communicating with the appropriate agent(s) to execute the operation. @param promise Promise to be completed when initialization is done / @Override public void start(Promise promise) { try { var cipherUtil = new CipherUtil(); var form = MultipartForm.create() .binaryFileUpload("zip", AgentConstants.AGENT_COMPRESSED_LOG, GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + AgentConstants.AGENT_COMPRESSED_LOG, "agent-logs " + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + " zip"); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_UPLOAD_LOG, message -> { var event = message.body(); var host = event.getString(HOST); try { WebClientUtil.getWebClient().post(AgentConfigUtil.getAgentHTTPServerPort(), host, "/upload") .putHeader("content-type", "multipart/form-data") .putHeader(HttpHeaders.COOKIE.toString(), APIConstants.COOKIE) .sendMultipartForm(form, result -> { if (result.succeeded()) { vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT + DOT_SEPARATOR + host, event.put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_DOWNLOAD_LOG) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)) .put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()).put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_SUCCEED) .put(GlobalConstants.FILE_NAME, result.result().bodyAsJsonObject().getString(GlobalConstants.FILE_NAME)) .put(GlobalConstants.RESULT, result.result().bodyAsJsonObject().getString(GlobalConstants.RESULT))); } else { LOGGER.error(result.cause()); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT + DOT_SEPARATOR + host, event.put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_DOWNLOAD_LOG).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)) .put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()).put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL).put(GlobalConstants.MESSAGE, result.cause().getMessage()).put(GlobalConstants.ERROR, CommonUtil.formatStackTrace(result.cause().getStackTrace()))); } vertx.fileSystem().deleteBlocking(GlobalConstants.CURRENT_DIR + GlobalConstants.PATH_SEPARATOR + AgentConstants.AGENT_COMPRESSED_LOG); }); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT + DOT_SEPARATOR + host, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_DOWNLOAD_LOG).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)) .put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()).put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL).put(GlobalConstants.MESSAGE, exception.getCause().getMessage()).put(GlobalConstants.ERROR, exception.getCause().getMessage())); } }).exceptionHandler(LOGGER::error); vertx.eventBus().localConsumer(EventBusConstants.EVENT_REMOTE, message -> { try { var buffer = Buffer.buffer(message.body()); var topic = buffer.getString(2, buffer.getShortLE(0) + 2); //skipping motadata -> agent manager events if (message.body() != null && topic.contains(EventBusConstants.AGENT_TOPIC) && !topic.contains(EventBusConstants.MOTADATA_MANAGER_TOPIC)) { var event = CodecUtil.toJSONObject(cipherUtil.decrypt(buffer.getBytes(2 + buffer.getShortLE(0), buffer.length()))); if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled()) { LOGGER.trace(String.format("Received event on topic %s: %s", topic, event.encodePrettily())); } var host = event.getString(HOST, EMPTY_VALUE); switch (event.getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE)) { case EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_RESTART -> { var agent = event.getString(AgentConstants.AGENT_TYPE); if (agent != null && ProcessUtil.stop(agent)) { // only start agent if agent.status is yes if (AgentConfigUtil.getAgentEnableStatus(agent + ".agent.status").equalsIgnoreCase(GlobalConstants.YES)) { ProcessUtil.start(agent, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_RESTART); if (agent.equalsIgnoreCase(AgentConstants.Agent.LOG.getName())) { ProcessUtil.start(AgentConstants.Agent.WINDOWS_EVENT_LOG.getName(), EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_RESTART); } } } else { vertx.eventBus().publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT, new JsonObject().put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL).put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_RESTART) .put(AgentConstants.AGENT_TYPE, agent) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)).put(GlobalConstants.MESSAGE, String.format("Failed to stop agent %s, reason : agent not found", agent))); } } // If received message of unknown agent then register again case EventBusConstants.EVENT_UNKNOWN -> EventBusConstants.registerAgent(host); case EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_CONFIGURATION_CHANGE -> { var status = false; if (event.getString(Agent.AGENT_CONFIGS) != null) { status = CommonUtil.dumpConfigs(Agent.AGENT_FILE, new JsonObject(event.getString(Agent.AGENT_CONFIGS))); } // will create properties file for trace services var configs = new JsonObject(event.getString(Agent.AGENT_CONFIGS)); if (configs.containsKey(Agent.AGENT_TRACE)) { for (var key : configs.getJsonObject(Agent.AGENT_TRACE).getMap().keySet()) { try { AgentConstants.dumpPropertyFile(CURRENT_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR + CONFIG_DIR + PATH_SEPARATOR + key + ".properties", configs.getJsonObject(Agent.AGENT_TRACE).getJsonObject(key).put("otel.service.name", key).mergeIn(TraceConstants.SERVICE_DEFAULT_PROPERTIES), LOGGER); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } } } // Will send agent configuration update message to server if (status) { vertx.eventBus().publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT, event.put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_SUCCEED).put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_CONFIGURATION_CHANGE) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)).put(Agent.AGENT_CONFIGS, event.getString(Agent.AGENT_CONFIGS))); } else { vertx.eventBus().publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT, event.put(GlobalConstants.STATUS, GlobalConstants.STATUS_FAIL).put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()).put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_CONFIGURATION_CHANGE) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID)).put(GlobalConstants.MESSAGE, "Failed to update agent configuration")); } } case EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_HEARTBEAT -> { vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT + DOT_SEPARATOR + host, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT).put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID))); } case EventBusConstants.EVENT_LICENSE_UPDATE -> LicenseUtil.load(event.getJsonObject(EventBusConstants.EVENT)); case EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT_DOWNLOAD_LOG -> { LOGGER.info("downloading log files started....."); vertx.executeBlocking(future -> { LogUtil.zipLogFiles(event); future.complete(); }, result -> { }); } default -> { //do nothing } } if (!OS_AIX) { var acknowledge = true; switch (event.getString(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE)) { case EventBusConstants.EVENT_DISCOVERY -> discover(event); case EventBusConstants.EVENT_METRIC_POLL -> poll(event); case EventBusConstants.EVENT_REDISCOVER -> rediscover(event); case EventBusConstants.EVENT_PLUGIN_ENGINE -> run(event); default -> acknowledge = false; } if (acknowledge) { vertx.eventBus().send(EventBusConstants.EVENT_AGENT + DOT_SEPARATOR + host, new JsonObject().put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_TYPE, EventBusConstants.EVENT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT).put(Agent.AGENT_UUID, BootstrapAgent.getAgentUUID()) .put(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID))); EventBusConstants.updateEvent(event.getLong(EventBusConstants.EVENT_ID), String.format(InfoMessageConstants.EVENT_TRACKER_EVENT_QUALIFIED, DateTimeUtil.timestamp()), null, host); } } } } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); } }); promise.complete(); } catch (Exception exception) { LOGGER.error(exception); promise.fail(exception); } } / Executes plugin engine requests on agents.

It supports both streaming and non-streaming modes:

question: How does CommonUtil.setFilePermissions() work?
answer:
Sets POSIX file permissions on a file for non-Windows systems.

This method applies POSIX-style permissions to a file using the Java NIO Files API. The permissions string should be in the format used by the chmod command, such as "rwxr-xr--" (owner: read/write/execute, group: read/execute, others: read).

This method only executes on POSIX-compliant file systems (Linux, Unix, macOS). On Windows systems, the method does nothing and relies on Windows default file permissions, which are typically sufficient for most use cases.

This approach avoids UnsupportedOperationException on Windows while ensuring proper permission control on systems that require explicit permission setting. Windows files get reasonable default permissions automatically when created. @param file The file to set permissions on @param permissions A string representing the POSIX permissions (e.g., "rwxr-xr--")

question: How does TransportProvider.getClient() work?
answer:
Creates and returns a transport client implementation based on the provided configuration.

This factory method examines the configuration to determine which transport client implementation to instantiate. The transport protocol is specified in the configuration using the {@link EventBusConstants#TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL} key.

Currently supported transport client implementations:

  • {@link ZMQClient} - For ZeroMQ transport protocol

The method also checks for the {@link EventBusConstants#AUTO_RECONNECT} flag in the configuration. If set to true, the returned client will be wrapped in an {@link TransportReconnectClient} to provide automatic reconnection capabilities.

The configuration object should contain all necessary parameters for the specific transport implementation, such as:

  • Host address to connect to
  • Port number
  • Socket mode (SUB, PUSH, etc.)
  • Protocol-specific options (high water mark, etc.)
  • Auto-reconnect flag and parameters

Example configuration for ZMQ client with auto-reconnect:

{@code       JsonObject config = new JsonObject()           .put(TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL, TransportProtocol.ZMQ.getValue())           .put(AUTO_RECONNECT, true)           .put("host", "localhost")           .put("port", 5555)           .put("socket_mode", SocketMode.SUB);       }
@param config a JsonObject containing the transport client configuration @return a TransportClient implementation based on the specified protocol, optionally wrapped in an AutoReconnectClient if auto-reconnect is enabled @throws IllegalArgumentException if the specified protocol is not supported or if the configuration is invalid @see TransportClient @see ZMQClient @see TransportReconnectClient @see EventBusConstants.TransportProtocol

The class supports a wide range of UI actions including:

  • Configuration testing (credentials, connections, etc.)
  • Report generation and export
  • Notification management
  • File uploads and downloads

question: Show the pattern for: How does MotadataAppManager.initializeManager() work?
answer:
The MotadataAppManager class is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the Motadata application.

This class serves as the central control system for the Motadata application, handling operations such as:

  • Starting, stopping, and restarting application components
  • Managing application upgrades and patches
  • Handling backup and restore operations
  • Coordinating communication between distributed components
  • Managing HTTP servers and event bus handlers
  • Monitoring system health and status

The MotadataAppManager extends Vert.x's AbstractVerticle to leverage the event-driven, non-blocking programming model for handling concurrent operations efficiently. It interacts with various system components through the event bus and maintains the overall state of the application.

This class implements a robust error handling mechanism and ensures proper coordination between different components during critical operations like upgrades and restarts.

Architecture and Design

The MotadataAppManager follows a reactive, event-driven architecture:

  • Event Processing: The class processes events received through the Vert.x event bus, dispatching them to appropriate handler methods based on event type.
  • Asynchronous Operations: All operations are performed asynchronously using Vert.x's Future/Promise pattern to ensure non-blocking behavior.
  • Component Management: The class manages the lifecycle of child processes and components, ensuring they are started, stopped, and monitored appropriately.
  • HTTP Server: The class sets up and manages an HTTP server for handling web-based operations and API endpoints.

Event Handling

The MotadataAppManager handles various types of events:

  • Lifecycle Events: Start, stop, restart events for application components
  • State Change Events: Enable, disable events for components
  • Upgrade Events: Events for upgrading application components or the manager itself
  • Backup/Restore Events: Events for backing up and restoring system data
  • Heartbeat Events: Events for monitoring system health
  • Switchover Events: Events for high availability operations

File Operations

The class performs various file operations for backup, restore, and upgrade:

  • Copying and transferring files between directories
  • Extracting and processing ZIP archives
  • Reading and writing configuration files
  • Managing system files and directories

Process Management

The MotadataAppManager manages external processes:

  • Starting and stopping child processes
  • Monitoring process health and status
  • Handling process output and errors
  • Managing process IDs and registration

Error Handling

The class implements comprehensive error handling:

  • All operations return Futures that can be composed and chained
  • Exceptions are caught, logged, and propagated appropriately
  • Error messages are standardized and include error codes
  • Recovery mechanisms are implemented for critical operations

Usage

The MotadataAppManager is typically used by:

  • System bootstrap processes to initialize the application
  • Administrative interfaces to control application lifecycle
  • Monitoring systems to track application health
  • Upgrade and maintenance processes to perform system updates

This method sets up the manager by:

  • Initializing the event engine for event bus communication
  • Setting up event handlers for various system operations
  • Starting the HTTP server for web-based operations
  • Registering event consumers for different types of events

The method handles events related to application lifecycle management, including start, stop, restart, upgrade, backup, and restore operations. @param startPromise the promise to complete when initialization is done @throws Exception if an error occurs during initialization / @Override public void start(Promise startPromise) throws Exception { initializeManager(startPromise); } / Initializes the Motadata Application Manager with all necessary components and event handlers.

This method performs comprehensive initialization of the manager including:

  • Event Bus Setup: Configures reply topics for event responses
  • Database Backup Handler: Registers consumer for database backup events with support for:
    • CONFIG_DB and regular database backups with different timeout configurations
    • Remote storage protocols (non-LOCAL) using worker processes
    • Local storage with file and directory backup capabilities
    • Source file deletion after successful backup (optional)
  • Event Engine Configuration: Initializes the main event processing engine with:
    • Blocking event processing with queue size of 1
    • Comprehensive event routing for lifecycle, state change, HA, monitoring, and upgrade events
    • Bootstrap type-specific property injection (Agent, Collector, Processor, etc.)
    • Event result handling with success/failure logging and status updates
  • Child Process Management: Calculates and starts required child processes based on bootstrap type
  • High Availability Setup: Deploys HA Manager for secondary/passive installation modes

Event Types Handled:

  • Lifecycle: START, STOP, RESTART events for agents and remote processors
  • State Management: ENABLE, DISABLE events for agents
  • High Availability: SWITCH_OVER events
  • Monitoring: HEARTBEAT events
  • Maintenance: DELETE, UPGRADE, BACKUP, RESTORE events

Backup Operation Details:

  • CONFIG_DB backups: 10-minute timeout, custom source path support
  • Regular backups: 1-hour timeout, uses default datastore backup path
  • Remote storage: Utilizes Go-based worker processes for protocol handling
  • Local storage: Direct file/directory copying with optional source cleanup

Error Handling: All operations include comprehensive exception handling with proper error code assignment and message propagation through the event bus system. @param startPromise the promise to complete when initialization is finished successfully or fails @see EventEngine @see HAManager @see BackupProfile @see StorageProfile @since 1.0

question: How does DependencyQueryProcessor.buildVirtualizationDependencies() work?
answer:
Builds dependencies for virtualization and HCI objects.

This method processes dependencies for virtualization objects (vCenter, ESXi, Hyper-V, etc.) and Hyper-Converged Infrastructure (HCI) objects (Prism, Nutanix, etc.). It extracts virtualization dependencies and builds the appropriate dependency structure based on the requested dependency format.

For TOP_BOTTOM_HIERARCHY format, it builds a multi-level hierarchy:

  • Cluster -> Hypervisor -> VM -> Server (if VM is provisioned as a server)
  • Hypervisor -> VM -> Server (if VM is provisioned as a server)

For FLAT format, it adds direct connections between virtualization components to the connections array. @param asyncResult The result of the dependency query @param event The original dependency query event @param parent The parent object (for hierarchical format) or null (for flat format) @param connections The connections array to populate (for flat format) @param objects Array of objects already processed @param future Promise to complete when the dependency building is done @param pendingItems Map tracking pending items for completion handling
